definition_zh: n. 信徒；信教者；相信某事（或主张某事）的人
definition_en: a person who believes in a religion; a person who is convinced that something is true, right or worthwhile
core_image: 礼拜散场后，门口那位说「信了一辈子」的老人
scene: 礼拜结束后，门口的老人说他一辈子都信。 After the service an old man at the door said he had been a believer all his life.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：believer 指宗教上的信徒；句意是礼拜后门口的老人说他一辈子都是信者。

pos.zh: 信徒；信奉者

senses.title: A religious believer
senses.definition: a person who holds a religious faith
senses.definitionCN: 持有宗教信仰的人
senses.example: Believers of several faiths shared the same hall.
senses.exampleCN: 几种信仰的信徒共用同一个礼堂。
senses.why: The agent ending -er on believe first named people who held a faith, which remains its main use.
senses.whyCN: believe 上的施事后缀 -er 最初就指持守信仰的人，这仍是其主用法。

senses.title: Someone convinced of an idea
senses.definition: a person who is convinced that a practice, policy or idea is right or useful
senses.definitionCN: 确信某种做法、政策或想法正确或有益的人
senses.example: She is a believer in long walks and early nights.
senses.exampleCN: 她笃信长距离散步和早睡。
senses.why: Once religion is no longer required, the same word covers any conviction held with confidence.
senses.whyCN: 一旦不再限于宗教，同一个词就能覆盖任何坚定的确信。

intro.en: Believer is believe plus -er, and believe began with love: to hold something dear was to hold it true.
intro.cn: believer 是 believe 加 -er，而 believe 起初与「爱」有关：珍视某物，就是认为它为真。

items.en: The root leubh meant to love or to hold dear, the deep base of believe.
items.cn: 词根 leubh 意为爱、珍视，是 believe 的深层基础。

items.en: Old English geliefan means to hold something dear and therefore true.
items.cn: 古英语 geliefan 意为「珍视因而信以为真」。

items.en: The prefix be- joins the verb, giving belyfan, to believe.
items.cn: 前缀 be- 加入该动词，形成 belyfan「相信」。

items.en: Middle English believe settles the spelling and the sense of holding as true.
items.cn: 中古英语 believe 固定了拼写与「信以为真」之义。

items.en: The agent ending -er names the person who believes, first in religion.
items.cn: 施事后缀 -er 造出 believer，最初用于宗教。

items.en: The word widens to anyone who supports an idea, as a believer in reform.
items.cn: 词义扩指任何拥护某种主张的人，如 a believer in reform。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps believe and belief beside the longer -er words; the near-meaning group ranks followers from a formal adherent to a new convert.
note.cn: 形近组把 believe 与 belief 放在较长的 -er 词旁边；近义组把追随者从正式的拥护者排到新皈依者。

entries.definition: To accept something as true.
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事为真。

entries.definition: A feeling that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 相信某事为真的看法。

entries.definition: A person who takes over a duty.
entries.definitionCN: 接替职务的人。

entries.definition: A dog trained to fetch shot game.
entries.definitionCN: 经训练衔回猎物的犬。

entries.tag: one who holds to a cause
entries.definition: A supporter of a party or doctrine.
entries.definitionCN: 政党或学说的拥护者。

entries.definition: A pupil who follows a teacher teaching.
entries.definitionCN: 追随老师教诲的学生。

entries.definition: A person strongly devoted to something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事极为热忱的人。

entries.definition: A person who has adopted a new faith.
entries.definitionCN: 新近改信某种信仰的人。

normalIntro.en: Believer is believe plus the person ending -er. And believe began as to hold dear, which is why faith and love share a root.
normalIntro.cn: believer 是 believe 加表「人」的 -er。而 believe 本义是「珍视」，所以信仰与爱同根。

normal.en: Believe is the verb; believer is the person.
normal.cn: believe 是动词，believer 是那个人。

normal.en: Belief is the state; be careful not to swap them.
normal.cn: belief 是状态，注意别与 believer 混用。

normal.en: A believer in progress trusts that things improve.
normal.cn: a believer in progress 相信事情会变好。

normal.en: Believers is the plural, one l and two e.
normal.cn: 复数是 believers，一个 l 两个 e。

normal.en: To hold something dear is to hold it true.
normal.cn: 珍视某物，就是认为它为真。

abstract.en: A person who lets a claim live rent-free.
abstract.cn: 让某个说法免费住进脑子里的人。

abstract.en: Trust given before evidence arrives.
abstract.cn: 证据到来之前就先给出的信任。

abstract.en: Love wearing the clothes of certainty.
abstract.cn: 穿上「确定」外衣的爱。

examples.en: The chapel holds believers of three different faiths.
examples.cn: 这座礼拜堂容纳三种不同信仰的信徒。

examples.en: He is a believer in plain speaking.
examples.cn: 他笃信有话直说。

examples.en: Believers and sceptics filled the hall alike.
examples.cn: 信者与怀疑者同样挤满了大厅。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：believe「相信」+ -er「人」= believer 信徒。同族辨析：believe 动词、belief 信念、believer 人。记一条古义线索：believe 原义「珍视」，所以「信」里带着「爱」。

root: believe 出自古英语 belyfan「信奉」，由 be- 加 geliefan 构成，深层为原始印欧语 leubh「爱、珍视」——「珍视故以为真」。13 世纪加施事后缀 -er 造出 believer，最初专指宗教信徒，18 世纪扩指任何赞同某种主张的人。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses, one root act: to hold something true because you hold it dear, first in religion and then in any conviction.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项，同一个根本动作：因为珍视所以认定为真——先在宗教里，再扩到任何确信。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old man at the chapel door saying he has believed all his life
core.cn: 核心意象：礼拜堂门口的老人说他信了一辈子

branches.en: A daily walk kept without fail.

branches.en: A margin full of pencilled agreement.

branches.en: Trust that asks for no proof first.

latinIntro.en: Latin credere means to believe or entrust, fides means faith, and devotus means devoted; they give credit, fidelity and devotee.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 credere 意为相信、托付，fides 意为信义，devotus 意为虔诚；它们给出 credit、fidelity 与 devotee。

definition_zh: 任性；突发奇想；反复无常的念头
definition_en: a sudden, unpredictable change of mood or behavior; an impulsive whim
core_image: 一阵说转就转的旋风：天空晴着晴着忽然翻脸
scene: 画廊里，收藏家昨天还非这幅画不买，今天却看也不看。 Her purchase of the vineyard was pure caprice.
sceneCN: 这里 caprice 是「一时兴起」（第 1 个义项：无端起意、不讲理由的突发念头）；句意是她买下那座葡萄园纯属一时兴起。

pos.zh: 任性；突发奇想
反复无常；（命运、天气的）变幻莫测

derivatives.zh: 由 caprice 加形容词后缀构成，义为「反复无常的；任性的」
同根音乐术语，义为「随想地；自由奔放地」（意大利语）

senses.title: A sudden unaccountable change of mind
senses.definition: an impulsive wish or change of intention without apparent reason
senses.definitionCN: 没有明显缘由的冲动愿望或主意突变
senses.example: She dyed her hair silver on a caprice.
senses.exampleCN: 她一时兴起把头发染成了银色。
senses.why: The older image is the goat's sudden leap: the mind jumps without warning.
senses.whyCN: 较早的意象是山羊的突然跃起：心思毫无征兆地一跳。

senses.title: Unpredictable changeability of things
senses.definition: the quality of being governed by chance or unpredictable swings, as weather or fortune
senses.definitionCN: 受偶然支配或摇摆不定的性质，如天气或运气
senses.example: Sailors know the caprice of the southern ocean.
senses.exampleCN: 水手们深知南大洋的变幻无常。
senses.why: What people do by caprice, nature seems to do by caprice too.
senses.whyCN: 人会任性无常，大自然看起来也是如此。

senses.title: A whimsical musical or artistic piece
senses.definition: a lively, free-form instrumental piece following the player's fancy, as a caprice
senses.definitionCN: 随演奏者兴致而作的活泼自由器乐曲，即随想曲
senses.example: Paganini's caprices for solo violin remain legendary.
senses.exampleCN: 帕格尼尼的小提琴随想曲至今仍是传奇。
senses.why: Music that leaps where it pleases borrows the goat's leap as its form.
senses.whyCN: 随心所欲跳跃的音乐借用了山羊一跃而起的形态。

intro.en: Caprice entered European languages through Italian capriccio, probably from capro, he-goat, suggesting the goat's sudden start; the precise path is debated.
intro.cn: caprice 经意大利语 capriccio 进入欧洲各语言，一般认为出自 capro（公山羊），暗指山羊的突然起跳；具体路径尚有争议。

items.en: The root *kapro- is associated with the he-goat, seen in Latin caper and capra.
items.cn: 词根 *kapro- 与公山羊相关，见于拉丁语 caper、capra。

items.en: Latin caper meant he-goat; capra meant she-goat, source of Capricorn.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caper 意为公山羊；capra 意为母山羊，Capricorn（摩羯座）即出于此。

items.en: Italian capriccio meant a sudden start like a goat's shudder, then a whim, then a free-form piece of music.
items.cn: 意大利语 capriccio 先指如山羊惊跳般的突发举动，继而指一时怪念，再指自由曲式的乐曲。

items.en: French caprice carried it into English in the seventeenth century with the whim and changeability senses.
items.cn: 十七世纪法语 caprice 携「怪念」与「无常」二义进入英语。

items.en: Today it labels impulsive choices, fickle weather and fortune, and Paganini's showpieces.
items.cn: 如今它形容一时兴起的决定、善变的天气与命运，以及帕格尼尼式的炫技曲。

note.en: Caprice stands with its goat relatives and a row of temperament words.
note.cn: caprice 与山羊词族的亲戚以及一排性格词汇站在一起。

entries.definition: Playful, quaint oddity of ideas, lighter than caprice.

entries.definition: Steadfast reliability and sameness of purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定可靠、始终如一，是 caprice 的反义对照。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the goat story and the weather-turning image.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕「山羊」典故与「天色骤变」画面的记忆钩子。

normal.en: Goat story: Italian capro, he-goat, gives the sudden leap behind caprice.
normal.cn: 山羊典故：意大利语 capro（公山羊）给出 caprice 背后那记突然起跳。

normal.en: Zodiac link: Capricorn the goat and caprice the goat-leap share caper, capra.
normal.cn: 星座关联：摩羯座的羊与 caprice 的羊同出 caper、capra。

normal.en: Music hook: Paganini wrote twenty-four Caprices; the noun names the piece too.
normal.cn: 音乐钩子：帕格尼尼写了二十四首随想曲；这个名词也指这种曲子。

normal.en: Adjective twin: capricious is the standard SAT partner of caprice.
normal.cn: 形容词孪生：capricious 是 caprice 在 SAT 里的标准搭档。

normal.en: Phrase frame: the caprice of fate is the literary way to blame luck.
normal.cn: 短语框架：the caprice of fate 是文学里归咎运气的说法。

abstract.en: A goat on a hillside turning mid-bite, bolting toward the ridge for no visible reason.
abstract.cn: 山坡上一只山羊正吃着草，忽然扭头向山脊狂奔，看不出任何理由。

abstract.en: Blue sky at breakfast, black clouds by noon, sun again by three.

abstract.en: A violin leaping across the strings wherever it pleases.
abstract.cn: 一把小提琴随心所欲地在弦上跳跃。

examples.en: The committee's verdict seemed governed by caprice rather than rules.
examples.cn: 委员会的裁决似乎凭一时好恶，而非依规而行。

examples.en: At the market she bought a parrot on a caprice.
examples.cn: 在集市上，她一时兴起买了一只鹦鹉。

examples.en: Vines suffer under the caprice of spring frosts.
examples.cn: 葡萄园饱受春季霜冻无常之苦。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克普瑞斯」——可（克）惜计划（普）锐（瑞）意取消（斯），说变就变，正是任性反复；联想山羊想吃就吃、想跳就跳，全凭心血来潮。

root: 一般认为经意大利语 capriccio（山羊的惊跳；怪念）进入欧洲语言，词基为拉丁语 caper / capra（公山羊／母山羊），可上溯至与山羊相关的词根 *kapro-。十七世纪经法语 caprice 进入英语，义为「一时怪念」「反复无常」，后亦指自由曲式的随想曲。同根词有 capricious、Capricorn；词源路径在细节上仍有争议。

sensesIntro.en: From the goat's sudden leap the word covers impulsive choices, fickle fortune, and free-form music.
sensesIntro.cn: 从山羊的突然一跳出发，词义涵盖冲动之举、无常的命运与自由曲式的音乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a goat leaping sideways for no reason anyone can see.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只旁若无由、横跳而起的山羊。

branches.en: THE DECISION: choices made on no ground but mood.
branches.cn: 决定：全凭情绪、毫无根据的选择。

branches.en: THE SKY: weather and fortune as moody masters.
branches.cn: 天空：把天气与命运看作善变的主宰。

branches.en: THE STAGE: music that obeys only the player's fancy.
branches.cn: 舞台：只听命于演奏者兴致的乐曲。

branches.en: THE BLAME: caprice as the name for what cannot be predicted or held to account.
branches.cn: 归咎：凡无法预测、无法追责者，皆名之曰 caprice。

branches.en: THE CHARM: the same word allowed to mean delightful spontaneity.
branches.cn: 魅力：同一个词也可以指讨喜的随性。

intro.en: Caprice is a borrowed noun without English affixes; its derivational life sits in the goat family and the Italian musical form.
intro.cn: caprice 是整体借入的名词，不带英语固有词缀；其派生活动在山羊词族与意大利音乐体裁之中。

definition_zh: 泛化的；普遍化的；概括性的；（疾病）全身性的
definition_en: widened from particular cases into a broad rule, or spread through the whole of something rather than staying in one part
core_image: 一张网格纸上零散的小黑点被一支笔连成一大片灰面
scene: 这里指「泛化的」。 A conclusion generalized from a single village cannot describe the whole country.
sceneCN: 这里 generalized 是「外推成通则的」（第 1 个义项：由个别案例推及一般）；句意：仅从一个村庄外推得出的结论无法描述整个国家。图中可辨识物件：网格纸、灰色填涂面、放大镜、铅笔、指示箭头。

pos.zh: 泛化的；普遍化的；概括性的；（疾病）全身性的（多作定语，也可作表语）

collocations.zh: 泛化的结论；笼统的结论

senses.title: Drawn out into a rule
senses.titleCN: 扩为通则：从个别情形推出一条规律
senses.definition: taken from particular instances and stated as a rule that covers many of them
senses.definitionCN: 从具体事例中提取出来，并表述为可覆盖众多同类情形的规律
senses.example: The claim was generalized from three experiments in one laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 这一主张是从同一个实验室的三次实验中推出来的。
senses.why: general comes from Latin generalis 'belonging to a whole kind', and -ize means 'to make'; -ed turns the verb into an adjective, so generalized literally means 'made kind-wide'.
senses.whyCN: general 出自拉丁 generalis“属于整个类别的”，-ize 意为“使成为”，-ed 把动词转为形容词，因此 generalized 字面就是“被做成整类通用的”。

senses.title: Applying to a whole class
senses.titleCN: 适用于整类：不限于某个特例
senses.definition: valid for a whole group or category rather than for one member of it
senses.definitionCN: 对整个群体或类别有效，而非只对其中某一个成员有效
senses.example: A generalized rule for all metals must also fit mercury.
senses.exampleCN: 一条适用于所有金属的通则也必须适用于汞。
senses.why: Once a statement is made general, its scope is the whole kind; the adjective marks that breadth of application.
senses.whyCN: 一旦陈述被“一般化”，其覆盖范围就是整个类别；这个形容词标记的正是这种适用面的宽度。

senses.title: Stated without detail
senses.titleCN: 只给大意的：略去细节的概括说法
senses.definition: expressed in broad terms, with the specific details left out
senses.definitionCN: 以宽泛的措辞表达，具体细节被略去
senses.example: He gave a generalized account of the meeting and named no one.
senses.exampleCN: 他对会议只作了笼统叙述，没有点任何人的名字。
senses.why: To generalize is also to strip away particulars; the participle then describes speech or writing that has lost its specifics.
senses.whyCN: generalize 同时意味着剥离特殊性；分词形式于是描述那种丢掉了具体细节的言辞或文字。

senses.title: Affecting the whole body
senses.titleCN: 全身性的：医学上波及全身而非局部
senses.definition: in medicine, of a condition that spreads through the whole body instead of one organ or area
senses.definitionCN: 医学上指疾病波及全身，而不是局限于某个器官或部位
senses.example: A generalized seizure involves the whole brain rather than one region.
senses.exampleCN: 全身性癫痫发作涉及整个大脑，而不是某一个区域。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the 'whole rather than part' sense: a condition that is not localized has been generalized across the body.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了“整体而非局部”这一层意思：没有局限化的病症，就等于扩散到了全身。

senses.title: Statistical: broadly framed
senses.titleCN: 统计上的广义模型：不绑定某一具体情形
senses.definition: in statistics, describing a model or method built to cover a wide family of cases rather than one fixed form
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中指为覆盖一大类情形而构建、而非固定于单一形式的模型或方法
senses.example: The generalized linear model extends ordinary regression to counts and proportions.
senses.exampleCN: 广义线性模型把普通回归扩展到计数与比例数据。
senses.why: Statistics generalizes the textbook model by loosening one assumption, so the label 'generalized' marks the wider family that results.
senses.whyCN: 统计学通过放宽某一假设来“推广”教科书模型，因此“广义的”这个标签标记的是由此产生的更大模型族。

senses.title: Vague and imprecise
senses.titleCN: 笼统的：不够精确，含批评意味
senses.definition: used critically of a statement that is so broad that it says very little
senses.definitionCN: 带批评意味地形容某说法宽泛到几乎没说出什么内容
senses.example: The report's recommendations are too generalized to guide any decision.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告的建议过于笼统，无法指导任何决策。
senses.why: Breadth can become emptiness: when a claim covers everything, it distinguishes nothing, and the same adjective turns into a reproach.
senses.whyCN: 宽度可以变成空洞：当一个论断覆盖一切时，它就区分不出任何东西，同一个形容词便转为贬义。

senses.title: Pushed beyond its origin
senses.titleCN: 外推过度的：越过原本成立的范围
senses.definition: extended to situations beyond the ones in which it was actually established
senses.definitionCN: 被扩展到其实际成立情形之外的场合
senses.example: Results generalized from mice to humans often fail to hold.
senses.exampleCN: 从小鼠外推到人类的结果往往并不成立。
senses.why: The -ed form can also record a completed act of transfer, so it names findings that have been carried past the boundary where they were tested.
senses.whyCN: -ed 形式也可记录一次已完成的迁移动作，因此它指那些被搬过受检验边界之外的发现。

senses.title: Simplified into a pattern
senses.titleCN: 概化成图的：把细节简化为整体图案
senses.definition: in mapping and design, reduced to a simplified overall pattern by dropping small details
senses.definitionCN: 在地图绘制与设计中，通过删去细小细节而简化为整体图案
senses.example: A generalized coastline keeps the main bays and drops every inlet.
senses.exampleCN: 概化后的海岸线保留主要海湾，省略所有小湾。
senses.why: Cartographers call the deliberate thinning of detail generalization; the participle describes a surface that has been treated that way.
senses.whyCN: 制图学把有意删减细节称为 generalization（概化）；这个分词描述的就是经过此种处理的表面。

intro.en: Generalized is an English formation: the adjective general, borrowed from Latin generalis, plus the verb suffix -ize and the past-participle ending -ed. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: generalized 是英语内部构成的词：形容词 general 借自拉丁 generalis，再加动词后缀 -ize 与过去分词词尾 -ed。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin generalis meant 'belonging to a whole kind or class'. It was built on genus 'kind, stock, family', whose deeper root is generally taken to be a Indo-European form meaning 'to beget'. That deeper link is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 拉丁 generalis 意为“属于整个类别的”，由 genus“种类、族、家系”构成。其更深词根一般被认为是某个意为“生育、产生”的印欧形式，但这属于重构。

items.en: Generalis passed through Old French as general and entered English in the 13th century as an adjective meaning 'of a whole class'. The first records are legal and religious.
items.cn: generalis 经古法语 general 进入英语，13 世纪时作形容词，意为“整类的”。最早记录见于法律与宗教文本。

items.en: The ending -ize comes from Late Latin -izare, itself from Greek -izein, a productive verb-forming suffix. English generalize appears in the 18th century with the sense 'to reduce to a general form'.
items.cn: 后缀 -ize 来自晚期拉丁 -izare，后者又出自希腊 -izein，是能产的动词构词后缀。英语 generalize 于 18 世纪出现，意为“化为一般形式”。

items.en: Adding -ed produced the adjective generalized, first used for statements and later for conditions spread through a whole body or system.
items.cn: 加上 -ed 构成形容词 generalized，最初用于陈述，后用于波及整个身体或系统的状态。

items.en: The 20th century added specific technical senses: generalized anxiety in psychiatry, generalized seizure in neurology, generalized linear model in statistics, and generalization in cartography.
items.cn: 20 世纪增加了专门技术义项：精神病学中的广泛性焦虑、神经学中的全身性发作、统计学中的广义线性模型，以及制图学中的概化。

items.en: The exact date of the first English use of generalize is uncertain, and the Indo-European root behind Latin genus is a reconstructed form rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: generalize 在英语中首次使用的确切年代存疑；拉丁 genus 背后的印欧词根是重构形式，并非有记录的实际词。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same family that are easily swapped; the second holds near-synonyms that stress breadth or vagueness.
note.cn: 第一组是同族易混词；第二组是强调宽泛或含糊的近义词。

entries.definition: Meaning 'affecting all or most', but attaching to the whole rather than marking a completed act of broadening. A general rule is simply a rule for all; a generalized rule has been made to cover all.
entries.definitionCN: 意为“涉及全体或大多数的”，但它直接修饰整体，不标记一次已完成的推广动作。general rule 是本身就适用于全体的规则；generalized rule 是被推及全体的规则。

entries.definition: The verb meaning 'to draw a general rule'. It names the act, while generalized describes the result of that act.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为“归纳出通则”，指动作本身；generalized 描述该动作的结果。

entries.definition: A noun for the quality of being broad, or for a vague statement. It cannot replace the adjective before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指宽泛性，也指笼统的说法；不能像形容词那样放在名词前。

entries.definition: Also from Latin genus, but it means 'characteristic of a whole class' or 'unbranded'. It never implies that someone drew a conclusion from samples.
entries.definitionCN: 同出拉丁 genus，但意为“整类共有的”或“无商标的”，不含“由样本归纳而来”之意。

entries.definition: Applying to every case whatsoever; stronger than generalized, which only claims broad coverage.
entries.definitionCN: 适用于无一例外的所有情形；比 generalized 更强，后者只声称覆盖广泛。

entries.definition: Wide in scope and often too broad to be accurate; it carries the same critical edge as sense 6 but more force.
entries.definitionCN: 范围宽大且常宽到不准确；与第 6 个义项同样带批评意味，但语气更强。

entries.definition: Covering a large range; a neutral word for width that does not say whether the width was earned.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖范围大；是中性的“宽”，不说明这种宽是否站得住。

entries.definition: Not clearly expressed or defined; it targets unclear boundaries rather than wide coverage.
entries.definitionCN: 表达或界定不清；它针对的是边界模糊，而不是覆盖范围大。

entries.definition: Present or occurring over a large area; it spreads across space, not across categories of cases.
entries.definitionCN: 在大片区域内存在或发生；它是在空间上铺开，而不是在事例类别上推广。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: general + -ize 'make' + -ed: something has been made general.
normal.cn: general + -ize“使成为”+ -ed：某事物被做成了通用的。

normal.en: The base genus means 'kind', so generalized keeps the image of one member standing for the whole kind.
normal.cn: 词基 genus 意为“种类”，所以 generalized 保留了“一个成员代表整个类别”的意象。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the range: generalized anxiety, generalized seizure, generalized linear model, generalized statement.
normal.cn: 固定搭配展示了义项范围：广泛性焦虑、全身性发作、广义线性模型、概括性陈述。

normal.en: The family runs generalize, generalization, general, generally, generality and generic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 generalize、generalization、general、generally、generality、generic。

normal.en: generic looks like a synonym but means 'class-wide or unbranded', not 'inferred from cases'.
normal.cn: generic 看似同义，实际意为“整类共有的或无商标的”，不是“由个案归纳来的”。

abstract.en: Picture a single footprint being copied until it covers a whole field of snow.
abstract.cn: 想象一个脚印被复制，直到覆满整片雪地。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow funnel opening into a wide mouth: many small cases pour in and one broad rule comes out.
abstract.cn: 想象一个窄漏斗通向宽口：许多小案例灌进去，一条宽规则流出来。

abstract.en: Picture a painter filling every separate cell with the same grey until the grid reads as one surface.
abstract.cn: 想象画者把每个小格都填成同一种灰，直到整张网格看起来只有一整片。

examples.en: The authors admitted that their model was generalized from data collected in one climate zone.
examples.cn: 作者承认，他们的模型是从一个气候带收集的数据外推而来的。

examples.en: A generalized anxiety disorder is not tied to any single situation.
examples.cn: 广泛性焦虑障碍并不与任何单一情境绑定。

examples.en: Generalized maps sacrifice small inlets in order to show the shape of the coast.
examples.cn: 概化地图牺牲小海湾，以显示海岸的整体形状。

dict_mnemonic.text: “将军（general）下令，一概而论”——由个别推到全体 → generalized 泛化的、全身性的

root: 拉丁 generalis“属于整类的”← genus“种类、族”；英语 general + -ize（使成为）+ -ed（形容词化）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a single case is stretched until it stands for the whole class, and that stretch can be useful, vague, or risky.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着一个动作展开：单个案例被拉宽到代表整类，而这一拉宽可以有用、可以空洞，也可以有风险。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scattered dots fused by one stroke into a single broad grey area.
core.cn: 核心意象：零散的点被一笔连成一整片宽大的灰色。

branches.en: RULE-MAKING: a conclusion drawn from single cases and given the scope of a whole class.
branches.cn: 立规则：由单个案例得出的结论被赋予整类的适用范围。

branches.en: LOSING DETAIL: the same widening thins specifics until the statement becomes empty.
branches.cn: 失去细节：同一过程把具体信息稀释，直到陈述变得空洞。

branches.en: WHOLE BODY: medicine applies 'not localized' quite literally to disease.
branches.cn: 全身：医学把“非局部”直接用于疾病。

branches.en: WIDE MODEL: statistics broadens a fixed model into a family by relaxing one assumption.
branches.cn: 宽模型：统计学放宽一个假设，把固定模型扩展成模型族。

branches.en: TWO DIRECTIONS: one goes too far beyond the evidence, the other deliberately simplifies a surface into a pattern.
branches.cn: 两个方向：一个是越出证据之外走得太远，另一个是有意把表面简化为图案。

intro.en: Generalized is a transparent English build: a Latin-borrowed adjective, a Greek-derived verb suffix, and an Old English participial ending.
intro.cn: generalized 的构造清晰可拆：一个借自拉丁的形容词、一个源自希腊的动词后缀、一个古英语分词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The root genus 'kind' supplies a large family: general, generate, generation, genus, generic, generous and genius all trace back to the same 'begetting, kind' source, though each entered English by its own path.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 genus“种类”衍生出庞大的词族：general、generate、generation、genus、generic、generous、genius 都可追溯到同一个“生育、种类”的来源，但各自经不同路径进入英语。

items.meaning: made broad or spread through the whole
items.example: A generalized rule must still be tested case by case.
items.exampleCN: 泛化的规则仍必须逐例检验。

items.meaning: to draw a broad rule from particulars
items.example: It is risky to generalize from one season of data.
items.exampleCN: 仅凭一季数据就作概括是有风险的。

items.meaning: the act of broadening, or the broad statement produced
items.meaningCN: 概括行为；由此得出的概括性说法
items.example: The paper offers a cautious generalization about urban growth.
items.exampleCN: 这篇论文对城市增长提出了谨慎的概括。

items.meaning: affecting all or most; not detailed
items.example: The general pattern holds across all four regions.
items.exampleCN: 总格局在四个地区都成立。

items.meaning: in most cases; as a broad statement
items.example: Generally, warmer seas hold less dissolved oxygen.
items.exampleCN: 一般来说，较暖的海水溶解氧更少。

items.meaning: the quality of being broad; a vague statement
items.example: The argument loses force at that level of generality.
items.exampleCN: 在那种笼统程度上，这个论证失去了力度。

items.meaning: shared by a whole class; without a brand name
items.example: The generic form of the drug costs a third as much.
items.exampleCN: 该药物的非专利剂型价格只有三分之一。

items.example: The species belongs to a genus found only in Antarctica.
items.exampleCN: 该物种属于一个仅见于南极洲的属。

latinEntries.meaning: belonging to a whole kind or class
verb-forming suffix meaning 'to make or do'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 动词后缀，意为“使之成为、做”

definition_zh: 天体；地球大气层之外的自然物体（恒星、行星、卫星、小行星、彗星等）
definition_en: a natural object in space beyond the earth's atmosphere, such as a star, planet, moon, asteroid or comet
core_image: 黑绒布上散布着大小不一的发光小球，每颗都沿一条看不见的弧线缓慢移动
scene: 天文台圆顶缓缓打开，观测者把镜筒对准海王星轨道外一个模糊的光点。 The telescope tracked a faint celestial body beyond the orbit of Neptune.
sceneCN: 这里 celestial body 指「地球大气层之外的自然物体」（第 1 个义项：天体总称）；句意为望远镜追踪到海王星轨道之外一个微弱的天体。图中可辨识物件：望远镜、轨道弧线、模糊光点、星图。

pos.zh: 天体（可数名词；复数 celestial bodies）

derivatives.zh: 身体的；肉体的（同出 body 词根）

senses.title: A natural object in space
senses.definition: any naturally formed object beyond the earth's atmosphere, considered as a single unit
senses.definitionCN: 地球大气层之外自然形成的、被当作一个整体看待的物体
senses.example: Every celestial body follows a path fixed by gravity.
senses.exampleCN: 每一个天体都沿着由引力固定的路径运行。
senses.why: the phrase is the plain cover term: celestial marks its place in the sky, body marks it as one object.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法是最朴素的统称：celestial 标明它在天上，body 标明它是一个单独物体。

senses.title: A star
senses.definition: a celestial body that produces its own light by nuclear fusion
senses.definitionCN: 靠核聚变自行发光的天体
senses.example: A star is a celestial body that shines by its own fusion.
senses.exampleCN: 恒星是靠自身聚变发光的天体。
senses.why: stars were the first celestial bodies to be sorted out, because they shine without help.
senses.whyCN: 恒星是最早被区分出来的一类天体，因为它们无需外物就能发光。

senses.title: A planet
senses.definition: a celestial body that orbits a star, is massive enough to be round, and has cleared its neighbourhood
senses.definitionCN: 绕恒星运行、质量足以呈球形并已清空其轨道附近的天体
senses.example: A planet is a celestial body that orbits a star and has cleared its neighbourhood.
senses.exampleCN: 行星是绕恒星运行并已清空轨道附近的天体。
senses.why: the modern definition turns the old word into a test that a body either passes or fails.
senses.whyCN: 现代定义把这个旧词变成一项检验，天体要么通过，要么不通过。

senses.title: A natural satellite
senses.definition: a celestial body that orbits a planet or a smaller body
senses.definitionCN: 绕行星或更小天体运行的天体
senses.example: The moon is the only natural celestial body that people have visited.
senses.exampleCN: 月球是人类唯一造访过的天然天体。
senses.why: moons were once counted as planets; once they were seen to circle planets, they became satellites among celestial bodies.
senses.whyCN: 卫星一度被算作行星；当人们看出它们绕着行星转，它们就成了天体中的卫星。

senses.title: A minor body
senses.titleCN: 小天体（小行星与彗星等）
senses.definition: a small celestial body such as an asteroid, comet or meteoroid, left over from the formation of a planetary system
senses.definitionCN: 小行星、彗星、流星体等小天体，为行星系形成时的残留物
senses.example: Comets and asteroids are small celestial bodies left over from the early solar system.
senses.exampleCN: 彗星与小行星是早期太阳系遗留下来的小天体。
senses.why: the phrase covers leftovers too small to be round, so it keeps a place for rubble as well as for worlds.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法也涵盖小到无法呈球形的残渣，因此既给世界留位置，也给碎石留位置。

senses.title: A dwarf planet
senses.definition: a round celestial body that orbits a star but has not cleared its neighbourhood
senses.definitionCN: 绕恒星运行、呈球形但未清空轨道附近的天体
senses.example: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet, a small celestial body in its own class.
senses.exampleCN: 冥王星被重新归类为矮行星，自成一类小天体。
senses.why: the dwarf class was created when the planet test was tightened, and the wider phrase absorbed the losers.
senses.whyCN: 当行星的检验标准收紧时，矮行星这一类别被造出来，而更宽泛的天体说法收留了落选者。

senses.title: An exoplanet
senses.definition: a celestial body detected in orbit around another star
senses.definitionCN: 在另一颗恒星周围轨道上被探测到的天体
senses.example: An exoplanet is a celestial body detected around another star.
senses.exampleCN: 系外行星是在另一颗恒星周围探测到的天体。
senses.why: once instruments could see the wobble of distant suns, the phrase extended beyond our own system.
senses.whyCN: 当仪器能看见遥远恒星摆动时，这个说法就超出了我们的行星系。

senses.title: An artificial object
senses.definition: a human-made object in orbit, sometimes listed as an artificial celestial body although many catalogues exclude it
senses.definitionCN: 在轨道上运行的人造物体，有时被列为「人造天体」，但许多编目并不把它算入
senses.example: A spacecraft is sometimes listed as an artificial celestial body, though many catalogues exclude it.
senses.exampleCN: 航天器有时被列为「人造天体」，但许多编目将其排除。
senses.why: the extension is a boundary case: the phrase grew in astronomy, and engineers borrowed it for objects they had launched.
senses.whyCN: 这一延伸属于边界情形：这个说法生长于天文学，工程师又借它来指自己发射的物体。

intro.en: The phrase joins Latin caelestis 'heavenly' with English body, a word of Old English origin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这一短语把拉丁 caelestis「天上的」与英语本族词 body 组合在一起。年代均为约数。

items.en: Caelestis 'of the sky, heavenly' comes from caelum 'sky, heaven'; its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: caelestis「天空的、天上的」来自 caelum「天空、天」；其更深来源未得到证明。

items.en: Body goes back to Old English bodig 'trunk, chest', the physical frame of a person or animal. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and a suggested link to Old High German botah is only a hypothesis.
items.cn: body 可追溯到古英语 bodig「躯干、胸部」，指人或动物的身体骨架。其更深来源不确定，把它与古高地德语 botah 相联系只是假说。

items.en: English combines the adjective with body to name a distinct physical object; in astronomical writing the phrase is fixed by the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 英语把这个形容词与 body 组合起来，指一个独立可辨的物体；在天文写作中，这一短语在十八世纪固定下来。

items.en: Telescopes and orbital calculations made the phrase the ordinary cover term for stars, planets, moons and smaller objects.
items.cn: 望远镜与轨道计算使这一短语成为恒星、行星、卫星及更小物体的常用统称。

items.en: Spacecraft are sometimes called artificial celestial bodies, though many reference works restrict the phrase to natural objects.
items.cn: 航天器有时被称为「人造天体」，但许多工具书仍把这个说法限于自然物体。

items.en: First English date approximate: no exact first use of the compound is recorded, and it becomes common in astronomical writing only in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.
items.cn: 首见年代为约数：这一复合说法的确切首见英语书证未被记录，直到十八、十九世纪它才在天文写作中常见起来。

note.en: Group one holds neighbouring phrases that share the word celestial but name a model, a discipline or an instrument; group two holds true alternatives for an object in space.
note.cn: 第一组是同样带 celestial 的相邻说法，但分别指模型、学科或仪器；第二组才是太空中物体的真正近义说法。

entries.definition: An imaginary sphere on which the stars are projected for calculation; it is a coordinate surface, not a physical body.
entries.definitionCN: 为计算而把星星投影其上的假想球面；它是坐标面，不是实体。

entries.definition: The mathematical study of orbital motion; the phrase names a discipline, not a thing in space.
entries.definitionCN: 研究轨道运动的数学分支；这个说法指的是一门学科，而非太空中的东西。

entries.definition: A globe marked with constellations and star positions, used for teaching and navigation.
entries.definitionCN: 标有星座与恒星位置的地球仪式仪器，用于教学与导航。

entries.definition: Fragments of rockets and satellites in orbit; unlike a celestial body, it is not a natural object.
entries.definitionCN: 轨道上的火箭与卫星碎片；与天体不同，它不是自然形成的物体。

entries.definition: The standard technical term for a naturally occurring object in space; it overlaps almost completely with celestial body.
entries.definitionCN: 指太空中自然形成的物体的标准技术术语，与 celestial body 几乎完全重合。

entries.definition: The older everyday phrasing, common in religious and popular writing before the technical term spread.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的日常说法，在技术术语普及之前常见于宗教与通俗文字。

entries.definition: A body that orbits a star and has cleared its neighbourhood; it is a hyponym, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 绕恒星运行并已清空轨道附近的天体；它是下位词，而非同义词。

entries.definition: A body that shines by fusion; calling every celestial body a star is the commonest overgeneralisation.
entries.definitionCN: 靠聚变发光的天体；把一切天体都叫作恒星是最常见的过度概括。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin caelestis 'heavenly' plus English body 'one physical object'.
normal.cn: 拉丁 caelestis「天上的」加英语 body「一个物体」。

normal.en: The plural is irregular in the second word: celestial bodies, not celestial bodys.
normal.cn: 复数变化在第二个词上：celestial bodies，而不是 celestial bodys。

normal.en: The phrase covers stars, planets, moons, asteroids, comets, dwarf planets and exoplanets.
normal.cn: 这个说法涵盖恒星、行星、卫星、小行星、彗星、矮行星与系外行星。

normal.en: Synonyms split by register: heavenly body is older and popular, astronomical object is technical.
normal.cn: 近义词按语体分开：heavenly body 较旧且通俗，astronomical object 偏技术。

normal.en: The boundary case is the spacecraft, sometimes called an artificial celestial body.
normal.cn: 边界情形是航天器，有时被称为「人造天体」。

abstract.en: Picture marbles of different sizes rolling on a dark cloth, each on its own invisible arc.
abstract.cn: 想象大小不一的弹珠在深色布上滚动，各自沿一条看不见的弧线。

abstract.en: Picture a bonfire seen from a hill: one point of light that makes its own glow.
abstract.cn: 想象从山丘上看见一堆篝火：一个自己发光的点。

abstract.en: Picture a stone that has circled the same lamp for billions of years.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头绕着同一盏灯转了几十亿年。

examples.en: The catalogue lists every known celestial body in the survey area.
examples.cn: 该星表列出了巡天区域内所有已知天体。

examples.en: Gravity holds every celestial body in its orbit.
examples.cn: 引力把每一个天体都约束在轨道上。

examples.en: A new celestial body was announced after three nights of observation.
examples.cn: 经过三夜观测，一个新的天体被公布。

dict_mnemonic.text: 天体就是「天上的一整个物体」：不管它是恒星、行星还是碎石，只要在天空里自成一个整体，就叫天体

root: 拉丁 caelestis「天上的」+ 英语 body「物体」；caelestis 出自 caelum「天空」，body 出自古英语 bodig「躯干」，两者更深来源均不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses sort the same phrase by what the object is: the general cover term, then a star, a planet, a moon, a leftover rock, a dwarf planet, a world around another sun, and finally a human-made boundary case.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按「这个物体是什么」把同一个说法分类：先是总称，再是恒星、行星、卫星、残余碎石、矮行星、绕另一颗太阳的世界，最后是人造的边界情形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one distinct object hanging in the dark, held on a path by gravity.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个独立物体悬在黑暗中，被引力牵在一条路径上。

branches.en: THE COVER TERM: first of all the phrase simply names one natural object out in space.
branches.cn: 统称：这个说法首先只指太空中一个自然物体。

branches.en: OWN LIGHT: a star is the case where the object makes its own glow.
branches.cn: 自发光：恒星是物体自己发光的那个情形。

branches.en: ORBIT AND CLEARANCE: a planet adds both a stellar orbit and a swept path.
branches.cn: 绕行与清空：行星同时要求绕恒星运行与清空轨道。

branches.en: SMALLER CLASSES: moons circle planets, rubble never became round, and dwarf planets fail the clearance test.
branches.cn: 更小的类别：卫星绕行星，碎石从未成球，矮行星未通过清空检验。

branches.en: BEYOND THE OLD FRAME: the phrase stretches to worlds around other suns and, at the edge, to objects people built.
branches.cn: 超出旧框架：这个说法延伸到绕其他恒星的世界，并在边缘延伸到人造物体。

intro.en: The phrase is built from a Latin adjective and an English noun, so its two halves belong to two different layers of the language.
intro.cn: 这个短语由一个拉丁形容词和一个英语名词构成，两半分别属于语言的两个不同层次。

latinIntro.en: Latin caelum and caelestis supply the first half, while body and its relatives come from Old English; the astronomical compounds are built on the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 前半由拉丁 caelum 与 caelestis 提供，body 及其同族词来自古英语；天文复合词则都建立在英语名词 body 上。

items.meaning: of the sky or of heaven
items.example: A celestial map hung beside the telescope.
items.exampleCN: 望远镜旁挂着一张星空图。

items.meaning: a physical object; the frame of a person or animal
items.example: Every body in the simulation has mass.
items.exampleCN: 模拟中的每个物体都有质量。

items.example: The telescope tracked a faint celestial body.
items.exampleCN: 望远镜追踪到一个微弱的天体。

items.example: Older books speak of the heavenly bodies.
items.exampleCN: 较早的书里说「天上的物体」。

items.example: Stars are projected onto the celestial sphere.
items.exampleCN: 恒星被投影到天球上。

items.example: Celestial mechanics predicts the eclipse to the minute.
items.exampleCN: 天体力学把食的时刻预测到分钟。

items.example: Bodily motion differs from orbital motion.
items.exampleCN: 身体运动与轨道运动不同。

items.example: A coordinate point is bodiless by design.
items.exampleCN: 坐标点在设计上就是无形的。

definition_zh: 生物地球化学的（把生物、地质与化学过程放在一起考察的，尤其用于元素在圈层间的循环）
definition_en: relating to the combined biological, geological and chemical processes by which elements move through the earth system
core_image: 一块岩石被细菌啃出细缝，根须钻进缝里吸走金属，雨水再把残余冲进河里，生、地、化三股力在同一处交叠
scene: 研究者在同一块岩石上同时记录菌群、矿物与酸碱变化。 A biogeochemical approach explains why the lake turned acidic after the mine opened.
sceneCN: 这里 biogeochemical 指「把生物、地质与化学过程合并考察的」（第 1 个义项：跨学科属性）；句意为生物地球化学的视角解释了矿场开采后湖泊为何变酸。

pos.zh: 生物地球化学的（用于名词前，无比较级；副词形式加 -ly）

derivatives.zh: bio-（希腊 bios「生命」）+ geo-（希腊 gē「大地」）+ chemistry → 生物地球化学：研究生命、岩石与化学过程的交互
biogeochemistry + -ist（从业者后缀）→ 生物地球化学家
geo- + chemical + -al → 地球化学的：只讲岩石与化学，不含生物这一维
bio- + chemical + -al → 生物化学的：只讲生物体内的化学，不含地质这一维
bio- + geographic → 生物地理的：讲物种分布，不讲元素流转
希腊 khēmeia（冶炼之术）经阿拉伯 al-kīmiyā 与拉丁 alchimia → 化学：研究物质组成与变化的学问

senses.title: The combined viewpoint
senses.definition: treating biological, geological and chemical processes as one interacting system
senses.definitionCN: 把生物、地质与化学过程当作一个相互作用的系统来处理
senses.example: A biogeochemical approach explains why the lake turned acidic after the mine opened.
senses.exampleCN: 生物地球化学的视角解释了矿场开采后湖泊为何变酸。
senses.why: the word exists precisely because no one of the three processes explains the result alone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词之所以存在，正因为三者中任何一个单独都解释不了结果。

senses.title: Element circulation
senses.definition: describing the movement of an element among air, water, rock and life
senses.definitionCN: 描述元素在空气、水、岩石与生命之间的移动
senses.example: Carbon and nitrogen are studied as biogeochemical cycles.
senses.exampleCN: 碳与氮都作为生物地球化学循环来研究。
senses.why: the compound's main job is to name element turnover that crosses the living and non-living divide.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词的主要职责，是命名跨越生物与非生物界限的元素周转。

senses.title: Stores and fluxes
senses.definition: expressing a system as measurable reservoirs linked by flows
senses.definitionCN: 把系统表达为由流动连接的可测储库
senses.example: The biogeochemical budget lists every store and flux in the watershed.
senses.exampleCN: 这份生物地球化学收支列出了流域中每个储库与通量。
senses.why: to combine three processes quantitatively, they must be turned into stocks and rates.
senses.whyCN: 要把三种过程定量合并，就必须把它们变成存量与速率。

senses.title: Rock, water and microbes
senses.titleCN: 岩石、水与微生物的交界
senses.definition: concerning the weathering zone where microbes alter minerals and water carries the products
senses.definitionCN: 涉及微生物改造矿物、水搬运产物的风化带
senses.example: Biogeochemical weathering releases metals that plants then absorb.
senses.exampleCN: 生物地球化学风化释放金属，随后被植物吸收。
senses.why: the most literal use is at the surface where life touches rock directly.
senses.whyCN: 最字面的用法就在生命直接接触岩石的地表。

senses.title: Tracers and signatures
senses.definition: using isotopes or chemical ratios to follow a process through the environment
senses.definitionCN: 用同位素或化学比值追踪环境中的一个过程
senses.example: A biogeochemical tracer revealed that the sulphur came from the mine.
senses.exampleCN: 一种生物地球化学示踪物表明硫来自那座矿。
senses.why: when the processes are invisible, their chemical fingerprints become the evidence.
senses.whyCN: 当过程不可见时，它们的化学指纹就成了证据。

senses.title: Models and prediction
senses.definition: describing computer models that couple biology, geology and chemistry to forecast change
senses.definitionCN: 描述把生物、地质与化学耦合起来预测变化的计算模型
senses.example: The biogeochemical model predicted a drop in soil carbon.
senses.exampleCN: 该生物地球化学模型预测土壤碳将下降。
senses.why: prediction requires all three processes in one set of equations.
senses.whyCN: 预测要求把三种过程装进同一组方程。

senses.title: Natural processes
senses.definition: characterising ordinary natural processes such as decay, weathering or sedimentation
senses.definitionCN: 刻画腐烂、风化或沉积等寻常自然过程
senses.example: Decay is a biogeochemical process as much as a biological one.
senses.exampleCN: 腐烂既是生物过程，也是生物地球化学过程。
senses.why: the adjective reminds us that a plain natural process always has a chemical and a mineral side.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词提醒我们，寻常的自然过程总有化学与矿物的一面。

senses.title: Human disturbance
senses.definition: describing altered cycles, acidification, contamination or nutrient loading caused by people
senses.definitionCN: 描述由人造成的循环改变、酸化、污染或养分负荷
senses.example: Mine drainage creates a biogeochemical problem that persists for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 矿场排水造成一个持续数十年的生物地球化学问题。
senses.why: the term became urgent when human activity began to reshape the same three processes.
senses.whyCN: 当人类活动开始重塑同样这三种过程，这个词才变得紧迫。

senses.title: The discipline label
senses.definition: marking a field, a method or a researcher as belonging to biogeochemistry
senses.definitionCN: 标明某一领域、方法或研究者属于生物地球化学
senses.example: Her biogeochemical training let her read both the rock and the microbes.
senses.exampleCN: 她的生物地球化学训练让她既能读懂岩石，也能读懂微生物。
senses.why: as a discipline grew up, the adjective became a label for its people and methods.
senses.whyCN: 随着一门学科成长，这个形容词成了其研究者与方法的标签。

intro.en: Biogeochemical stacks three Greek elements: bios 'life', gē 'earth', and khēmeia, the art of working metals, which reached English as chemistry through Arabic and Latin. The compound belongs to the twentieth century, when Vernadsky and others made the biosphere a chemical object of study.
intro.cn: biogeochemical 叠了三个希腊成分：bios「生命」、gē「大地」，以及 khēmeia「冶炼金属之术」，后者经阿拉伯语与拉丁语成为英语 chemistry。这个复合词属于二十世纪，是维尔纳茨基等人把生物圈变成化学研究对象的时期。

items.en: Bios meant life or a way of living and supplies the bio- of biology and biogeochemistry.
items.cn: bios 意为生命或生活方式，提供 biology 与 biogeochemistry 的 bio-。

items.en: Gē meant earth, the ground; it gives the geo- of geology and geography.
items.cn: gē 意为大地、地面，给出 geology 与 geography 的 geo-。

items.en: Khēmeia named the art of working metals; Arabic al-kīmiyā and Latin alchimia carried it to English chemistry.
items.cn: khēmeia 指冶炼金属之术；阿拉伯 al-kīmiyā 与拉丁 alchimia 把它带到英语 chemistry。

items.en: Nineteenth-century naturalists joined bio- to geo- to describe the distribution of life over the earth.
items.cn: 十九世纪博物学家把 bio- 与 geo- 拼合，描述生命在地球上的分布。

items.en: Vernadsky's work on the biosphere established biogeochemistry as the study of life as a geological and chemical force.
items.cn: 维尔纳茨基关于生物圈的工作确立了生物地球化学，把生命当作地质与化学力量来研究。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the adjective's earliest recorded use is not consistently dated, though every element is documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：这个形容词最早的使用记录各家年代不一，但每个成分都有据可查。

note.en: Group one holds the look-alike adjectives that keep only part of the meaning; group two holds the fields and adjectives it overlaps with.
note.cn: 第一组是只保留了部分含义的形近形容词；第二组是与它重叠的学科与形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to the chemistry of rocks and earth materials; it leaves out the living processes that biogeochemical includes.
entries.definitionCN: 与岩石和地球物质的化学有关；它略去了生物地球化学所包含的生命过程。

entries.definition: Relating to chemistry inside living things; it says nothing about rock, soil or sediment.
entries.definitionCN: 与生物体内的化学有关；它不涉及岩石、土壤或沉积物。

entries.definition: Relating to the geographic distribution of species; it is about where organisms live, not how elements move.
entries.definitionCN: 与物种的地理分布有关；讲生物住在哪里，不讲元素如何流动。

entries.definition: The discipline itself; the adjective describes work belonging to it.
entries.definitionCN: 学科本身；形容词描述属于该学科的工作。

entries.definition: Relating to the relations of organisms and environment; it overlaps but does not name chemical or geological processes.
entries.definitionCN: 与生物和环境的关系有关；有重叠，但不命名化学或地质过程。

entries.definition: Relating to the surroundings in general; the biogeochemical label is narrower and technical.
entries.definitionCN: 与环境总体有关；生物地球化学这个标签更窄、更技术化。

entries.definition: The study of the planet as interacting spheres; biogeochemistry is one of its working languages.
entries.definitionCN: 把行星当作互相作用的圈层来研究；生物地球化学是其工作语言之一。

entries.definition: The turnover of nutrients in an ecosystem; it is a common subject of biogeochemical study, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 生态系统中养分的周转；它是生物地球化学的常见课题，而非同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the three real Greek roots and the three real processes they name.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：三个真实的希腊词根，以及它们命名的三种真实过程。

normal.en: bio- is bios, life; geo- is gē, earth; chemical is khēmeia, metalworking.
normal.cn: bio- 即 bios「生命」；geo- 即 gē「大地」；chemical 即 khēmeia「冶炼」。

normal.en: Three hands on one rock: a microbe, a rain cloud and a chemical reaction.
normal.cn: 三只手同在一块岩石上：微生物、雨云与化学反应。

normal.en: If a question involves life, rock and chemistry at once, the adjective fits.
normal.cn: 若一个问题同时涉及生命、岩石与化学，这个形容词就适用。

normal.en: Vernadsky is the name to attach: he treated the biosphere as a chemical engine.
normal.cn: 该记住的名字是维尔纳茨基：他把生物圈当作化学引擎。

normal.en: The usual partner noun is cycle, because elements are what travel.
normal.cn: 最常搭配的名词是 cycle，因为流动的正是元素。

abstract.en: It is a conversation between a stone, a bacterium and a river.
abstract.cn: 它是一场石头、细菌与河流之间的对话。

abstract.en: The word is a three-way junction with no dead ends.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一个没有死路的三岔口。

abstract.en: Life is not outside geology; it is one of geology's chemists.
abstract.cn: 生命并不在地质之外；它是地质的化学家之一。

examples.en: Biogeochemical models couple soil microbes to mineral weathering.
examples.cn: 生物地球化学模型把土壤微生物与矿物风化耦合起来。

examples.en: The team measured biogeochemical gradients across the sediment surface.
examples.cn: 团队测量了穿过沉积物表层的生物地球化学梯度。

examples.en: Her paper treats the wetland as a single biogeochemical reactor.
examples.cn: 她的论文把这片湿地当作一个整体的生物地球化学反应器。

dict_mnemonic.text: bio（生命）+ geo（大地）+ chemical（化学）＝把生命、岩石与化学放在一起看；常见搭配是 cycle，因为元素在圈层间流动。

root: bio-（希腊 bios「生命」）+ geo-（希腊 gē「大地」）+ chemical（希腊 khēmeia「冶炼术」经阿拉伯语与拉丁语入英语）；复合词为二十世纪生物地球化学所立。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from the widest view to the narrowest: the combined viewpoint, element circulation, stores and fluxes, the rock-water-microbe zone, tracers, models, natural processes, human disturbance and the discipline label.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从最宽到最窄：合并视角、元素循环、储库与通量、岩石与水与微生物的交界、示踪物、模型、自然过程、人类扰动，以及学科标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a microbe etching a mineral, a root following the crack, rain carrying the residue into a stream.
core.cn: 核心意象：微生物蚀刻矿物，根须沿着裂缝跟进，雨水把残余带进溪流。

branches.en: THE VIEW AND THE FIELD: first the combined outlook, then the discipline that institutionalises it.
branches.cn: 视角与学科：先是合并的眼光，再是把它制度化为一门学科。

branches.en: CIRCULATION AND ACCOUNTING: element turnover, then the stores and fluxes that measure it.
branches.cn: 循环与核算：先是元素周转，再是衡量它的储库与通量。

branches.en: THE CONTACT ZONE: rock-water-microbe weathering, then ordinary natural processes of the same kind.
branches.cn: 接触带：岩石与水与微生物的风化，再是同类寻常自然过程。

branches.en: EVIDENCE AND PREDICTION: chemical tracers, then coupled models.
branches.cn: 证据与预测：先是化学示踪物，再是耦合模型。

branches.en: HUMAN DAMAGE: acid drainage, contamination and nutrient loading as biogeochemical problems.
branches.cn: 人类造成的损害：酸性排水、污染与养分负荷成为生物地球化学问题。

intro.en: Biogeochemical is a three-part Greek compound with an English adjective ending: life, earth and metalworking, joined by -al.
intro.cn: biogeochemical 是希腊语三部分复合词加上英语形容词词尾：生命、大地与冶炼，由 -al 连接。

latinIntro.en: The roots are Greek and have no native Latin cognates; Latin acted only as a carrier, taking khēmeia through Arabic as alchimia and borrowing Greek terms such as geographia.
latinIntro.cn: 这些词根属希腊语，拉丁语中没有本土同族词；拉丁语只作传递通道，把 khēmeia 经阿拉伯语作 alchimia 传入，并借入 geographia 等希腊词。

items.example: Bios is the root of biology.
items.exampleCN: bios 是 biology 的词根。

items.example: Gē gives the geo- of geology.
items.exampleCN: gē 给出 geology 的 geo-。

items.example: Khēmeia travelled through Arabic into chemistry.
items.exampleCN: khēmeia 经阿拉伯语进入 chemistry。

items.structure: al-kīmiyā (Arabic noun, with the definite article)
items.example: Al-kīmiyā became Medieval Latin alchimia.
items.exampleCN: al-kīmiyā 变成中世纪拉丁 alchimia。

items.structure: chemistry (English noun from alchimia and earlier Greek khēmeia)
items.meaning: the science of substances and their changes
items.meaningCN: 研究物质及其变化的科学
items.example: Chemistry now names a laboratory science.
items.exampleCN: chemistry 如今指一门实验科学。

items.meaning: the study of life, rock and chemical interaction
items.meaningCN: 研究生命、岩石与化学交互的学科
items.example: Biogeochemistry grew out of biosphere science.
items.exampleCN: 生物地球化学由生物圈科学发展而来。

items.example: Biogeochemical data mix field and lab work.
items.exampleCN: 生物地球化学数据混合了野外与实验室工作。

items.example: Geochemical surveys map ore bodies.
items.exampleCN: 地球化学测量绘制矿体分布。

items.example: Biochemical assays measure enzymes.

definition_zh: 愿意的；乐意的；自愿的；甘愿的；听话的；愿意倾听的
definition_en: ready or glad to do something, often without being asked or forced
core_image: 一个本来可以拒绝的人，把已经放下的工具又拿起来，说好，我来
scene: 搬家前夜，朋友临时说缺一个人手，他本已请了假，却还是把外套挂回门边，问几点到。 He was willing to give up his day off and asked what time to arrive.
sceneCN: 这里 willing 指「本来可以拒绝却乐意答应」（第 1 个义项：愿意做某事）；句意为尽管请了假，他还是愿意放弃休息，并问几点到。

pos.zh: 愿意的；乐意的；自愿的；甘愿的；顺从的

derivatives.zh: 乐意地（由 willing 加副词后缀，把乐意转成动作方式）
乐意；意愿（由 willing 加名词后缀，从人的态度转为抽象状态）
不愿意的（由否定前缀加 willing，把乐意整个反转）
不情愿（由否定前缀加 willing 再加名词后缀，指拒绝的心理状态）

senses.title: Ready to do something
senses.definition: prepared and glad to do something if asked or needed
senses.definitionCN: 如果被请求或需要，愿意并且乐意去做
senses.example: She is always willing to answer questions after class.
senses.exampleCN: 她课后总是愿意回答问题。
senses.why: The adjective starts from an open door: nothing blocks the action, so the person can say yes at once.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从一扇开着的门开始：没有什么挡住行动，所以人立刻就能说「好」。

senses.title: Giving consent without pressure
senses.definition: agreeing freely, with no force or trickery
senses.definitionCN: 自由地同意，没有强迫或欺骗
senses.example: Participants gave willing consent before the interviews began.
senses.exampleCN: 访谈开始前，参与者自愿表示了同意。
senses.why: Willingness here is legal and ethical: the yes must come from the person's own decision, not from a push.
senses.whyCN: 这里的乐意带有法律与伦理意味：这个「好」必须出自行本人的决定，而不是被推出来的。

senses.title: Eager and cooperative
senses.definition: showing eagerness to join in and help
senses.definitionCN: 表现出想加入和帮忙的热切
senses.example: The new intern was a willing helper at every event.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的实习生在每场活动上都是个热心的帮手。
senses.why: Readiness with energy becomes cooperation; the person does not wait to be told but steps toward the work.
senses.whyCN: 乐意加上能量就成了配合：这个人不等别人开口，而是自己朝工作迈过去。

senses.title: Done or given freely
senses.definition: offered or accepted without complaint, even at a real cost
senses.definitionCN: 即使有实际代价，也毫无怨言地给出或接受
senses.example: Their willing sacrifice kept the shelter open all winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们甘愿付出，让收容所整个冬天都开着。
senses.why: When the cost is real, the yes is no longer cheap; the word then points at generosity rather than mere permission.
senses.whyCN: 当代价真实存在，这个「好」就不再廉价；词义随之指向慷慨，而不只是许可。

senses.title: Easily managed
senses.definition: compliant and easy to direct, sometimes with less independence than is healthy
senses.definitionCN: 顺从、容易指挥，有时独立性不足
senses.example: The manager wanted a willing instrument rather than a thinking partner.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经理想要一件顺手的工具，而不是一个会思考的伙伴。
senses.why: Something that never resists can be used like a tool; the word slides from readiness into pliability, and the tone can turn critical.
senses.whyCN: 从不抵抗的东西可以像工具一样被使用；词义从乐意滑向易摆布，语气也可能转为批评。

senses.title: God willing
senses.definition: used in the fixed phrase God willing to mean 'if nothing prevents it'
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示「但愿如此」的固定说法，表示「如果没有阻碍的话」
senses.example: God willing, we will meet again next spring.
senses.exampleCN: 但愿明年春天我们还能再见。
senses.why: The phrase leaves the final decision to a higher power: human readiness is real, but it is not the last word.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把最终决定交给更高的力量：人的乐意是真的，但不是最后一句话。

senses.title: Willing suspension of disbelief
senses.definition: in literary theory, the reader's choice to accept a story's impossible events
senses.definitionCN: 文学理论中，读者选择接受故事里不可能发生的事
senses.example: The opening scene earns the audience's willing suspension of disbelief.
senses.exampleCN: 开场那一场戏赢得了观众自愿的暂时相信。
senses.why: The reader knows the story is not real and still agrees to be moved; readiness is aimed at belief itself.
senses.whyCN: 读者知道故事不真实，却仍然同意被打动；这里的乐意指向的是「相信」本身。

senses.title: A willing ear
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase a willing ear, a person who listens readily
senses.definitionCN: 指在固定说法中乐意听人说话的人
senses.example: After the long trip, he found a willing ear in the station café.
senses.exampleCN: 长途旅行之后，他在车站咖啡馆里找到一个愿意听他说的人。
senses.why: The ear stands for the whole person: readiness is concentrated in one body part that is offered to someone else's story.
senses.whyCN: 耳朵代指整个人：乐意集中在一个身体部位上，被递给别人的故事。

intro.en: Willing is the present-participle adjective of the native Germanic verb will, recorded in English from the early fourteenth century. No Latin borrowing is involved in this family.
intro.cn: willing 是本土日耳曼语动词 will 的现在分词形容词，从十四世纪初起在英语中有记录。这一词族没有拉丁语借入成分。

items.en: Old English willan meant 'to wish, desire; be willing'. Its present participle willende is the direct ancestor of the modern form willing.
items.cn: 古英语 willan 意为「希望、意愿；愿意」，它的现在分词 willende 就是现代形式 willing 的直接祖先。

items.en: The verb is reconstructed as *willjan 'to will, wish', with the noun *wiljo 'will, desire'. These are reconstructed forms, not attested words.
items.cn: 这个动词被重构为原始日耳曼语 *willjan「愿意、希望」，名词是 *wiljo「意愿、愿望」。这些都是重构形式，不是有记录的词。

items.en: By the early fourteenth century willing was used as an adjective meaning 'eager to do, favorably disposed', and the adverb willingly appears soon after.
items.cn: 到十四世纪初，willing 已作形容词使用，意为「急于去做、有好感」，副词 willingly 也很快出现。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the word also stressed promptness and readiness in action, and fixed phrases such as God willing spread in everyday speech.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个词还强调行动上的爽快与随时待命，「但愿如此」之类的固定说法在日常口语中传播开来。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective for everyday readiness, and the phrase willing suspension of disbelief became a standard term in literary criticism after Coleridge.
items.cn: 现代英语保留这个形容词表示日常的乐意；「自愿暂时相信」这一说法在柯勒律治之后成为文学批评的标准术语。

items.en: Source uncertain: deeper Indo-European connections are debated. A reconstructed root *wel- 'to wish' is often proposed, but it is a reconstruction, not a recorded word, and its exact reach is disputed; this entry treats the English family as Germanic and builds no Latin branch from it.
items.cn: 来源不确定：更深的印欧语联系有争议。常有人提出重构词根 *wel-「希望」，但它只是重构形式，不是有记录的词，覆盖范围也有争论；本词条把英语这一族按日耳曼语线处理，不据此建立拉丁语分支。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound close and are often confused with willing; the second holds near neighbours that also describe a yes, but with a different strength or source.
note.cn: 第一组是与 willing 形近或音近、容易混淆的词；第二组是同为「答应」但力度或来源不同的近义词。

entries.definition: The verb and noun at the root of willing: to wish or desire, and the power of choice.
entries.definitionCN: willing 的词根动词与名词：希望、意愿，以及选择的能力。

entries.definition: Built from will plus -ful, but it means stubborn or done on purpose, not ready to agree.
entries.definitionCN: 由 will 加表示「充满……」的形容词后缀构成，但意思是固执或故意的，而不是乐意同意。

entries.definition: Craftiness, from wile 'a trick'. It shares letters with willing but not a root.
entries.definitionCN: 狡猾，来自 wile「诡计」。它与 willing 共享字母，却没有共同词根，二者并非同源。

entries.definition: The negative form of the same adjective; the prefix reverses the yes without changing the family.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个形容词的否定形式；前缀把「好」反转，却没有换掉词族。

entries.definition: Prepared and able; it can describe tools as well as people, while willing describes people and their attitude.
entries.definitionCN: 准备好的、能够的；既可形容人也可形容工具，而 willing 只描写人的态度。

entries.definition: Full of keen desire and impatient to begin; stronger and less calm than willing.
entries.definitionCN: 满怀热望、急着开始；比 willing 更强、更不平静。

entries.definition: Obeying a rule or order; it stresses behaviour under authority, not inner readiness.
entries.definitionCN: 服从规则或命令；强调在权威下的行为，而不是内心的乐意。

entries.definition: Done by free choice rather than force, often in legal or official contexts; it names the status of an act, not a feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 出于自由选择而非强迫，常用于法律或正式语境；它说的是行为的性质，而非感受。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词语素、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: will (to wish) + -ing: willing is literally 'wishing, wanting', which is why it means ready rather than forced.
normal.cn: will（希望）加现在分词词尾：willing 字面上就是「正在希望、想要」，所以它表示乐意而非被逼。

normal.en: The family runs will, willing, willingly, willingness, unwilling, unwillingness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 will、willing、willingly、willingness、unwilling、unwillingness。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the target of the readiness: be willing to do, willing consent, a willing ear, God willing.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出乐意指向哪里：愿意做、自愿同意、愿意倾听、但愿如此。

normal.en: The negative is un- plus willing, not a separate root: unwilling simply closes the open door.
normal.cn: 否定形式是否定前缀加 willing，不是另一个词根：unwilling 只是把那扇开着的门关上。

normal.en: Willing suspension of disbelief is a fixed phrase from literary criticism, not a separate sense of the root.
normal.cn: 「自愿暂时相信」是文学批评里的固定说法，并不是词根另长出的意思。

abstract.en: Picture an open door with no lock on the inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇从里面没有锁的门。

abstract.en: Picture a hand already reaching for the tool before the name is called.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在名字被叫到之前就已经伸向工具。

abstract.en: Picture a yes that costs a day off, which makes it worth more.
abstract.cn: 想象一个要牺牲一天休假的「好」，正因如此它更值钱。

examples.en: She was willing to move to another city for the job.
examples.cn: 为了这份工作，她愿意搬到另一座城市。

examples.en: A willing listener can do more good than quick advice.
examples.cn: 一个愿意倾听的人，比急着给建议的人更有用。

examples.en: They signed the agreement with willing consent.
examples.cn: 他们自愿同意并签了这份协议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威尔灵」—— 威尔抬手说我来，做事带着一股愿意的灵气 → willing 愿意的；乐意的

root: 本土日耳曼语线：古英语 willan「希望、意愿」的现在分词 willende 演变为 willing；与名词 will 同源，英语这一族没有从拉丁语借入的同族词，更深的印欧词根属重构形式且有争议。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one open door: a person who does not need to be pushed. The yes can be legal consent, energetic help, a costly gift, pliable obedience, a fixed phrase about providence, a reader's choice to believe, or an ear offered to a story.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一扇开着的门展开：一个不需要别人推的人。这个「好」可以是法律同意、热心帮忙、有代价的付出、顺从好使、关于天意的固定短语、读者选择相信，或一只递给故事的耳朵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open door that no one has to push.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇不需要别人推的门。

branches.en: THE CORE: readiness is an unlocked door, and the action can begin at once.
branches.cn: 核心：乐意是一扇没上锁的门，行动可以立刻开始。

branches.en: THE YES AND ITS PRICE: free consent and costly sacrifice are the same yes seen with and without a bill.
branches.cn: 「好」与它的代价：自由同意和有代价的付出，是同一个「好」在有账单和没账单时的样子。

branches.en: THE YES IN COMPANY: it steps forward as a helper, or concentrates into an ear offered to someone.
branches.cn: 人群中的「好」：它作为帮手向前迈步，或收拢成一只递向别人的耳朵。

branches.en: THE YES WITHOUT A SPINE: readiness that never resists can become mere pliability.
branches.cn: 没有脊梁的「好」：从不抵抗的乐意，可能变成单纯的易摆布。

branches.en: THE YES IN FORMULAS: providence and fiction both use the word inside fixed phrases.
branches.cn: 固定说法里的「好」：天意与虚构都把这个词收进了固定短语。

intro.en: Willing is a Germanic verb stem plus a participle ending, and the family grows by adding common prefixes and suffixes.
intro.cn: willing 是日耳曼语动词词干加分词词尾，整个词族靠常见前缀和后缀继续生长。

latinIntro.en: The stem is the native Germanic will; English has no Latin-borrowed relative of this family, so the Latin section is intentionally empty.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是本土日耳曼语的 will；英语中没有从拉丁语借入的这一词族成员，因此拉丁同族词部分有意留空。

items.structure: Old English willan 'to wish, desire' (verb and noun root)
items.meaning: to wish; the power of choosing
items.example: Will is the root behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: will 是整个词族背后的词根。

items.meaning: the ending that makes 'the one who wills'
items.meaningCN: 把动词变成「正在愿意的人」的词尾
items.example: The ending turns the verb into a description.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成一种描写。

items.example: She gave a willing answer.
items.exampleCN: 她乐意地作了回答。

items.example: He agreed willingly.
items.exampleCN: 他乐意地同意了。

items.example: Her willingness was obvious.
items.exampleCN: 她的乐意显而易见。

items.example: The witness was unwilling to speak.
items.exampleCN: 那名证人不愿意开口。

items.example: His unwillingness ended the discussion.
items.exampleCN: 他的不情愿让讨论停了下来。

items.example: The visit was a gesture of goodwill.
items.exampleCN: 这次访问是善意的表示。

items.example: The debate concerns free will.
items.exampleCN: 这场争论关乎自由意志。
