definition_zh: 藻类的；由藻类组成的；藻类造成的
definition_en: relating to, consisting of, or caused by algae
core_image: 浅水池壁上那层滑腻的绿膜，肉眼只看到一片绿色，显微镜下才是一团单细胞生物
scene: 池塘边，几个孩子发现浅水处的石头上覆着一层滑腻的绿膜，老师蹲下来指着水样说，那是微型藻类在迅速繁殖。 A thick algal film had formed on the stones where the water was warm and still.
sceneCN: 这里 algal 指「藻类形成的、藻类的」（第 1 个义项：与藻类相关或由藻类构成）；句意为在温暖静止的浅水处，石头上已经结了一层厚厚的藻膜。

pos.zh: 藻类的；由藻类组成的；由藻类引起的

derivatives.zh: 藻类（alga 的复数，也作集合名）

senses.title: Relating to algae as organisms
senses.titleCN: 与藻类这一生物类群有关
senses.definition: relating to algae, the simple photosynthetic organisms that live in water and damp places
senses.definitionCN: 与藻类有关的；藻类指生活在水中或潮湿处、能进行光合作用的简单生物
senses.example: Algal cells were counted under the microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 藻细胞在显微镜下被逐一计数。
senses.why: The suffix -al turns the noun alga into an adjective of relation, so algal means 'of algae' before it means anything more specific.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把名词 alga 变成表关系的形容词，因此 algal 的基础义就是「藻的」，其余义项都由此细化。

senses.title: Consisting of a mass of algae
senses.definition: made up of a dense layer or mass of algae
senses.definitionCN: 由密集的藻类层或藻类群体构成的
senses.example: A green algal mat covered the rock at the outflow.
senses.exampleCN: 出水口的岩石上覆着一层绿色的藻席。
senses.why: Because algae often grow as a sheet rather than as separate plants, the adjective came to describe the whole mat, not just its members.
senses.whyCN: 藻类常成片生长而非一株株分立，因此这个形容词也用来描述整片藻席，而不只是其中的个体。

senses.title: Caused by algae
senses.definition: brought about by the growth of algae, especially in water
senses.definitionCN: 由藻类生长所引起，尤指水体中的现象
senses.example: The reservoir turned green during an algal bloom.
senses.exampleCN: 藻华期间水库变成了绿色。
senses.why: Once algae are the cause rather than the subject, the adjective marks origin: the bloom is not algae itself but what their growth produces.
senses.whyCN: 当藻类成为原因而不是主体时，这个形容词标记来源：藻华不是藻本身，而是藻类生长造成的现象。

senses.title: Carrying algal toxins
senses.titleCN: 含藻毒素的；有毒藻产生的
senses.definition: produced by toxic algae and able to harm people or animals that drink the water
senses.definitionCN: 由有毒藻类产生、能危害饮水者或动物的
senses.example: Algal toxins forced the town to switch to bottled water.
senses.exampleCN: 藻毒素迫使全镇改用瓶装水。
senses.why: Public-health writing needed a short label for poisons made by algae, and algal toxin became that fixed phrase.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生写作需要一个简短标签来指藻类产生的毒素，algal toxin 于是成为固定说法。

senses.title: Used as a feedstock
senses.definition: grown or harvested as raw material for fuel, feed or chemicals
senses.definitionCN: 作为燃料、饲料或化工原料而养殖或采收的
senses.example: Algal oil is pressed from tanks of cultivated microalgae.
senses.exampleCN: 藻油由培养微藻的槽罐中压榨而来。
senses.why: Industry extended 'of algae' to 'derived from algae', because the material, not the organism, is what the refinery handles.
senses.whyCN: 工业把「藻的」扩展为「从藻得到的」，因为工厂处理的是材料而不是生物体。

senses.title: Living inside a host
senses.definition: describing algae that live within the tissue of a host organism such as a coral
senses.definitionCN: 描述生活在珊瑚等宿主体内的藻类
senses.example: Reef-building corals depend on their algal partners for sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 造礁珊瑚依赖体内的共生藻提供糖分。
senses.why: In symbiosis the algae are no longer free-living, so the adjective signals the partner role rather than a place.
senses.whyCN: 在共生关系中藻类不再自由生活，因此这个形容词标示的是「伙伴角色」而非地点。

senses.title: Preserved in rock
senses.titleCN: 保存在岩层中的藻类遗迹
senses.definition: referring to structures in sedimentary rock that were built by algae
senses.definitionCN: 指沉积岩中由藻类建造的结构
senses.example: Algal limestone records shallow seas of the distant past.
senses.exampleCN: 藻灰岩记录了远古的浅海。
senses.why: Geology keeps the same adjective because the rock is still, literally, made of algal remains.
senses.whyCN: 地质学沿用同一形容词，因为这种岩石确实由藻类遗骸构成。

senses.title: Tasting or smelling of algae
senses.definition: having the earthy, fishy taste or smell associated with algae in water
senses.definitionCN: 带有水中藻类那种土腥、鱼腥的味道或气味
senses.example: The tap water had an algal taste after the warm spell.
senses.exampleCN: 回暖之后，自来水带上了藻味。
senses.why: Water-quality reports speak of algal taste and odour, so the adjective also names a sensory impression rather than an organism.
senses.whyCN: 水质报告常说「藻味与藻腥气」，于是这个形容词也指一种感官印象，而非生物体。

intro.en: Algal is an English adjective built from Latin alga 'seaweed' plus the relational suffix -al; the noun is classical, the adjective is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: algal 是英语形容词，由拉丁 alga「海藻」加表关系的后缀 -al 构成；名词是古典的，形容词是近代形成的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Alga meant 'seaweed, sea wrack'. Its deeper origin is not established; a suggested link to algere 'to be cold' is only a guess, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: alga 意为「海藻、海草」。其更深来源未得到证明；有人把它与 algere「发冷」联系起来，那只是猜测，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Classical Latin already had the adjective algosus 'full of seaweed', which shows the noun was productive long before the English form appeared.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语已有形容词 algosus「长满海藻的」，说明这个名词在英语形式出现之前早就有构词能力。

items.en: From the eighteenth century botanists used algae as a group name, and English took the Latin plural in -ae rather than adding an English -s.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，植物学家用 algae 作类群名，英语直接沿用拉丁语以 -ae 结尾的复数，而不加英语的 -s。

items.en: The adjective algal is recorded from the mid-nineteenth century, first in botanical descriptions and later in water-quality writing.
items.cn: 形容词 algal 自 19 世纪中叶有记录，最初用于植物学描述，后来进入水质研究文字。

items.en: Twentieth-century technology fixed phrases such as algal bloom, algal mat, algal toxin and algal fuel, where the adjective simply labels the source.
items.cn: 20 世纪的技术文献固定了 algal bloom、algal mat、algal toxin、algal fuel 等说法，其中形容词只标示来源。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the pre-Latin origin of alga is unsettled, and any Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：alga 在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，凡为它提出的印欧形式都属重构形式，而非有记录的词。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same word and its closest derivatives, which are constantly mixed up; group two holds adjectives from neighbouring habitats that are not interchangeable.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词及其最近派生形式，最易混用；第二组是来自相邻生境的形容词，彼此不能替换。

entries.definition: One alga is a single organism; algal is the adjective made from it, never a plural.
entries.definitionCN: 一个 alga 是单个藻体；algal 是由它构成的形容词，从不用作复数。

entries.definition: The plural of alga and also the informal group name; it is a noun, so it cannot replace algal in front of another noun.
entries.definitionCN: alga 的复数，也作非正式的类群名；它是名词，不能像 algal 那样放在另一个名词前作定语。

entries.definition: Built with -oid 'like', it says something looks like algae without necessarily being algal.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -oid「像」构成，表示某物看起来像藻，但不一定真的属于藻类。

entries.definition: The branch of botany that studies algae; the -logy marks a discipline, not a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 研究藻类的植物学分支；-logy 标示学科，而非性质。

entries.definition: Describes organisms that drift in open water, algae included; it answers where they live, while algal answers what they are.
entries.definitionCN: 描述在开阔水域漂浮生活的生物，包含藻类；它回答「住在哪里」，algal 回答「是什么」。

entries.definition: Describes life on or near the seabed; an algal mat may be benthic, but the adjective benthic says nothing about algae.
entries.definitionCN: 描述生活在海底或其附近的生物；藻席可以是底栖的，但 benthic 本身与藻类无关。

entries.definition: Covers bacteria and other single-celled organisms as well as algae, so it is broader than algal.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖细菌与其他单细胞生物，也包括藻类，因此比 algal 范围更宽。

entries.definition: Describes the process of using light to make food; many algae are photosynthetic, but the term also covers plants.
entries.definitionCN: 描述利用光能制造养分的过程；许多藻类能进行光合作用，但这个词也涵盖植物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: alga is the noun, -al makes the adjective: algal simply means 'of algae'.
normal.cn: alga 是名词，加 -al 构成形容词：algal 的意思就是「藻的」。

normal.en: The plural is algae, with Latin -ae, but algal never takes a plural ending.
normal.cn: 复数是拉丁式的 algae（-ae 结尾），但 algal 本身没有复数形式。

normal.en: Algology is the study of algae, and algologist is the person who does it.
normal.cn: algology 是藻类学，algologist 是从事藻类研究的人。

normal.en: Algicide kills algae, the way herbicide kills plants and insecticide kills insects.
normal.cn: algicide 杀藻，正如 herbicide 除草、insecticide 杀虫。

normal.en: Fixed phrases carry the technical senses: algal bloom, algal mat, algal toxin, algal fuel.
normal.cn: 固定搭配承担技术义：藻华、藻席、藻毒素、藻类燃料。

abstract.en: Picture a clear pond going opaque green in a single warm week.
abstract.cn: 想象一池清水在一个温暖的星期里变成不透光的绿。

abstract.en: Picture one drop of pond water holding a whole microscopic forest.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴池水里藏着一整座微观森林。

abstract.en: Picture a limestone cliff that is really a cemetery of algae turned to stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一面石灰岩崖壁，其实是被石化了的藻类墓地。

examples.en: Algal growth in the bay doubled after the fertiliser runoff.
examples.cn: 化肥径流之后，海湾里的藻类生长量翻了一倍。

examples.en: The team measured algal biomass to estimate the bloom's size.
examples.cn: 团队测量藻类生物量以估算藻华的规模。

examples.en: Coral bleached when the algal partners inside it died.
examples.cn: 当体内的共生藻死亡时，珊瑚就白化了。

dict_mnemonic.text: alga 读起来像「阿狗」——水里的藻类多得像狗毛一样糊在石头上；algal 就是「藻的」

root: 拉丁 alga「海藻」+ 英语形容词后缀 -al；alga 的更深来源不确定，与 algere「发冷」的联系只是假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all radiate from one attribute: something is of algae, made of algae, or produced by algae; the uses move from the microscope to the lake, the fuel tank, the coral polyp, the rock layer and finally the tap.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从同一个属性展开：某物属于藻、由藻构成或由藻产生；用法从显微镜走向湖泊、燃料罐、珊瑚虫、岩层，最后走到水龙头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slippery green film on a stone, invisible cells seen as one mass.
core.cn: 核心意象：石头上那层滑腻的绿膜，看不见的细胞汇成一片。

branches.en: PLAIN ATTRIBUTE: from a microscope count to a taste in tap water, the link is simply 'of algae'.
branches.cn: 单纯属性：从显微镜计数到自来水里的味道，联系都只是「与藻有关」。

branches.en: ONE SHEET: algae grow as a mat, so the adjective names a mass rather than a specimen.
branches.cn: 成片：藻类成席生长，因此形容词指的是一片，而非一个标本。

branches.en: ALGAE AS CAUSE: a bloom and its toxins are results attributed to algae.
branches.cn: 藻为起因：藻华与其毒素都是归因于藻类的结果。

branches.en: ALGAE AS MATERIAL: industry turns the organism into oil, feed and chemicals.
branches.cn: 藻作材料：工业把生物体变成油、饲料与化工品。

branches.en: ALGAE INSIDE SOMETHING ELSE: a partner in coral tissue, a ghost in limestone.
branches.cn: 藻在别物之中：珊瑚组织里的伙伴，石灰岩里的幽灵。

intro.en: Algal can be read as a stem plus one suffix, and the stem itself supports a small family of technical words.
intro.cn: algal 可拆为一个词干加一个后缀，而这个词干本身还支撑着一小族技术词。

latinIntro.en: Latin alga 'seaweed' yields alga, algae, algal and algology in English; algosus is the classical adjective built on the same noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 alga「海藻」在英语中衍生 alga、algae、algal 与 algology；algosus 是同一名词构成的古典形容词。

items.example: The singular names one organism.
items.exampleCN: 单数形式指一个藻体。

items.meaning: algae, the group as a whole
items.example: Algae drifted in dense patches.
items.exampleCN: 藻类成片漂浮。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into a relational adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表关系的形容词。

items.example: An algal film covered the stones.
items.exampleCN: 一层藻膜覆盖着石头。

items.example: Algology grew out of nineteenth-century botany.
items.exampleCN: 藻类学从 19 世纪的植物学中发展出来。

items.example: The algologist sampled the kelp bed each spring.
items.exampleCN: 这位藻类学家每年春天都给海藻林取样。

items.example: The pool was treated with an algicide.
items.exampleCN: 泳池用杀藻剂处理过。

items.meaning: a gum extracted from brown algae
items.example: Alginate thickens the ice-cream mix.
items.exampleCN: 藻酸盐使冰淇淋浆料变稠。

items.meaning: a rapid overgrowth of algae in water
items.example: The algal bloom stained the shoreline green.
items.exampleCN: 藻华把岸线染成绿色。

latinEntries.structure: algosus, algosa, algosum (adjective, first and second declension)

definition_zh: 发掘；考古发掘工作、现场或成果；土方开挖；挖出的坑
definition_en: the process of digging out earth or buried material, especially for archaeology, or the hole made by digging
core_image: 方形探坑一层层向下收窄，坑壁插着标签，坑底露出石砌地面
scene: 工地被划成整齐的方格，工人用小铲一层层刮去表土，坑壁贴上编号纸条，坑底渐渐露出石砌地面。 The excavation, the careful digging of a buried site, uncovered a wall that had lain under the field for centuries.
sceneCN: 这里 excavation 指「考古发掘的过程与工程」（第 1 个义项：有方法地把埋藏物挖出并记录）；句意为这次发掘揭开了一道在田野下埋了数百年的墙。可辨识物件：方格探坑、小铲、编号纸条、石砌地面、土堆。

pos.zh: 发掘；开挖；发掘现场或坑（可数，复数 excavations）

senses.title: The process of digging out buried material
senses.definition: the systematic removal of soil and deposits to expose remains or reach a level
senses.definitionCN: 有系统地移去土壤与堆积，以暴露遗存或到达某一层位
senses.example: The excavation uncovered a wall that had lain under the field for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这次发掘揭开了一道在田野下埋了数百年的墙。
senses.why: ex- 'out' plus cavare 'to hollow' gives 'hollow out'; the noun names the whole act of making a hollow.
senses.whyCN: ex-「出」加 cavare「挖空」构成「挖出空洞」；名词指整个挖空行为。

senses.title: The site or pit of a dig
senses.definition: the place, trench or pit where digging is under way
senses.definitionCN: 正在挖掘的地点、探沟或坑
senses.example: Visitors were kept back from the excavation.
senses.exampleCN: 参观者被挡住，不能靠近发掘现场。
senses.why: the act and the place share one word because the hole is the act's visible result.
senses.whyCN: 行为与地点共用一个词，因为坑就是行为可见的结果。

senses.title: The finds produced by a dig
senses.definition: the objects and records recovered in the course of digging
senses.definitionCN: 挖掘过程中获得的物件与记录
senses.example: The excavation produced three coins and a seal.
senses.exampleCN: 这次发掘出三枚硬币和一枚印章。
senses.why: a dig is judged by what it yields, so the noun can stand for its output.
senses.whyCN: 一次发掘以其收获来评判，因此名词可代指其产出。

senses.title: Earthwork or engineering cut
senses.definition: the removal of soil for a foundation, road, tunnel or canal
senses.definitionCN: 为地基、道路、隧道或运河而移走土壤
senses.example: The excavation for the tunnel took two years.
senses.exampleCN: 隧道开挖花了两年。
senses.why: the engineering sense came first in English; archaeology later borrowed the same term.
senses.whyCN: 英语中工程义先出现，考古学后来借用了同一术语。

senses.title: The archaeological method
senses.definition: the controlled technique of digging in layers, recording context and preserving finds
senses.definitionCN: 按层位挖掘、记录背景并保存器物的受控技术
senses.example: Modern excavation records every layer before removing it.
senses.exampleCN: 现代发掘在移除每一层之前先作记录。
senses.why: once digging became a science, the word named a method rather than mere earth-moving.
senses.whyCN: 当挖掘成为科学，这个词就命名方法，而不只是搬土。

senses.title: The hole or trench left behind
senses.definition: the cavity, trench or cutting made by removal of material
senses.definitionCN: 因移走材料而形成的洞、沟或切口
senses.example: Rainwater collected in the old excavation.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水积在旧坑里。
senses.why: the result persists after the work ends, and the noun covers that persistent shape.
senses.whyCN: 工作结束后结果仍在，名词也涵盖这一持久形状。

senses.title: Metaphor: deep investigation
senses.definition: by extension, a thorough inquiry that removes layers of concealment
senses.definitionCN: 引申指层层去除掩盖的彻底调查
senses.example: The journalist's excavation of the files took months.
senses.exampleCN: 记者对这些档案的「发掘」花了数月。
senses.why: the metaphor treats secrecy as soil: each layer removed brings evidence closer.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把秘密当作泥土：每移走一层，证据就更近一步。

senses.title: Abstraction: the uncovering of what was buried
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：把埋藏之物揭开
senses.definition: any process by which something covered or forgotten is brought into view
senses.definitionCN: 任何使被覆盖或被遗忘之物显现的过程
senses.example: Excavation is memory done with tools.
senses.exampleCN: 发掘是用工具进行的记忆。
senses.why: the deepest sense is revelation by removal, whether the layers are earth, paper or silence.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层是「移除以显现」，无论层是泥土、纸张还是沉默。

intro.en: Excavation comes from Latin excavare, ex- 'out' plus cavare 'to make hollow', from cavus 'hollow'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: excavation 来自拉丁 excavare，由 ex-「出」与 cavare「挖空」构成，后者源于 cavus「空的」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cavus meant 'hollow, excavated'; it also gave English cavity and cave through related forms.
items.cn: cavus 意为「空的、挖空的」；它也经相关形式衍生英语 cavity 与 cave。

items.en: Cavare meant 'to make hollow, to dig out'; it turned the adjective into a verb of action.
items.cn: cavare 意为「使成空、挖出」；它把形容词变成动作动词。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus cavare produced excavare, 'to hollow out, dig out'.
items.cn: ex-「出」加 cavare 构成 excavare，意为「挖空、挖出」。

items.en: Excavatio named a hollowing out; English excavation came from this action noun.
items.cn: excavatio 指挖空；英语 excavation 来自这个行为名词。

items.en: Excavation entered English in the seventeenth century for earthworks; the archaeological sense developed in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: excavation 在十七世纪进入英语，指土方工程；考古义在十九世纪发展起来。

items.en: Source uncertain (first English date and root shape): dictionaries differ on the earliest English use, and the pre-Latin root of cavus is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（英语首见年代与词根形态）：辞书对最早的英语用例说法不一，cavus 的拉丁语前词根属重构。

note.en: Group one holds digging words easily confused with excavation; group two holds neighbouring ideas of removal and discovery.
note.cn: 第一组是易与 excavation 混淆的挖掘类词；第二组是移走与发现的邻近概念。

entries.definition: To carry out excavation; the noun names the work, the verb names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 指进行发掘；名词指工作，动词指去做。

entries.definition: A person or machine that excavates; it names the doer, not the deed.
entries.definitionCN: 指实施开挖的人或机器；命名施动者，而非行为。

entries.definition: A hollow space, especially in a tooth or body; it shares the root but names the void, not the work.
entries.definitionCN: 指空洞，尤指牙体或身体中的腔；同词根，但命名空处，而非工作。

entries.definition: A long narrow ditch; it can be the product of excavation or a separate military work.
entries.definitionCN: 指狭长沟；它可以是开挖的产物，也可以是单独的军事工事。

entries.definition: To break and remove ground; it is general and informal, while excavation implies method and record.
entries.definitionCN: 指破土并移走土；日常而宽泛，而 excavation 暗示方法与记录。

entries.definition: Digging to extract ore or coal; its purpose is economic, not archaeological.
entries.definitionCN: 指为开采矿石或煤而挖；目的在经济效益，而非考古。

entries.definition: Taking stone or sand from an open pit; the scale and purpose differ from a research dig.
entries.definitionCN: 指从露天坑取石或取砂；规模与目的不同于研究性发掘。

entries.definition: Bringing a buried thing to light; it stresses the find rather than the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 指使埋藏物见光；强调发现，而非整个过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin pieces, the engineering-first history and the layer-by-layer method.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁成分、工程义在先的历史，以及逐层发掘的方法。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + cavare 'hollow': to hollow out the ground.
normal.cn: ex-「出」+ cavare「挖空」：把地面挖空。

normal.en: The family runs excavate, excavation, excavator, cavity, cave.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 excavate、excavation、excavator、cavity、cave。

normal.en: Engineering came first in English; archaeology borrowed the word later.
normal.cn: 英语中工程义在先；考古学后来借用了这个词。

normal.en: A modern dig records each layer before removing it.
normal.cn: 现代发掘在移除每一层之前先记录。

normal.en: Typical partners are archaeological, rescue, site and work.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是「考古的」「抢救性的」「现场」与「工程」。

abstract.en: Picture a hole that is also a notebook: every spadeful is written down.
abstract.cn: 想象一个坑同时也是一本笔记：每一铲都被记下。

abstract.en: Picture layers of paint removed from a wall until an older image appears.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上的层层颜料被去掉，直到旧画显现。

abstract.en: Picture a secret buried in paper rather than soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一个秘密埋在纸里，而不是土里。

examples.en: The excavation was halted when the water table rose.
examples.cn: 当地下水位上升时，发掘被停止。

examples.en: Every excavation destroys what it does not record.
examples.cn: 每一次发掘都会毁掉它未记录的东西。

examples.en: The road excavation exposed three old foundations.
examples.cn: 道路开挖露出了三处旧地基。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）+ cav（洞）+ ation」——把洞挖出来 → 发掘；开挖

root: 拉丁 excavatio，来自 excavare「挖空」= ex-（出）+ cavare（使空），cavare 源于 cavus「空的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one hollow: earth is removed. The hollow becomes a process, a place, a set of finds, an engineering cut, a method, a lasting hole, a metaphor for inquiry and finally any uncovering by removal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个空洞展开：土被移走。这个空洞先成为过程，再成为地点、一组出土物、工程切口、方法、留下的坑、调查的比喻，最后成为任何「移除以显现」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stepped pit narrowing downward, tags on the walls, a stone floor at the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：逐层收窄的阶梯探坑，坑壁插着标签，坑底露出石地面。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE PLACE: the hollow is both work and workplace.
branches.cn: 行为与地点：空洞既是工作，也是工作场所。

branches.en: THE YIELD AND THE HOLE: what comes out and what remains are two ends of one act.
branches.cn: 收获与坑：取出之物与留下之物是同一行为的两端。

branches.en: ENGINEERING AND METHOD: moving soil becomes a science when records matter.
branches.cn: 工程与方法：当记录变得重要，搬土就成为科学。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: secrecy is soil, and inquiry is the spade.
branches.cn: 比喻：秘密是土，调查是铲。

branches.en: REVELATION BY REMOVAL: the deepest sense covers earth, paper and silence alike.
branches.cn: 移除以显现：最深的一层同时涵盖泥土、纸张与沉默。

intro.en: Excavation is a Latin verb plus an action suffix; the root cavus also builds words for hollow spaces.
intro.cn: excavation 是拉丁动词加行为后缀；词根 cavus 也构成表示空腔的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cavus and cavare give cavity, cave, excavate and excavation; ex- adds the direction outward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cavus 与 cavare 衍生 cavity、cave、excavate 与 excavation；ex- 增添向外的方向。

items.example: The prefix marks removal outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出向外的移走。

items.example: The adjective describes the space made.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述被造出的空间。

items.example: The verb turns emptiness into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把「空」变成动作。

items.example: The Latin verb covered both engineering and burial.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词兼指工程与埋藏。

items.example: Excavation names the process and its result.
items.exampleCN: excavation 兼指过程与结果。

items.example: They excavated the floor to the bedrock.
items.exampleCN: 他们把地面挖到基岩。

items.structure: excavate + -or (one who or that which acts)
items.example: The excavator lifted a bucket of clay.
items.exampleCN: 挖掘机提起一斗黏土。

items.example: The cavity in the tooth was filled.
items.exampleCN: 牙上的洞被补好。

items.example: The cave kept a constant temperature.
items.exampleCN: 洞穴保持恒温。

latinEntries.structure: cavus, cava, cavum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: 使成为奴隶；束缚；使沉迷
definition_en: to make someone a slave, or to keep someone under a force that controls their life
core_image: 铁链扣住手腕，把人从自由的人变成他人手中的财产
scene: 史料记载，沿海村落整批居民被船队运走贩卖。 Ship captains enslaved coastal communities for profit.
sceneCN: 这里 enslave 是「使成为奴隶」（第 1 个义项：夺走自由并视为财产）；句意：船长们为牟利而奴役沿岸居民。

pos.zh: 奴役；束缚；使沉迷

senses.title: To make a person the property of another
senses.definition: to take away someone's freedom and treat that person as owned property
senses.definitionCN: 夺走某人的自由并将其视为财产
senses.example: Colonial powers enslaved millions of people.
senses.exampleCN: 殖民势力奴役了数以百万计的人。
senses.why: The prefix en- puts someone into a state, and the state named here is the one slave denotes.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 en- 表示把人置于某种状态，这里就是 slave 所指的状态。

senses.title: To keep someone under a controlling force
senses.definition: to prevent someone from choosing freely because a powerful influence holds them
senses.definitionCN: 因强大力量掌控某人，使其无法自主选择
senses.example: Debt enslaved the small factory owner.
senses.exampleCN: 债务束缚了这家小厂的主人。
senses.why: Figuratively the chain need not be iron: any force that removes real choice can enslave.
senses.whyCN: 引申而言锁链未必是铁的：任何剥夺真实选择权的力量都能构成奴役。

senses.title: To give yourself so completely that a thing rules you
senses.definition: to devote so much time and will to something that it controls your life
senses.definitionCN: 把时间与意志过多交给某事物，以至于被它统治
senses.example: Ambition enslaved the novelist in his final years.
senses.exampleCN: 野心在小说家晚年把他牢牢困住。
senses.why: Applied to feelings and goals, the verb warns that a thing you love can become a master.
senses.whyCN: 用于情感与目标时，这个动词警示：你所爱之物也可能变成主人。

intro.en: Slave reached English through French and German from the name of a people, and en- later built a verb on it.
intro.cn: slave 经法语与德语进入英语，源自一个民族的族名；后来英语用 en- 由它造出动词。

items.en: Slověnin meant a Slav, many of whom were captured in early medieval wars.
items.cn: Slověnin 指斯拉夫人，早期中世纪战争中许多人被俘。

items.en: Sclave came to mean a person bought as a servant.
items.cn: Sclave 转指被买来服役的人。

items.en: Esclave carries the word into French and then into England.
items.cn: esclave 把该词带入法语，随后传入英国。

items.en: Sawle appears in English records of the trade.
items.cn: 中古英语出现 sawle，用于贸易记录。

items.en: Enslave is attested with the literal sense of owning persons.
items.cn: 近古英语中 enslave 有使人沦为奴隶的确证。

items.en: The figurative sense of being ruled by debt or habit becomes common.
items.cn: 现代英语中，被债务或习惯支配的比喻义变得常用。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same noun; group two holds other verbs of taking freedom.
note.cn: 第一组是同一名词派生的词；第二组是其他剥夺自由的动词。

entries.definition: The noun that supplies the meaning; the prefix only turns it into an action.
entries.definitionCN: 提供核心义的名词；前缀只把它变成动作。

entries.definition: The condition or the historical process named as a fact rather than an act.
entries.definitionCN: 作为事实或过程来表述的状态。

entries.definition: The person who performs the act, preferred in modern historical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 施动者，现代史学写作更倾向使用。

entries.definition: Sounds close but means to settle comfortably, with no link to bondage.
entries.definitionCN: 读音相近，实指安顿舒适，与奴役无关。

entries.definition: To catch in a snare; the loss is of freedom of movement rather than of personhood.
entries.definitionCN: 陷入罗网，失去的是行动自由而非人格。

entries.definition: Historically to hold in thrall; now often means to captivate delightfully.
entries.definitionCN: 史指处于束缚，今常指令人着迷。

entries.definition: To bring a people under rule, closer to political control than to ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 使一个民族臣服，更近政治统治而非所有权。

entries.definition: The condition itself rather than the act of imposing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指处境本身，而非施加该处境的行为。

normalIntro.en: Enslave is en plus slave, so the verb literally means to put someone into slavery.
normalIntro.cn: enslave 是 en 加 slave，因此字面义是把人置于奴役状态。

normal.en: Read it as make a slave of, and the grammar follows at once.
normal.cn: 读作「使成为奴隶」，语法随即清楚。

normal.en: Passive voice is common: enslaved by debt, enslaved by habit.
normal.cn: 被动式常见：被债务奴役、被习惯奴役。

normal.en: Historical writing now prefers enslaver over slave owner for the buyer side.
normal.cn: 史学写作现更倾向用 enslaver 取代 slave owner。

normal.en: The figurative use keeps the violence of the literal one, so it is strong words.
normal.cn: 比喻用法保留本义的暴力色彩，因此语气很重。

normal.en: Pair with a people, a workforce, or a self, the three usual objects.
normal.cn: 常见宾语是民族、劳工群体或自身。

abstract.en: Picture an iron ring closing around an ankle.
abstract.cn: 想象铁环在脚踝上扣紧。

abstract.en: Imagine a ledger of bills that decides every meal a family eats.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠账单决定一家人每餐吃什么。

abstract.en: Think of a desk lamp burning at dawn while the writer has not slept.
abstract.cn: 想想天未亮书桌灯仍亮着，而作者一夜未眠。

examples.en: Millions were enslaved and transported across the ocean.
examples.cn: 数以百万计的人被奴役并运过大洋。

examples.en: He felt enslaved by his own obligations.
examples.cn: 他觉得自己被责任束缚住了。

examples.en: Addiction can enslave even the wealthy.
examples.cn: 成瘾甚至能让富人也沦为俘虏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因死累屋」——因为死累而困在屋里出不去，所以 enslave 是奴役；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 斯拉夫语 Slověnin（斯拉夫人）→ 中古高地德语 Sclave → 古法语 esclave → 中古英语 slave＋前缀 en-（使进入）→ 现代英语 enslave，核心义「使人沦为奴隶」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb moves from owning persons, to being controlled by forces such as debt, to being ruled by one's own passions.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从占有他人，到被债务之类力量控制，再到被自身欲望支配。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain fastened to someone who did not choose it.
core.cn: 核心意象：锁链扣在一个并未同意的人身上。

branches.en: Physical ownership is the historical base sense.
branches.cn: 人身占有是对应的历史义项。

branches.en: Economic pressure supplies a modern figurative chain.
branches.cn: 经济压力提供了现代的比喻锁链。

branches.en: Inner compulsion turns the self into both captive and captor.
branches.cn: 内在强迫使自我同时成为囚徒与看守。

branches.en: Both senses remove the possibility of refusal.
branches.cn: 两个义项都剥夺拒绝的可能。

branches.en: Debt and passion alike can dictate a whole life.
branches.cn: 债务与欲望都能支配人的一生。

intro.en: A productive English prefix is attached to a borrowed noun, and the family grows with English endings.
intro.cn: 英语能产前缀加在借入名词上，词族由英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin sclavus and dux are the written forms behind the word for a Slav and for a leader.
latinIntro.cn: 中古拉丁语 sclavus 与 dux 分别是斯拉夫人与首领的书面形式。

items.example: En- builds enslave from slave.
items.exampleCN: en- 由 slave 造出 enslave。

items.example: Slave is the base.
items.exampleCN: slave 是词基。

items.meaning: a Slav, later a bonded person
items.meaningCN: 斯拉夫人，后指被束缚者
items.example: Sclavus is the written Latin form.
items.exampleCN: sclavus 是对应的拉丁书写形式。

items.example: The ending forms enslavement.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成 enslavement。

items.example: The ending forms enslaver.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成 enslaver。

items.example: Dis- gives the rare verb disenslave.
items.exampleCN: dis- 构成罕见动词 disenslave。

items.example: Compare the cousin verb enthral.
items.exampleCN: 对比同族动词 enthral。

items.example: Serf names a related condition.
items.exampleCN: serf 指相关的一种处境。

items.example: Vassal sits between free and enslaved.
items.exampleCN: vassal 介于自由与奴役之间。

definition_zh: 真实性；可靠性；真品性；正宗性；本真；真诚；权威性（古义）；原真性；认证有效性
definition_en: the quality of being true, trustworthy, or genuinely from the source claimed, whether in a statement, an object, a place, or a person
core_image: 一枚旧印章压在纸上：纸会旧、字会淡，但印痕仍证明它出自该出的人之手
scene: 展灯下，策展人俯身灯前，对观众缓缓说道。 A curator under a lamp says: People ask about authenticity, but what they really want is a reason to believe the story.
sceneCN: 这里 authenticity 指「真实性、真品性」（第 1 个义项、第 3 个义项：内容与事实相符、物件非伪造）；句意：人们问的是真伪，其实想要的是一个相信这个故事的理由。画面里有放大镜、旧画框和一枚印章。

pos.zh: 真实性；可靠性；真品性；正宗性；本真

senses.title: True to the facts
senses.definition: the quality of being true to the facts, not invented or false
senses.definitionCN: 与事实相符、并非编造或虚假的性质
senses.example: Historians questioned the authenticity of the diary's later pages.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家质疑这本日记后几页的真实性。
senses.why: -ity makes an abstract noun of authentic, whose Greek source authentikos came from authentes 'one who acts on his own authority'. Truth here is imagined as a warrant held by the person who was actually there.
senses.whyCN: -ity 把 authentic 变成抽象名词；其希腊语来源 authentikos 出自 authentes「凭自己权威行事的人」。这里的「真」被想象成当事人手里握着的一份凭证。

senses.title: Worthy of belief
senses.definition: the quality of deserving belief or trust
senses.definitionCN: 值得相信或信赖的性质
senses.example: The witness's authenticity was never in doubt.
senses.exampleCN: 这名证人的可靠性从未受到怀疑。
senses.why: Authentic meant 'authoritative, duly authorized' in mid-14th-century English before it meant 'factual'. The credibility sense still carries that residue: a claim is believed because its source is entitled to speak.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪中叶的英语里，authentic 先指「有权威、经正式授权的」，后来才指「符合事实」。可信义仍带着这层残余：一个说法被相信，是因为它的来源有权说话。

senses.title: The original object
senses.definition: the quality of being the original object, not a copy or forgery
senses.definitionCN: 是原件而非复制品或伪造品的性质
senses.example: Experts spent months confirming the authenticity of the painting.
senses.exampleCN: 专家花了几个月确认这幅画的真伪。
senses.why: Medieval Latin authenticus named a document with legal force; a sealed original proved itself. Applied to objects, the word asks whether this is the very thing, not a stand-in.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 authenticus 指具有法律效力的文件；盖了印的原件能自证。用到物品上，这个词问的是「是不是就是这一件」，而不是替身。

senses.title: Faithful to a place
senses.titleCN: 正宗性：照着当地原样做
senses.definition: the quality of following the original regional method or recipe
senses.definitionCN: 遵循原产地做法或配方的性质
senses.example: The restaurant's authenticity rests on its wood-fired oven and local flour.
senses.exampleCN: 这家餐厅的正宗性靠的是柴火烤炉和本地面粉。
senses.why: When a practice travels, 'original' becomes 'local and unchanged'. The noun then praises fidelity to a place's own way rather than to a document.
senses.whyCN: 一种做法流传出去后，「原初」就变成「当地且未改」。这个词于是称赞对某地自身做法的忠实，而不是对一份文件的忠实。

senses.title: The authentic self
senses.definition: the quality of living or acting in accordance with one's own character and values
senses.definitionCN: 按自己的性格与价值生活或行动的性质
senses.example: Her essays are valued for their emotional authenticity.
senses.exampleCN: 她的随笔因情感本真而受重视。
senses.why: Existential writers took 'acting on one's own authority' literally: an authentic person is one whose acts are their own, not borrowed. Authenticity becomes self-authorship.
senses.whyCN: 存在主义作家把「凭自己权威行事」按字面理解：本真的人，其行为出于自己，而非借来。authenticity 于是成了「自己写自己」。

senses.title: Unforced feeling
senses.definition: the quality of expressing feelings without pretence
senses.definitionCN: 不带伪装地表达情感的性质
senses.example: There was an authenticity in his apology that no polished speech could match.
senses.exampleCN: 他的道歉里有一种真诚，是任何漂亮辞令都比不上的。
senses.why: The social sense narrows the existential one: if the feeling comes from the self, it shows. Genuine and authentic overlap here, though genuine stresses origin and authentic stresses warrant.
senses.whyCN: 社交义把存在主义义收窄：若情感出自本人，就会显出来。这里 genuine 与 authentic 重叠，但 genuine 强调来源，authentic 强调凭证。

senses.title: Authoritative, in older use
senses.titleCN: 权威性：古义里的「正式有效」
senses.definition: the quality of being authoritative or formally valid, an older sense now rare
senses.definitionCN: 具有权威或正式效力的性质，此为现已罕见的旧义
senses.example: In medieval law, the authenticity of a charter lay in its seal, not in its story.
senses.exampleCN: 在中世纪法律里，一份特许状的有效性在于它的印章，而不在于它的叙述。
senses.why: The earliest English sense of authentic was 'authoritative, duly authorized', and the noun inherited it before 'factual' took over. The phrase 'of doubtful authenticity' still echoes that legal use.
senses.whyCN: authentic 最早的英语义是「有权威、经正式授权」，名词先继承了它，「符合事实」后来才占上风。短语 of doubtful authenticity 仍回响着那个法律用法。

senses.title: Fidelity to an original state
senses.titleCN: 原真性：复原到从前的样子
senses.definition: fidelity to an original state or style, as demanded in restoration or early music
senses.definitionCN: 忠于原状或原风格，如文物修复或早期音乐所要求的
senses.example: Early-music groups argue about authenticity in tempo and tuning.
senses.exampleCN: 早期音乐团体为速度和调音上的原真性争论不休。
senses.why: Restorers and period performers turned the question 'is it the original?' into a rule: reconstruct the object or performance as it once was. The noun names a standard of fidelity, not a physical fact.
senses.whyCN: 修复者和古乐演奏者把「这是不是原件」变成一条规则：把物件或演出复原成它曾经的样子。这个名词命名的是一种忠实标准，而非一件实物事实。

senses.title: Legally verified validity
senses.titleCN: 认证有效性：验过之后才算数
senses.definition: the legal validity of a signature, document, or record after it has been checked
senses.definitionCN: 签名、文件或记录经查验后具有的法律效力
senses.example: The notary checked the authenticity of the signature before the transfer.
senses.exampleCN: 公证人在过户前核查了签名的真实性。
senses.why: Forensic and legal usage keeps the oldest institutional sense: an instrument is authentic when it has been properly executed and can be proved so. Verification is the modern ritual of authorizing.
senses.whyCN: 法律与鉴定用法保留了最古老的制度义：文书经正式签署并能被证明，才算 authentic。查验就是现代版的「授权」仪式。

intro.en: Authenticity is a late abstract noun built on authentic, a word that began as a claim about authority, not about facts. Greek authentes was 'one who acts on his own authority'; -ity turned that warrant into a quality that can be questioned.
intro.cn: authenticity 是较晚出现的抽象名词，建立在 authentic 之上；而 authentic 最初讲的不是事实，而是权威。希腊语 authentes 指「凭自己权威行事的人」，-ity 把这份凭证变成一种可以被质疑的性质。

items.en: authentikos 'original, genuine, principal' came from authentes 'one acting on one's own authority', analysable as autos 'self' + hentes 'doer, being'. The deeper root of hentes, PIE *sene- (2) 'to accomplish', is reconstructed and marked source uncertain.
items.cn: authentikos「原初的、真正的、主要的」出自 authentes「凭自己权威行事的人」，可分析为 autos「自己」+ hentes「行事者、存在者」。hentes 更深的词根 PIE *sene- (2)「完成」是重构形式，标为「来源不确定」。

items.en: authenticus was the Latin form of the Greek adjective, used of documents and authorities. Legal force, not philosophical truth, was its first job in Western use.
items.cn: authenticus 是这个希腊形容词的拉丁形式，用于文件和权威。它在西方用法里的第一份工作是法律效力，而不是哲学真理。

items.en: autentique 'authentic; canonical' passed the word into English with its air of official approval and its missing -h-, which English later restored.
items.cn: 古法语 autentique「真正的；正典的」把这个词带进英语，带着官方认可的气息，也带着丢掉的 h；英语后来把这个 h 补了回去。

items.en: autentik is recorded as 'authoritative, duly authorized', and in the same period as 'real, entitled to acceptance as factual'. The two senses coexisted from the start.
items.cn: autentik 被记录为「有权威的、经正式授权的」，同一时期也指「真实的、可被接受为事实的」。两个义项从一开始就并存。

items.en: Earlier abstract nouns authentity (1650s) and authenticness (1620s) failed to settle. authenticity is recorded in 1760, formed from authentic + -ity, and that pattern won.
items.cn: 更早的抽象名词 authentity（17 世纪 50 年代）和 authenticness（17 世纪 20 年代）都没能站住。authenticity 记录于 1760 年，由 authentic + -ity 构成，这个模式最终胜出。

items.en: 'Genuine original' extended to art and objects, then to regional food and heritage, and in the 20th century to the self and to historically informed performance.
items.cn: 「真品原件」义扩展到艺术与物品，再扩展到地方饮食与文化遗产；20 世纪又扩展到「真实的自我」和「历史复原演奏」。

note.en: The first group shares the authent- stem or the -icity ending; the second group names qualities that answer the same question: can this be trusted as what it claims to be?
note.cn: 第一组共享 authent- 词干或 -icity 词尾；第二组是回答同一个问题的近义词：这东西能不能被信作它所声称的样子？

entries.definition: real, genuine, or reliable. Remove -ity and you have the adjective from which authenticity is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 真正的；地道的；可靠的。去掉 -ity 就是构成 authenticity 的形容词。

entries.definition: the process of proving something is genuine, especially a user's identity. It is an action noun, while authenticity is a quality noun.
entries.definitionCN: 认证；身份验证。它是动作名词，而 authenticity 是性质名词。

entries.definition: the quality of being false, imitative, or performed rather than genuine.
entries.definitionCN: 不真实；虚假；造作。

entries.definition: the creator of a work, from Latin auctor. It resembles authentic in sound but comes from a different family.
entries.definitionCN: 作者；创作者，出自拉丁语 auctor。它听起来像 authentic，但词族不同。

entries.definition: the quality of being real and not adulterated or imitated. It stresses origin, while authenticity stresses warranted truth.
entries.definitionCN: 真正；纯正；非伪造。它强调来源，authenticity 强调有凭证的真。

entries.definition: the quality of being based on sound reasoning or proper legal form. It covers the legal end of authenticity.
entries.definitionCN: 有效性；正当性。它覆盖 authenticity 的法律一端。

entries.definition: the quality of consistently working or being trustworthy. It matches the 'worthy of belief' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 可靠性；可信赖。对应 authenticity 的「值得相信」义。

entries.definition: the quality of being convincing enough to be believed. It is about the audience's trust rather than the object's origin.
entries.definitionCN: 可信度；公信力。它讲的是受众的信任，而非物品的来源。

entries.definition: the quality of being the first of its kind, or of coming from the maker's own mind. It overlaps with authenticity in art.
entries.definitionCN: 原创性；独创性。在艺术语境与 authenticity 重叠。

normalIntro.en: The stem authent- carries 'one who acts on his own authority'; -ity is the suffix that turns any adjective of quality into a noun of quality.
normalIntro.cn: 词干 authent- 带着「凭自己权威行事者」的意思；-ity 则是把性质形容词变成性质名词的后缀。

normal.en: authentic + -ity: add the abstract-noun suffix and the adjective becomes the thing people argue about.
normal.cn: authentic + -ity：加上抽象名词后缀，形容词就变成了人们争论的那个「真不真」。

normal.en: Same ending as reality and validity: -ity words name a quality that can be measured or challenged.
normal.cn: 和 reality、validity 同样的词尾：-ity 名词命名的是一种可被衡量、可被质疑的性质。

normal.en: A signature checked by a notary is authenticity in its oldest clothes: a seal that authorizes.
normal.cn: 公证人核对的签名，是 authenticity 最古老的样子：一枚授权的印章。

normal.en: authentic food, authentic self, authentic document: one word, three questions about origin.
normal.cn: 地道的食物、真实的自我、真迹文件：同一个词，问了三个关于来源的问题。

normal.en: The -th- in the middle is the Greek theta's footprint; the French form dropped it and English put it back.
normal.cn: 中间的 -th- 是希腊字母 theta 留下的脚印；法语形式丢了它，英语又补了回来。

abstract.en: Authenticity is not a fact but a claim: it asks who is entitled to say this is so.
abstract.cn: authenticity 不是事实，而是一项主张：它问的是谁有权说「就是这样」。

abstract.en: The same word covers a sealed charter, a village recipe and a person's inner life: authority has moved inward.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖盖印的特许状、乡村食谱和一个人的内心：权威从外部移到了内部。

abstract.en: Every verification is a small ritual: the object does not change, only our warrant for believing it.
abstract.cn: 每一次验证都是一场小仪式：物件没有变，变的只是我们相信它的凭证。

examples.en: The lab uses isotope tests to establish the authenticity of the ivory.
examples.cn: 实验室用同位素检测来确定这批象牙的真伪。

examples.en: Tourists often mistake performance for authenticity.
examples.cn: 游客常把表演当成了真实。

examples.en: She writes with an authenticity that comes from refusing easy answers.
examples.cn: 她的写作有一种真诚，来自拒绝轻易的答案。

dict_mnemonic.text: authentic（真货）+ ity（一贴）——给真货贴上一张证明，贴上「真」的标签 → authenticity 真实性；真品性

root: 源自希腊语 authentikos「原初的、真正的」← authentes「凭自己权威行事者」（autos「自己」+ hentes「行事者」），经拉丁语 authenticus、古法语 autentique 进入英语；authenticity = authentic + -ity，把「有凭证的真」抽象成性质。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses circle one question: does this come from the source it claims? The answer may rest on facts, on a seal, on a recipe, on a period score, or on a person's own life.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围着同一个问题转：它是否出自它所声称的来源？答案可能落在事实上、印章上、食谱上、古乐谱上，也可能落在一个人的自身生活上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seal that proves the thing came from the hand it names.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚印章，证明这东西出自它所署的那只手。

chain: A SOURCE THAT SPEAKS FOR ITSELF

branches.en: TRUTH AND TRUST: a statement that matches the facts, and a source that deserves belief.
branches.cn: 真与信：与事实相符的陈述，以及值得相信的来源。

branches.en: THE ORIGINAL AND THE PROVEN: the very object, not a copy, and the legal validation of a signature.
branches.cn: 原件与验证：就是那一件而非复制品，以及签名的法律确认。

branches.en: FIDELITY TO A PLACE OR A TIME: the local recipe, and the restored period performance.
branches.cn: 对地点或时代的忠实：地方食谱，以及复原的历史演出。

branches.en: THE INNER SOURCE: a self that acts on its own authority, and a feeling that does not perform.
branches.cn: 内在来源：凭自己权威行动的自我，以及不表演的情感。

branches.en: THE OLD WARRANT: authority and formal validity, before truth became the main question.
branches.cn: 古老的凭证：在「真」成为主要问题之前，权威与正式效力。

intro.en: authenticity is authent- (Greek authentes, 'one acting on his own authority') + -ic (adjective) + -ity (quality noun). The family runs authenticate, authentication, inauthentic and inauthenticity; author is a look-alike, not a relative.
intro.cn: authenticity 是 authent-（希腊语 authentes「凭自己权威行事者」）+ -ic（形容词）+ -ity（性质名词）。词族有 authenticate、authentication、inauthentic、inauthenticity；author 只是形近，并非同族。

latinIntro.en: Greek authentikos became Latin authenticus; the verb authenticare produced authentication. Latin -itas (stem -itat-) is the source of English -ity.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 authentikos 变成拉丁语 authenticus；动词 authenticare 产生 authentication。拉丁语 -itas（词干 -itat-）是英语 -ity 的来源。

items.meaning: the quality of being genuine or trustworthy
items.example: The authenticity of the manuscript was never seriously challenged.
items.exampleCN: 这份手稿的真实性从未受到严肃质疑。

items.example: The shop sells authentic Basque linen.
items.exampleCN: 这家店出售正宗的巴斯克亚麻布。

items.meaning: in a genuine or original way
items.example: The room is authentically furnished for the period.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间按那个时代的原样布置。

items.meaning: to prove that something is genuine
items.example: Two experts authenticated the drawing.
items.exampleCN: 两位专家鉴定了这幅素描为真迹。

items.meaning: the act of proving genuineness or identity
items.example: Two-factor authentication protects the account.
items.exampleCN: 双重认证保护这个账户。

items.meaning: a person or device that verifies
items.example: The app serves as an authenticator.
items.exampleCN: 这个应用充当认证器。

items.example: The accent sounded inauthentic to local ears.
items.exampleCN: 在本地人听来，那口音不地道。

items.meaning: the quality of being false or performed
items.example: Viewers sensed the inauthenticity of the speech.
items.exampleCN: 观众感觉到了那篇演讲的造作。

items.example: The 1620s preferred authenticness to authenticity.
items.exampleCN: 17 世纪 20 年代的人更爱用 authenticness 而非 authenticity。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 真正的；原初的；有权威的

latinEntries.meaning: originator, creator; not the source of authentic
latinEntries.meaningCN: 创始者；作者（并非 authentic 的来源）

definition_zh: 加密；把明文转换成只有持钥匙者才能读懂的密文
definition_en: to convert readable information into a coded form that only the key holder can read
core_image: 一个人把摊开的信纸一行行卷进一只带锁的圆筒，纸上原本的字迹在筒口消失
scene: 值班员把摊在桌上的文件一行行扫进带锁的圆筒，筒口之外只剩乱码。 The clerk used a short passphrase to encrypt every report before it left the office.
sceneCN: 这里 encrypt 指把明文转成密文的动作（第 1 个义项：对文本执行加密）；句意：职员用一句简短口令把每份报告都加密后才送出办公室。

pos.zh: 加密；把……编成密码

senses.title: To turn text into code
senses.definition: to apply a fixed transformation that makes a message unreadable without the key
senses.definitionCN: 用固定变换让消息在没有钥匙时无法读懂
senses.example: They encrypt the draft before it crosses the network.
senses.exampleCN: 文件还在网络里穿行之前，他们就把它加密了。
senses.why: the verb is the direct action of the noun encryption; the object is whatever text is being changed.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词就是名词 encryption 所指动作本身，宾语是被改变的任何文本。

senses.title: To hide a message from eavesdroppers
senses.definition: to scramble a message so that an intercepting party gains nothing
senses.definitionCN: 把消息打乱，使截获的一方什么也得不到
senses.example: A courier who cannot read the packet is the point of encrypting it.
senses.exampleCN: 让送信人读不懂包裹，正是加密它的目的。
senses.why: the purpose of the action is built into the verb, so the verb is used even when the method is left unstated.
senses.whyCN: 动作的目的已含在动词里，因此即使不说方法，人们也直接用这个动词。

senses.title: To protect stored files
senses.definition: to encode files or a whole disk so that physical theft does not expose them
senses.definitionCN: 对文件或整块磁盘编码，使实物被盗也不会泄露内容
senses.example: The team encrypts laptops before handing them to field staff.
senses.exampleCN: 团队先给笔记本加密，再交给外勤人员。
senses.why: the same verb covers any data that must stay unreadable, whether it moves or rests.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词涵盖一切必须保持不可读的数据，无论它在传输还是静止。

senses.title: To secure a channel
senses.definition: to apply coding to traffic between two machines or two people
senses.definitionCN: 对两台机器或两个人之间的流量施加编码
senses.example: The browser encrypts the session as soon as the handshake ends.
senses.exampleCN: 握手一结束，浏览器就对这次会话加密。
senses.why: a connection is protected by protecting what runs through it, so the verb takes a channel as its object.
senses.whyCN: 保护连接就是保护在其中流动的内容，因此动词可以接「通道」作宾语。

senses.title: To write in historical cipher
senses.definition: to write by hand with a substitution or transposition of letters
senses.definitionCN: 用手工替换或换位字母的方式书写
senses.example: The envoys encrypted their dispatches with a shifting alphabet.
senses.exampleCN: 使节们用一种移动字母表加密公文。
senses.why: the verb inherits the centuries-old craft before it inherits the machine.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词先继承了数百年历史的手艺，之后才继承机器。

senses.title: To put a file in a sealed envelope
senses.definition: to make one particular item readable only to its intended receiver
senses.definitionCN: 使某一份内容只对指定接收者可读
senses.example: She encrypts the attachment to a single colleague.
senses.exampleCN: 她把附件加密，只允许一位同事打开。
senses.why: public-key methods let one item be sealed for one reader, and the old verb covers that everyday act.
senses.whyCN: 公钥方法能让一份内容只对一个读者封存，旧动词便用来指这个日常动作。

senses.title: To meet a legal duty
senses.definition: to render personal or business data unreadable as a rule or regulation requires
senses.definitionCN: 按规则或法规要求把个人或业务数据变得不可读
senses.example: Clinics must encrypt records they keep beyond the visit.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所必须对就诊后仍保存的记录进行加密。
senses.why: when a law names an action, the verb of that action becomes a duty and gains a fixed administrative use.
senses.whyCN: 当法规点名某个动作，这个动作的动词就成了义务，并获得固定的行政用法。

senses.title: To make speech needlessly obscure
senses.definition: to express something in language so indirect that it works like a code
senses.definitionCN: 用极其间接的语言表达，效果如同密码
senses.example: He encrypted a simple refusal inside three paragraphs of praise.
senses.exampleCN: 他把一句简单的拒绝藏进三段赞美之中。
senses.why: unreadable-by-design writing is the shared image, so the verb stretches from ciphers to evasive prose.
senses.whyCN: 「故意写得读不懂」是共同意象，于是动词从密码延伸到躲闪的文风。

intro.en: Encrypt is a modern English verb made by adding the prefix en- to the Greek root kryptos, hidden. It borrowed the shape of older French verbs but the meaning of a technical craft.
intro.cn: encrypt 是近代英语动词，在希腊词根 kryptos「隐藏」前加 en- 构成。它借用了古法语动词的形式，装进去的却是技术手艺的含义。

items.en: Greek kryptos, hidden, came from kryptein, to hide. The root named anything covered or kept out of sight.
items.cn: 希腊语 kryptos「隐藏的」来自 kryptein「隐藏」。这个词根指任何被遮盖、被藏起来的东西。

items.en: Latin took crypta for a covered vault and used it for underground chambers, giving English the place word crypt.
items.cn: 拉丁语以 crypta 指有顶的拱室，多用于地下空间，并给英语留下了表示地窖的 crypt。

items.en: Verbs beginning with en- were common in French, and English built new ones on that pattern rather than borrowing this verb whole.
items.cn: 法语中以 en- 开头的动词很常见，英语是按这个模式自造新词，而不是整体借入这个动词。

items.en: The verb pairs en-, into, with the hidden root, so it says to put something into hiding. It is recorded in English only in the modern period.
items.cn: 这个动词把 en-「进入」与「隐藏」词根配在一起，意思是把某物放进隐藏状态。它在英语中的记载只见于近代。

items.en: Military signalling gave the verb its technical sense, and computing made it an everyday word for protecting files and traffic.
items.cn: 军事通信给了它技术含义，计算机则让它成为保护文件与流量的日常词。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper pre-Greek origin of kryptein is not settled; compared forms are reconstructions, so no single ancestral root is claimed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：kryptein 在希腊语之前更早的来源没有定论，被比较的形式属于重构形式，因此不主张单一祖根。

note.en: The first group is the same hidden-root in its other parts of speech; the second group is the neighbouring technical actions.
note.cn: 第一组是「隐藏」词根的其他词性形式；第二组是相邻的技术动作。

entries.definition: The process or the result; the verb names what a person does, the noun names what is done.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程或结果；动词说人做了什么，名词说被做成了什么。

entries.definition: To turn the code back into readable text; it names the journey home, not the outward trip.
entries.definitionCN: 把代码还原成可读文本；它指回程，而不是去程。

entries.definition: The state of having been put into code, as in an encrypted disk.
entries.definitionCN: 指已经处于编码状态，如「已加密的磁盘」。

entries.definition: Puzzling by intention; no key is involved, only a manner of speaking.
entries.definitionCN: 指故意让人费解；不涉及密钥，只是一种说话方式。

entries.definition: To change form so that a system can store or send it; nothing is hidden, and anyone with the rule can read it.
entries.definitionCN: 改变形式以便系统存储或发送；并不隐藏，懂规则的人都能读。

entries.definition: To mix something so its order is lost; it describes the visible effect, while encrypt names the deliberate method.
entries.definitionCN: 把内容打乱到失去顺序；它描述可见的效果，encrypt 则指有意采用的方法。

entries.definition: A system of symbol substitution; one ciphers a message by applying a cipher to it.
entries.definitionCN: 符号替换的体系；人们把密码体系施于消息，从而加密消息。

entries.definition: To keep something from being seen or known; the everyday word behind the technical one.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物不被看见或知道；是技术词背后那个日常说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations built on the real pieces and the real verb family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想，建立在真实构件与真实动词词族之上。

normal.en: en- means into, kryptos means hidden: to encrypt is to put into hiding.
normal.cn: en- 表示「进入」，kryptos 表示「隐藏」：encrypt 就是把东西放进隐藏状态。

normal.en: The four verb forms are regular: encrypts, encrypted, encrypted, encrypting.
normal.cn: 四个动词形式都规则：encrypts、encrypted、encrypted、encrypting。

normal.en: Objects tell the story: encrypt a file, a message, traffic, a disk.
normal.cn: 看宾语就知道用法：加密文件、消息、流量、磁盘。

normal.en: Pair it with its reverse: encrypt on the way out, decrypt on the way back.
normal.cn: 与反义词成对记：出去时 encrypt，回来时 decrypt。

normal.en: The preposition is with: encrypt with a key, never encrypt by a key.
normal.cn: 介词用 with：encrypt with a key，而不是 encrypt by a key。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing a written page into a cylinder and the page coming out as gravel.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把写满字的纸推进圆筒，出来的却是一把碎石。

abstract.en: Picture a lock that changes its own shape every time the key turns.
abstract.cn: 想象一把锁，每次钥匙转动，锁孔就自己换一个形状。

abstract.en: Picture a whisper that only one ear in a crowded hall can decode.
abstract.cn: 想象满厅人群里的一句低语，只有一只耳朵能解出来。

examples.en: Banks encrypt customer records as a matter of routine.
examples.cn: 银行把加密客户记录当作日常操作。

examples.en: The app encrypts each photo before uploading it.
examples.cn: 这款应用在上传前会把每张照片加密。

examples.en: You can encrypt the whole drive without slowing daily work much.
examples.cn: 你可以加密整个硬盘，而不太影响日常使用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因（en）刻入（crypt）」——把内容刻进去藏起来，就是加密

root: 希腊 kryptos「隐藏的」← kryptein「隐藏」→ 拉丁 crypta「拱室」→ 英语 crypt；英语以 en-「进入」+ 该词根构成动词 encrypt，近代才见于记载。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the plain technical act to its protective purposes, then to the old craft, the sealed item, the legal duty and the evasive style.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从单纯的技术动作出发，走向各种保护目的，再到古老手艺、封存单品、法律义务与躲闪文风。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a written page rolled into a locked cylinder, its letters vanishing at the mouth.
core.cn: 核心意象：写满字的纸被卷进带锁的圆筒，字迹在筒口消失。

branches.en: MAKING UNREADABLE: the plain act, and the figurative act of writing prose that hides its meaning.
branches.cn: 使之不可读：既指本义动作，也指把文章写得意在藏意的比喻用法。

branches.en: KEEPING FROM A READER: hiding a message from eavesdroppers, or sealing one item for one receiver.
branches.cn: 对读者设限：既让窃听者读不到，也为单一接收者封存一份内容。

branches.en: DATA AT REST: files and disks encoded so that theft of the object yields nothing.
branches.cn: 静态数据：文件与磁盘被编码，实物被盗也得不到内容。

branches.en: DATA IN MOTION: the same action applied to a live connection or session.
branches.cn: 传输数据：同一动作施于正在运行的连接或会话。

branches.en: OLD CRAFT AND NEW DUTY: hand ciphers on one side, a regulated obligation on the other.
branches.cn: 旧手艺与新义务：一边是手工密码，一边是被规章规定的义务。

intro.en: Encrypt is a prefix plus a Greek root with no Latin element in its core; the surrounding forms add English and Latin endings.
intro.cn: encrypt 是一个前缀加一个希腊词根，核心部分没有拉丁成分；周边形式再加英语与拉丁词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributes the prefix shape in- behind English en- and the noun ending -tion used by encryption; the root itself is Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了英语 en- 背后的 in- 前缀形式，以及 encryption 所用的名词词尾 -tion；词根本身来自希腊语。

items.example: It moves the root from a state to an action.
items.exampleCN: 它把词根从状态变成动作。

items.example: The Latin prefix is the older shape behind English en-.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁前缀是英语 en- 背后的更早形式。

items.example: The adjective gives the family its core meaning.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词给整个词族提供核心含义。

items.example: The verb names the original act of covering.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指最初的遮盖动作。

items.example: An encrypted file is one that has been through the process.
items.exampleCN: 已加密的文件就是走完了流程的文件。

items.example: Encrypting is the work, not the finished state.
items.exampleCN: encrypting 指工作过程，不是完成状态。

items.example: The ending turns the verb into the name of a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成过程之名。

items.example: The prefix marks the journey back out of code.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记从代码里出来的回程。

items.example: The two endings together describe a sealed item.
items.exampleCN: 两个词尾合起来描述一件已封存的内容。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 有顶的拱室、隐蔽的空间

definition_zh: 幼稚的；孩子气的；愚蠢可笑的；（医学）儿童期特有的
definition_en: childish in a way that a grown person should have outgrown, or, of a physical sign, normal in a child and alarming in an adult
core_image: 两个穿西装的人在正式场合互相起外号
scene: 两个成年人在会上互相起外号，谁都不肯先停。 Two grown men traded nicknames across the table, a puerile contest that outlasted the agenda.
sceneCN: 这里 puerile 指幼稚得可笑（第 1 个义项：成年人的幼稚）；句意为两个成年人在会上互相起外号，谁也不肯先停，这场幼稚的较劲比议程还长。

pos.zh: 幼稚的；孩子气的；愚蠢可笑的；（医学）儿童期特有的

senses.title: Childish in an adult
senses.definition: of an adult, behaving, speaking or choosing with the silliness that a child should have left behind
senses.definitionCN: 形容成年人在行为、言语或选择上带着本该丢下的孩子气
senses.example: Two grown men traded nicknames across the table, a puerile contest that outlasted the agenda.
senses.exampleCN: 两个成年人在会上互相起外号，这场幼稚的较劲比议程还长。
senses.why: The word judges the age of the actor before it judges the act.
senses.whyCN: 这个词评判的是行为者的年龄，不只是行为本身。

senses.title: Puerile breathing
senses.definition: used clinically of a physical sign that is normal in a child and abnormal if it persists in an adult
senses.definitionCN: 临床上指某种体征在儿童身上正常、成人仍有则为异常
senses.example: The physician noted puerile breathing, which in an adult patient is a warning.
senses.exampleCN: 医生记下了儿童型呼吸音，这在成年病人身上是一个警示。
senses.why: No sneer survives here: the word simply places the sign inside childhood.
senses.whyCN: 这里没有一丝嘲讽：这个词只是把这种体征归入童年。

intro.en: Puerile is simply 'boyish' in Latin: puer was the word for a boy, and the adjective kept the schoolyard in it.
intro.cn: puerile 在拉丁语里就是「男孩的」：puer 是男孩，这个形容词把校园操场留在了词里。

items.en: Puer meant 'boy or child', and it also named a young servant.
items.cn: puer 意为「男孩、孩子」，也用来称年轻的仆役。

items.en: Puerilis meant 'of a boy, boyish', a plain adjective without any insult.
items.cn: puerilis 意为「男孩的、孩子气的」，本来只是个不带侮辱的形容词。

items.en: English borrowed puerile for things proper to childhood.
items.cn: 英语借入 puerile，指属于童年的事物。

items.en: Doctors used puerile for breathing sounds that are normal in children.
items.cn: 医生用 puerile 指儿童身上正常的呼吸音。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the adjective was chiefly a criticism of adults.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个形容词主要是对成年人的批评。

note.en: The look-alike group is the puer family; the near-meaning group separates childish, infantile, juvenile and immature.
note.cn: 形近组是 puer 词族；近义组把「孩子气的」「婴儿般的」「少年式的」与「不成熟的」分开。

entries.definition: childishness in an adult.
entries.definitionCN: 成年人的幼稚。

entries.definition: in a childish way.
entries.definitionCN: 以幼稚的方式。

entries.definition: a reversion to childish behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 退回儿童行为的现象。

entries.definition: relating to childbirth.
entries.definitionCN: 与分娩有关的。

entries.definition: silly in the way a child can be.
entries.definitionCN: 以孩子的方式显得傻气的。

entries.definition: babyish, or extremely immature.
entries.definitionCN: 婴儿般的，或极不成熟的。

entries.definition: youthful, often disapprovingly.
entries.definitionCN: 少年的，常带不赞许。

entries.definition: not yet fully developed.
entries.definitionCN: 尚未充分发展的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of two men in suits trading playground names.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「两个穿西装的人在互起操场上那种外号」的画面。

normal.en: Puerile holds puer, Latin for boy: the word is boyishness in a grown body.
normal.cn: puerile 里藏着 puer（拉丁语的男孩）：这个词是装在成人身体里的孩子气。

normal.en: Think of a boardroom that has turned into a playground.
normal.cn: 想象一间会议室变成了操场。

normal.en: Pu-er-ILE: the stress sits on ile, and the word ends like a label.
normal.cn: pu-er-ILE：重音落在 ile，词尾听起来像一个标签。

normal.en: Say PYOO-uh-ryl; the first syllable sounds like a scolding.
normal.cn: 读成 PYOO-uh-ryl，第一音节听起来像一声责骂。

normal.en: Pair it with childlike: one praises wonder, the other blames it.
normal.cn: 把它和 childlike 配对：一个称赞好奇，一个责怪好奇。

abstract.en: Puerile measures behaviour against the age of the person doing it.
abstract.cn: puerile 用行为者的年龄来衡量行为。

abstract.en: The word began as a neutral description of boyhood and became a weapon for reviewers.
abstract.cn: 这个词起初是对少年期中性的描述，后来成了评论者的武器。

abstract.en: Calling an adult puerile is a way of removing his argument without answering it.
abstract.cn: 说一个成年人幼稚，是一种不回答论证就把它拿掉的办法。

examples.en: Two grown men traded nicknames, a puerile contest that outlasted the agenda.
examples.cn: 两个成年人在互起外号，这场幼稚的较劲比议程还长。

examples.en: The physician noted puerile breathing, which in an adult patient is a warning.
examples.cn: 医生记下了儿童型呼吸音，这在成年病人身上是一个警示。

examples.en: Childlike wonder is a gift; puerile wonder is an excuse.
examples.cn: childlike 的好奇是礼物，puerile 的好奇是借口。

dict_mnemonic.text: puer（男孩）+ ile：一副男孩做派，就是「幼稚的」。

root: 拉丁语 puer（男孩、孩子）派生的 puerilis（孩子气的）

sensesIntro.en: Two senses share one root: a grown person still acting like a child, and a clinical sign that belongs to childhood alone.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项共用一个根：一个还在像孩子一样行事的成年人，以及一种只属于童年的临床体征。

core.en: AN ADULT BODY CARRYING A CHILD'S MARK
core.cn: 成人身上带着孩子的印记

chain: THE MARK OF A CHILD APPEARS

branches.en: Conduct that a grown person should have outgrown.
branches.cn: 成年人本该丢掉的行为。

branches.en: Speech and taste stuck at the playground level.
branches.cn: 停在操场水平的言语与趣味。

branches.en: The word used as a verdict on a person.
branches.cn: 这个词被用作对人的判词。

branches.en: The neutral clinical sense, where boyish means normal for a boy.
branches.cn: 中性的临床义：boyish 指对孩子而言正常。

branches.en: One root, two judgements: a sneer or a diagnosis.
branches.cn: 同一个根，两种判断：一声冷笑或一个诊断。

intro.en: The puer family is small and boyish: puerile is the adjective, puerility the noun, and puerilism the medical return to childhood.
intro.cn: puer 词族小而带男孩气：puerile 是形容词，puerility 是名词，puerilism 是退回童年的医学说法。

latinIntro.en: Latin puer supplies the boy and -ilis supplies the adjective; the word therefore says 'of a boy' before it says anything rude.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 puer 提供男孩，-ilis 提供形容词；所以这个词在说出任何贬义之前，只说了「男孩的」。

items.exampleCN: 他幼稚地开玩笑。
