definition_zh: 心理学家；心理学工作者：以科学方法研究心智与行为的人，也指从事心理咨询、心理测验或组织应用的执业者
definition_en: a person trained in the scientific study of the mind and behaviour, or one who applies that training in counselling, testing or organisations
core_image: 隔着单向玻璃的观察室里，一个人记录受试者按键前的停顿，纸上画满一格一格的时间刻度
scene: 隔着一面单向玻璃，研究者记录受试者按键前的停顿，把每一次犹豫都标在时间轴上。 The clinic hired a psychologist to treat those pauses as data rather than noise.
sceneCN: 这里指受过训练、以观察与测量研究心智与行为的人（第 1 个义项：心理学家这一职业身份）；句意为诊所请了一位心理学家，把这些停顿当作数据而非噪声。

pos.zh: 心理学家；心理学研究者
心理师；心理咨询或心理治疗执业者

derivatives.zh: psycho-（心智） + -logy（学科）→ 研究心智与行为的学科
psychology + -ical（属于……的）→ 属于心理或心理学的
psychological + -ly（方式副词）→ 从心理层面
psychology + -ize（使动）→ 用心理学的语言解释，语义偏移为「做心理分析」
psychology + -ism（主义、倾向）→ 把一切问题化约为心理问题的倾向

senses.title: A researcher of mind and behaviour
senses.titleCN: 研究心智与行为的研究者
senses.definition: a person who studies mental processes and behaviour by experiment, observation or measurement
senses.definitionCN: 以实验、观察或测量研究心理过程与行为的人
senses.example: The psychologist ran the memory task with two hundred volunteers.
senses.exampleCN: 这位心理学家让两百名志愿者做了记忆任务。
senses.why: psychologist is psychology plus -ist 'one who practises', so the word names the person before it names any particular job.
senses.whyCN: psychologist 是 psychology 加表示「从事者」的 -ist，因此这个词先指人，再指具体岗位。

senses.title: A clinical or counselling practitioner
senses.definition: a licensed professional who assesses and treats emotional or behavioural difficulties through talk-based methods
senses.definitionCN: 以谈话等方法评估并处理情绪或行为困难的持照专业人员
senses.example: A clinical psychologist saw him weekly for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 一位临床心理师每周为他看诊，持续了一年。
senses.why: the same training was applied to illness, so the title expanded from the laboratory to the consulting room.
senses.whyCN: 同样的训练被用于疾病，头衔便从实验室扩展到诊室。

senses.title: A school psychologist
senses.definition: a professional employed by a school to assess learning difficulties and support pupils and teachers
senses.definitionCN: 受雇于学校，评估学习困难并支持学生与教师的专业人员
senses.example: The school psychologist tested the pupil for a reading difficulty.
senses.exampleCN: 学校心理师为这名学生做了阅读困难评估。
senses.why: schools need measurement and advice on learning, which is a natural home for the applied title.
senses.whyCN: 学校需要测量与学习建议，这正是这个应用头衔的自然落点。

senses.title: An educational psychologist
senses.definition: a specialist who studies how people learn and advises on teaching, curriculum and assessment
senses.definitionCN: 研究人如何学习，并就教学、课程与评估提供建议的专家
senses.example: An educational psychologist redesigned the spelling programme.
senses.exampleCN: 一位教育心理学家重新设计了拼写课程。
senses.why: the discipline has a branch for learning, and its practitioner carries the branch name.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科有专门研究学习的分支，从业者便带着该分支的名字。

senses.title: An industrial and organisational psychologist
senses.definition: a specialist who applies psychology to hiring, teamwork, performance and workplace well-being
senses.definitionCN: 把心理学用于招聘、团队、绩效与职场福祉的专家
senses.example: An industrial psychologist audited the hiring tests for bias.
senses.exampleCN: 一位工业心理学家审查了招聘测试中的偏见。
senses.why: wherever people work in groups, measurement and behaviour study can be sold as a service, and the title follows the market.
senses.whyCN: 只要人们成群工作，测量与行为研究就能作为服务出售，头衔便跟着市场走。

senses.title: A tester who administers assessments
senses.titleCN: 实施与解释心理测评的人
senses.definition: a person who administers standardised tests and interprets the scores for schools, clinics or courts
senses.definitionCN: 为学校、诊所或法庭实施标准化测验并解释分数的人
senses.example: The psychologist administered the standardised test under timed conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 心理师在计时条件下实施了标准化测验。
senses.why: testing is the oldest applied skill of the field, and the person who administers a test is still called by the same title.
senses.whyCN: 测评是这一领域最古老的应用技能，实施测验的人仍用同一头衔。

senses.title: A sport psychologist
senses.definition: a specialist who works with athletes on attention, arousal, routine and competitive stress
senses.definitionCN: 帮助运动员处理注意、唤醒水平、赛前程序与竞赛压力的专家
senses.example: The sport psychologist taught the sprinter a pre-race routine.
senses.exampleCN: 运动心理师教给短跑选手一套赛前程序。
senses.why: performance under pressure is a measurable behaviour, so a branch of practice grew around it.
senses.whyCN: 压力下的表现是一种可测量的行为，围绕它便长出一个实践分支。

senses.title: A forensic or legal psychologist
senses.definition: a specialist who assesses memory, risk or competence for courts and legal proceedings
senses.definitionCN: 为法庭与法律程序评估记忆、风险或行为能力的人
senses.example: A forensic psychologist warned the court about false eyewitness confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 一位司法心理师提醒法庭注意目击者的虚假自信。
senses.why: courts need evidence about perception and decision, which puts the title inside the courtroom.
senses.whyCN: 法庭需要关于知觉与决策的证据，这个头衔因此进了审判庭。

senses.title: The older student of the soul
senses.definition: a scholar of the soul or mind in the period before psychology became an experimental science
senses.definitionCN: 在心理学成为实验科学之前研究灵魂或心智的学者
senses.example: Eighteenth-century psychologists argued about the seat of the soul.
senses.exampleCN: 十八世纪的心理学家争论灵魂的居所。
senses.why: the Greek root psykhe meant 'breath, life, soul', so the earliest bearer of the title studied the soul, not behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 psykhe 意为「气息、生命、灵魂」，最早带这个头衔的人研究的是灵魂，而非行为。

intro.en: Psychologist is psychology plus the agent suffix -ist. Psychology is a New Latin coinage joining Greek psykhe 'breath, life, soul' and logos 'word, account, reason'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: psychologist 是 psychology 加表施动者的后缀 -ist。psychology 是新拉丁语造词，把希腊语 psykhe「气息、生命、灵魂」与 logos「言说、论述、理性」合在一起。年代为约数。

items.en: Psykhe meant 'breath, life, soul', the breath that marks a living being; the related verb psychein meant 'to breathe'. The word could also name the departed spirit.
items.cn: psykhe 意为「气息、生命、灵魂」，是标记活物的那口气；相关动词 psychein 意为「呼吸」。这个词也可指离体的亡灵。

items.en: Logos meant 'word, speech, account, reason'. In compound names of disciplines, -logia meant 'the study or systematic account of'.
items.cn: logos 意为「言词、叙述、道理、理性」。在学科复合名称中，-logia 意为「对……的研究或系统论述」。

items.en: The compound psychologia appeared in sixteenth-century academic Latin for the study of the soul, before any experimental method existed.
items.cn: 复合词 psychologia 在 16 世纪的学术拉丁语中出现，指对灵魂的研究，当时还没有任何实验方法。

items.en: Psychology entered English in the seventeenth century as the study of the soul; the modern scientific sense dates from the nineteenth century, when laboratories and measurement were established.
items.cn: psychology 在 17 世纪进入英语，指对灵魂的研究；现代科学义始于 19 世纪，那时实验室与测量方法已经建立。

items.en: Greek -istes 'one who practises' passed through Latin -ista into English -ist, so psychologist names the person who practises psychology.
items.cn: 希腊语 -istes「从事者」经拉丁语 -ista 进入英语成为 -ist，因此 psychologist 指从事心理学的人。

items.en: Source uncertain (first coiner and first English use): several sixteenth-century authors used psychologia independently, and the exact first English use of psychologist is not settled; the date given here is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首创者与英语首见）：16 世纪有数位作者各自使用 psychologia，psychologist 的确切英语首见亦无定论；此处年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds titles built on the same psych- stem that name different roles; group two holds people who also sit with a client but are trained differently.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 psych- 词干、却指不同角色的头衔；第二组是同样与来访者对坐、但训练路径不同的人。

entries.definition: A physician who has completed medical training and may prescribe drugs; a psychologist normally cannot prescribe.
entries.definitionCN: 完成医学训练的医生，可以开药；心理学家通常不能开药。

entries.definition: A practitioner trained in the Freudian or related analytic tradition, not in academic psychology as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 受弗洛伊德或相关分析传统训练的人，而非接受整个学术心理学训练的人。

entries.definition: A specialist in the construction and statistical validation of tests; the role is narrower than the general title.
entries.definitionCN: 专做测验编制与统计验证的人，角色比通称更窄。

entries.definition: A general title for one who treats mental or physical difficulties; many therapists lack a psychology degree.
entries.definitionCN: 处理心理或身体困难者的通称；许多治疗师并没有心理学学位。

entries.definition: A practitioner who offers structured listening and advice, often in schools or community services.
entries.definitionCN: 提供有结构的倾听与建议的从业者，常见于学校或社区服务。

entries.definition: Anyone who works directly with patients, including physicians and nurses; the word marks setting, not discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 任何直接接触病人的人，包括医生与护士；这个词标记工作场所，不标记学科。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实复合词与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: psykhe 'soul' plus logos 'account': an account of the soul, later an account of behaviour.
normal.cn: psykhe「灵魂」加 logos「论述」：关于灵魂的论述，后来变成关于行为的论述。

normal.en: -ist marks the person, so psychologist is the one who practises what psychology studies.
normal.cn: -ist 标记人，因此 psychologist 就是从事心理学所研究之事的人。

normal.en: The family runs psychology, psychological, psychologically, psychologize, psychologism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 psychology、psychological、psychologically、psychologize、psychologism。

normal.en: Job titles pin the branches: clinical, school, educational, industrial, sport and forensic.
normal.cn: 岗位头衔钉住各分支：临床、学校、教育、工业、运动与司法。

normal.en: The oldest sense is the soul, which is why the spelling begins with psych- and not with behav-.
normal.cn: 最古老的义项是灵魂，这正是拼写以 psych- 开头而不是以 behav- 开头的原因。

abstract.en: Picture a person who watches a key press and writes down a number instead of a feeling.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人盯着一次按键，写下的是一个数字，而不是一种感受。

abstract.en: Picture two rooms separated by glass: one person performs, the other measures.
abstract.cn: 想象被玻璃隔开的两间屋子：一间里的人在表现，另一间的人在测量。

abstract.en: Picture an old manuscript titled 'on the soul' slowly acquiring a stopwatch.
abstract.cn: 想象一册题为「论灵魂」的旧手稿，慢慢多了一只秒表。

examples.en: The psychologist compared reaction times across age groups.
examples.cn: 这位心理学家比较了不同年龄组的反应时。

examples.en: A psychologist may not prescribe drugs unless trained as a physician.
examples.cn: 心理学家除非受过医学训练，否则不能开药。

examples.en: The school hired a psychologist to review its assessment policy.
examples.cn: 学校聘请了一位心理师来审查评估政策。

dict_mnemonic.text: psycho（心智）+ log（研究）+ ist（人）＝ 研究心智的人；记「玻璃两侧：一侧表现，一侧测量」。

root: 希腊 psykhe「气息、生命、灵魂」+ logos「言说、论述、理性」，经新拉丁 psychologia「灵魂之学」加 -istes「从事者」；更深词源无定论，psykhe 与「呼吸」的联系为通行解释。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one trained observer: first the researcher, then the clinic, the school, the classroom, the office, the test room, the track, the court, and finally the older student of the soul.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿着同一个受过训练的观察者展开：先是研究者，再依次是诊室、学校、课堂、办公室、测评室、赛场、法庭，最后回到早期研究灵魂的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a trained observer on one side of glass, recording a measurable act on the other side.
core.cn: 核心意象：受过训练的观察者站在玻璃一侧，记录另一侧可测量的行为。

branches.en: THE RESEARCHER: the title begins as the person who studies and measures mind and behaviour.
branches.cn: 研究者：这个头衔最初指研究并测量心智与行为的人。

branches.en: THE HELPING ROOMS: clinic and school take the same training into assessment and care.
branches.cn: 助人的房间：诊室与学校把同一套训练带进评估与照护。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTIONS: learning and work each grow a branch with its own title.
branches.cn: 机构：学习与工作各自长出一个带专属头衔的分支。

branches.en: THE TEST AND THE TRACK: administering a score and shaping a routine are both applied measurement.
branches.cn: 测评与赛场：给分与塑造赛前程序，都是应用性的测量。

branches.en: THE COURT AND THE SOUL: the title reaches legal evidence at one end and the old study of the soul at the other.
branches.cn: 法庭与灵魂：这个头衔一端抵达法律证据，另一端回到古老的灵魂之学。

intro.en: Psychologist can be read as two Greek roots plus two suffixes: psykhe and logos build the discipline, -logia names it, and -ist names the person.
intro.cn: psychologist 可以读作两个希腊词根加两个后缀：psykhe 与 logos 构成学科，-logia 命名学科，-ist 命名人。

latinIntro.en: The discipline name is New Latin, coined from Greek elements; Latin supplies the shape of the suffixes -logia and -ista, which English shortened to -logy and -ist.
latinIntro.cn: 学科名是新拉丁语，用希腊成分造出；拉丁语提供了 -logia 与 -ista 后缀的外形，英语将其缩短为 -logy 与 -ist。

items.example: The root names what early writers thought left the body at death.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指早期作者认为死亡时离开身体的东西。

items.example: The root turns a subject into a field of study.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把一个主题变成一门研究领域。

items.meaning: the study or systematic account of
items.example: The suffix appears in biology, geology and psychology alike.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀同样出现在 biology、geology 与 psychology 中。

items.example: The New Latin noun predates any laboratory.
items.exampleCN: 这个新拉丁名词早于任何实验室。

items.meaning: the study of mind and behaviour
items.meaningCN: 研究心智与行为的学科
items.example: The English noun narrowed from soul to behaviour.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语名词从灵魂收窄到行为。

items.meaning: relating to the mind or to psychology
items.meaningCN: 与心智或心理学有关的
items.example: The adjective describes what the noun studies.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述这门学科所研究的东西。

items.example: The suffix marks the practitioner rather than the field.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记从业者，而非领域。

items.example: The verb often carries a note of criticism.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词常带一点批评意味。

items.example: It also builds biologist, economist and therapist.
items.exampleCN: 它也构成 biologist、economist 与 therapist。

latinEntries.meaning: of the study of the soul

definition_zh: 灌木；灌木丛；（园艺）花灌木；灌木层；果味糖浆饮（旧义，另源）
definition_en: a woody plant smaller than a tree, usually with several stems growing from the base
core_image: 一株不到腰高的木本植物，从同一个基部抽出三根细茎，旁边高树的树干已经枯死
scene: 同一基部抽出三根细茎的矮灌木，在高树枯死的地方仍然活着。 A low shrub with three stems from the same base survived where the taller trees had died.
sceneCN: 这里 shrub 指「低于乔木、通常自基部分出多根茎的木本植物」（第 1 个义项：小型多茎木本植物）；句意为同一基部抽出三根茎的矮灌木，在高树枯死之处存活下来。图中可辨识物件：三根细茎、共同基部、枯死的高树干、裸露地面。

pos.zh: 灌木；灌木丛（可数；集合义不可数）
果味糖浆饮（加醋或酒，18 世纪旧义，词源不同）

forms.label: 形容词（灌木状的；多灌木的）
名词（灌木丛；灌木栽植区）

derivatives.zh: 半灌木（基部木质、上部草质）

senses.title: A small multi-stemmed woody plant
senses.definition: a woody plant that stays low and usually sends up several stems from the same base instead of one trunk
senses.definitionCN: 一种低矮的木本植物，通常自同一基部长出多根茎，而非单一下干
senses.example: A low shrub with three stems from the same base survived the drought.
senses.exampleCN: 同一基部抽出三根茎的矮灌木熬过了干旱。
senses.why: the word's core is lowness plus woodiness: it is not a small tree because it branches at the ground.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是「低矮」加「木质」：它不是小树，因为它在贴地处就分叉。

senses.title: Shrubs planted as a garden mass
senses.titleCN: 庭园中成片栽植的灌木
senses.definition: a group or mass of low woody plants grown together for cover, flowers or boundary
senses.definitionCN: 成片栽植的低矮木本植物，用于遮蔽、观花或作边界
senses.example: The gardener cut the shrub back hard after flowering.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁在花后把这丛灌木重剪了一遍。
senses.why: in garden talk the countable plant and the uncountable mass blur, so 'the shrub' can mean the whole bed.
senses.whyCN: 在园艺口语中，单株与成片混在一起，因此这个说法也可指整片花坛。

senses.title: The botanical growth form
senses.titleCN: 植物学上的灌木生长型
senses.definition: a growth form defined by persistent woody stems branching near ground level and a mature height well below the tree layer
senses.definitionCN: 一种生长型：具宿存木质茎、贴近地面分枝，成熟高度远低于乔木层
senses.example: The flora keys out the shrub by its basal branching, not by its height alone.
senses.exampleCN: 这本植物志以基部分枝、而非单以高度来检索灌木。
senses.why: botany needs a form category between herb and tree, and shrub names exactly that middle.
senses.whyCN: 植物学需要一个介于草本与乔木之间的形态类别，shrub 正指这个中间层。

senses.title: A flowering ornamental shrub
senses.definition: a woody plant chosen and pruned mainly for showy flowers or coloured foliage in a garden
senses.definitionCN: 主要因花艳或叶色而在庭园中被选用、修剪的木本植物
senses.example: A pink flowering shrub anchors the corner of the border.
senses.exampleCN: 一株开粉花的灌木压住花坛转角。
senses.why: horticulture shifted the emphasis from wild form to cultivated display, so shrub came to mean a planted ornament.
senses.whyCN: 园艺学把重点从野生形态移到栽培展示，于是 shrub 也指栽下的观赏植物。

senses.title: The shrub layer of a forest
senses.definition: the vertical layer of woody plants between the herb layer and the tree canopy
senses.definitionCN: 位于草本层与乔木树冠之间的木本植物层
senses.example: Deer browsing has stripped the shrub layer from the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 鹿的啃食已把这片林子的灌木层剥光。
senses.why: in ecology a single plant gives its name to a whole stratum, because that layer is made of such plants.
senses.whyCN: 生态学中用单株植物之名指整个层，因为该层正是由这类植物构成。

senses.title: A dryland or scrub shrub
senses.definition: a tough, often thorny or waxy-leaved woody plant that dominates dry scrub and semi-desert
senses.definitionCN: 常带刺或具蜡质叶的耐旱木本植物，在干旱灌丛与半荒漠中占优势
senses.example: Salt-tolerant shrubs line the dry lake bed.
senses.exampleCN: 耐盐灌木沿干涸湖床排成一线。
senses.why: where trees cannot hold, shrubs become the dominant cover, so the word doubles as a landscape label.
senses.whyCN: 在乔木立不住的地方，灌木成为主要覆盖，于是这个词也兼作景观标签。

senses.title: Woody encroachment on open land
senses.definition: the spread of woody plants into grassland or pasture, often seen as degradation
senses.definitionCN: 木本植物向草地或牧场扩张，常被视为退化
senses.example: Unchecked grazing let shrub take over the lower pasture.
senses.exampleCN: 放牧失控让灌木占据了低处牧场。
senses.why: a plant name turns into a process name when the plant's spread changes what the land is.
senses.whyCN: 当某种植物的扩张改变了土地性质，植物名就变成了过程名。

senses.title: The old fruit-syrup drink
senses.titleCN: 旧时的果味糖浆饮（另源）
senses.definition: a drink made from fruit juice, sugar and vinegar or rum, popular in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries
senses.definitionCN: 由果汁、糖与醋或朗姆酒调成的饮品，在 18 至 19 世纪流行
senses.example: A jug of raspberry shrub stood cooling on the sill.
senses.exampleCN: 一罐覆盆子糖浆饮放在窗台上晾凉。
senses.why: this is a homonym, not a development of the plant sense: it comes through Arabic sharab 'a drink'.
senses.whyCN: 这是同形异源词，并非植物义的引申：它经阿拉伯语 sharab「饮料」而来。

intro.en: Shrub 'low woody plant' is a Germanic word of uncertain deeper origin; shrub 'fruit drink' is an unrelated homonym from Arabic.
intro.cn: shrub「低矮木本植物」是日耳曼词，更深来源不确定；shrub「果汁饮」则是来自阿拉伯语的不相关同形词。

items.en: Old English scrybb named brushwood and low woody growth. The form is recorded chiefly in glosses, so its early history is thin.
items.cn: 古英语 scrybb 指柴枝与低矮木本植物。该形式主要见于注释文献，早期历史材料很少。

items.en: The word matches North Frisian skrobb 'brushwood' and West Flemish schrobbe 'climbing vetch', which points to a North Sea Germanic stock.
items.cn: 这个词与北弗里斯兰语 skrobb「柴枝」、西佛兰德语 schrobbe「野豌豆」相合，指向北海日耳曼语来源。

items.en: Middle English shrub kept both the plant and the cut-brushwood readings, and the plant sense gradually dominated.
items.cn: 中古英语 shrub 同时保留「植物」与「砍下的柴枝」两义，后来植物义逐渐占主导。

items.en: The drink shrub entered English in the eighteenth century through Arabic sharab 'a drink' (compare sherbet and syrup), a completely separate line.
items.cn: 指饮品的 shrub 于 18 世纪经阿拉伯语 sharab「饮料」进入英语（参较 sherbet 与 syrup），是完全独立的一线。

items.en: Source uncertain (root and first date): no Germanic etymon beyond the North Sea forms is attested, and the pre-Germanic root is a reconstruction; the first English citation of the plant sense is not securely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：除北海诸语形式外没有更早的日耳曼语书证，其日耳曼语之前的词根属重构；植物义的最早英语书证年代也不可靠。

note.en: Group one separates shrub from its closest woody-plant neighbours; group two separates the vegetation words that are not single plants.
note.cn: 第一组把 shrub 与最接近的木本植物词分开；第二组区分那些指植被而非单株的词。

entries.definition: A general word for a low woody plant, often wild and rounded; shrub is the more technical and garden term.
entries.definitionCN: 低矮木本植物的通称，常指野生、团状者；shrub 更技术化，也更常用于园艺。

entries.definition: Low woody vegetation as a cover type, often stunted or thorny; it rarely names a single plant.
entries.definitionCN: 作为覆盖类型的低矮木本植被，常矮小或多刺；很少指单株植物。

entries.definition: A young tree with a single stem; it differs from a shrub in having one trunk that will grow tall.
entries.definitionCN: 单茎的幼树；与灌木的区别在于只有一根将来会长高的主干。

entries.definition: A plant woody only at the base and herbaceous above, so it dies back partly each winter.
entries.definitionCN: 仅基部木质、上部草质的植物，每年冬季部分枯死。

entries.definition: A planted area of shrubs, usually in a garden or park; it names the bed, not the species.
entries.definitionCN: 庭园或公园中成片栽植的灌木区；指花坛，不指物种。

entries.definition: The low plants growing beneath a forest canopy, including herbs and shrubs; broader than shrub.
entries.definitionCN: 林冠下生长的低矮植物，含草本与灌木；范围比 shrub 宽。

entries.definition: A line of shrubs planted and clipped as a barrier; the shrubs are means, the barrier is the point.
entries.definitionCN: 成行栽植并修剪作屏障的灌木；灌木是手段，屏障才是目的。

entries.definition: A dense stand of shrubs or small trees hard to walk through; it stresses impenetrability.
entries.definitionCN: 难以穿行的密集灌木或小树丛；强调难以通过。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: One base, many stems: that is the difference between a shrub and a tree.
normal.cn: 一个基部、多根茎：这就是灌木与乔木的区别。

normal.en: The family runs shrub, shrubby, shrubbery, shrubland, subshrub.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 shrub、shrubby、shrubbery、shrubland、subshrub。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: flowering shrub, evergreen shrub, shrub layer, desert shrub.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：花灌木、常绿灌木、灌木层、荒漠灌木。

normal.en: Ecology names a whole layer after the plant: the shrub layer.
normal.cn: 生态学以这种植物之名为整层命名：灌木层。

normal.en: The homonym warning: the fruit drink comes from Arabic, not from the plant.
normal.cn: 同形异源提醒：果汁饮来自阿拉伯语，与植物无关。

abstract.en: Think of a hand that never grew one wrist but five fingers straight from the palm.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手没有手腕，五根手指直接从掌心长出。

abstract.en: Think of a low wall that keeps growing back after every cut.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵矮墙，每次被砍后都重新长回。

abstract.en: Think of a crowd of short people holding a tall forest up from below.
abstract.cn: 想象一群矮个子在下面把高处的森林托住。

examples.en: Goats will eat almost any shrub before they touch the grass.
examples.cn: 山羊几乎先吃光任何灌木，才去碰草。

examples.en: The shrub layer recovered two years after the fire.
examples.cn: 火灾两年后灌木层恢复了。

examples.en: A single shrub can anchor a whole dune.
examples.cn: 一株灌木就能固定整座沙丘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「shrub」读音像「刷布」——矮矮一丛，像刷子一样贴地散开 → 灌木

root: 古英语 scrybb「柴枝、低矮木本植物」，与北弗里斯兰语 skrobb、西佛兰德语 schrobbe 同源，属北海日耳曼语一线；更深词根不确定。指饮品的 shrub 另出阿拉伯语 sharab。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one plant: it grows low and many-stemmed, fills gardens and forest layers, takes over dry ground, and finally shares its spelling with an unrelated drink.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一株植物展开：它低矮多茎，填满庭园与森林层次，占据干旱地，最后又与一种无关的饮料共用拼写。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one root crown sending up several thin stems instead of a single trunk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个根颈抽出几根细茎，而不是一根主干。

branches.en: FORM: lowness and basal branching define the plant both in common speech and in botany.
branches.cn: 形态：低矮与基部分枝，在日常语与植物学中都定义这种植物。

branches.en: GARDEN: the plant becomes an ornamental mass chosen for flower and boundary.
branches.cn: 庭园：这种植物成为按花与边界选用的观赏群体。

branches.en: STRATUM: in a wood the same plant gives its name to a whole layer.
branches.cn: 层次：在林中，同一种植物为整个层命名。

branches.en: DRY LAND: where trees fail, shrubs dominate, and their spread can count as degradation.
branches.cn: 旱地：乔木立不住时灌木占优，其扩张可算作退化。

branches.en: HOMONYM: the drink is a separate Arabic loan, so the two meanings must not be linked.
branches.cn: 同形异源：饮料是独立的阿拉伯语借词，两义不可串联。

intro.en: Shrub is a free root that takes several suffixes, producing a compact family of plant and landscape words.
intro.cn: shrub 是自由词根，可接若干后缀，形成一组紧凑的植物与景观词族。

latinIntro.en: Shrub has no Latin ancestor; the only Latin-looking item here, sub-, is a prefix borrowed into English word formation, not evidence of a Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: shrub 没有拉丁语祖先；此处唯一像拉丁语的 sub- 是英语构词借用的前缀，不能当作拉丁词根的证据。

items.example: The shrub regrew from the cut stems.
items.exampleCN: 这株灌木从被砍的茎上重新长出。

items.meaning: like a shrub; full of shrubs
items.example: The shrubby slope holds the soil.
items.exampleCN: 长满灌木的坡地能保住土壤。

items.example: A clipped shrubbery hides the wall.
items.exampleCN: 一片修剪过的灌木丛遮住了墙。

items.example: Shrubland replaced the overgrazed pasture.
items.exampleCN: 灌木林地取代了过牧的牧场。

items.meaning: a plant woody only at the base
items.example: Lavender is often grown as a subshrub.
items.exampleCN: 薰衣草常被当作半灌木栽培。

items.example: The sprayed verge was almost shrubless.
items.exampleCN: 喷过药的路边几乎没有灌木。

items.meaning: where shrubs are the main cover
items.example: A shrub-dominated community followed the fire.
items.exampleCN: 火灾后形成以灌木为主的群落。

items.example: Shrub-steppe supports sagebrush and bunchgrass.
items.exampleCN: 灌木草原上长着山艾与丛生禾草。

definition_zh: 简短；简洁；短促
definition_en: the quality of being brief; shortness of speech or time
core_image: 一张便条只写三个字，钉在门上；门外的人一读即走
scene: 上司批语从不废话。 The report earned praise for its brevity and clarity.
sceneCN: 这里 brevity 是「简洁」（第 1 个义项：言简意赅的品质）；句意是那份报告因简洁清晰而受称赞。

pos.zh: 简短；简洁
短暂；短促（指时间或生命）

derivatives.zh: 同根形容词，义为「简短的」
由同根加副词后缀构成，义为「简短地」
由同根加名词后缀构成，义为「每日祈祷书」
由前缀加同根构成，义为「缩写；缩短」

senses.title: Shortness of speech or writing
senses.definition: the quality of expressing much in few words
senses.definitionCN: 以很少的话表达很多内容的质量
senses.example: Telegrams forced writers into brevity.
senses.exampleCN: 电报迫使写作者求简。
senses.why: The root means short; its first workplace is the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 词根义为「短」，它最早的用武之地是句子。

senses.title: Shortness of duration
senses.definition: the fact of lasting only a short time
senses.definitionCN: 仅延续很短时间的事实
senses.example: We mourned the brevity of the spring visit.
senses.exampleCN: 我们惋惜春日来访的短暂。
senses.why: Short applies to time as well as text, and the noun stretches to cover both.
senses.whyCN: 「短」既形容文字也形容时间，名词随之兼管两者。

senses.title: Conciseness as a virtue
senses.definition: brevity praised as a style or discipline
senses.definitionCN: 被视为文风或修养的简洁
senses.example: In this office, brevity is a professional virtue.
senses.exampleCN: 在这间办公室，简洁是一种职业美德。
senses.why: Once speech costs time or money, cutting words becomes a moral good.
senses.whyCN: 一旦说话要花时间或金钱，删词便成了善举。

senses.title: A concise remark or form
senses.definition: an instance of brief speech or a shortened form
senses.definitionCN: 一次简短的发言或缩略的形式
senses.example: His farewell was a brevity of two words.
senses.exampleCN: 他的道别只有短短两个字。
senses.why: The quality can be counted: each short utterance is one brevity.
senses.whyCN: 品质可以计数：每一次简短言谈即是一个 brevity。

senses.title: Shortness of life
senses.definition: the short span of human life, in reflective use
senses.definitionCN: 人生之短促，用于沉思语境
senses.example: Poets dwell on the brevity of our days.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人反复咏叹人生之短促。
senses.why: Life is the longest text we write, and it too is short.
senses.whyCN: 人生是我们写就的最长文本，而它同样短促。

senses.title: Terse manner of a person
senses.definition: a habit of speaking little and pointedly
senses.definitionCN: 说话少而尖刻干脆的习惯
senses.example: Known for her brevity, she answered in single words.
senses.exampleCN: 她以寡言著称，回答只有单词。
senses.why: The style of the text attaches to the speaker who produces it.
senses.whyCN: 文本的风格附着于产出文本的说话人。

senses.title: Economy in art or music
senses.definition: compression and economy in a work of art
senses.definitionCN: 艺术作品中的压缩与经济
senses.example: The song's brevity is its secret weapon.
senses.exampleCN: 这首歌的短小正是它的秘密武器。
senses.why: What holds for sentences holds for sonnets and songs: less can carry more.
senses.whyCN: 句子之道通于诗与歌：少可载多。

senses.title: A brief summary or abstract
senses.definition: in older use, a condensed account of a larger work
senses.definitionCN: 旧义指对长篇著作的缩略记述
senses.example: Monks kept brevities of the monastery chronicle.
senses.exampleCN: 僧侣们为修道院编年史做简编。
senses.why: A text that has been made short is itself called a shortness.
senses.whyCN: 被缩短的文本自身也被称作「短」——brevity 由此指简编。

intro.en: Brevity comes from Latin brevitas, formed on brevis, short, the same root behind brief and abbreviate.
intro.cn: brevity 源自拉丁语 brevitas，建立在 brevis（短的）之上，与 brief、abbreviate 同根。

items.en: The reconstructed root *mregh-u- meant short, giving brevis and Greek brachys alike.
items.cn: 重构词根 *mregh-u- 意为短，同时产出拉丁 brevis 与希腊 brachys。

items.en: Latin brevis meant short, and brevitas meant shortness, in speech and in time.
items.cn: 拉丁语 brevis 意为短，brevitas 意为短促，兼指言与时。

items.en: Old French kept breve as the adjective and breve as a short document.
items.cn: 古法语保留 breve 作形容词，亦作「短简文书」之义。

items.en: English borrowed brevity from Latin brevitas, in Chaucer's generation.
items.cn: 十四世纪，英语自拉丁语 brevitas 借入 brevity，时当乔叟之世。

items.en: The abstract noun settled into praise and blame of style: brevity versus tedium.
items.cn: 此后抽象名词定型于对文风的褒贬：简洁对冗长。

items.en: Modern use favors the speech sense, with the time sense in set phrases like the brevity of life.
items.cn: 现代用法以言辞义为主，时间义存于「人生苦短」类固定语。

note.en: The brev- family is regular; its nearest rivals are the concise family and the terse family.
note.cn: brev- 词族规则；最近的竞争者是 concise 与 terse 两族。

entries.definition: short and sometimes unfriendly compression

entries.definition: careful use of words or means

entries.definition: clearly and briefly expressed quality

normalIntro.en: Say brief and add -ity: briefness is brevity, the Latin way.
normalIntro.cn: 念 brief 再加 -ity：briefness 的拉丁式说法就是 brevity。

normal.en: brev- is the Latin root for short.
normal.cn: brev- 是拉丁词根「短」。

normal.en: -ity makes abstract nouns, as in clarity.
normal.cn: -ity 构成抽象名词，如 clarity。

normal.en: abbreviate hides the same root inside.
normal.cn: abbreviate 内藏同一词根。

normal.en: the Greek cousin is brachy-, as in brachytherapy.
normal.cn: 希腊语表亲是 brachy-，如 brachytherapy。

normal.en: brevity of life is the classic collocation.
normal.cn: brevity of life 是经典搭配。

abstract.en: A door note of three words that moves a whole day.
abstract.cn: 三个字的门上便条，挪动了一整天。

abstract.en: Short lines carry long weights.
abstract.cn: 短句能载重物。

abstract.en: Life itself is the briefest text: punctuate well.
abstract.cn: 人生本身就是最短的文本：标点要好。

examples.en: The general's orders were models of brevity.
examples.cn: 将军的命令堪称简洁的典范。

examples.en: For all its brevity, the speech moved the hall to tears.
examples.cn: 言简而意深，演讲令全场落泪。

examples.en: He reflected on the brevity of childhood as his son left for school.
examples.cn: 儿子上学去了，他感叹童年之短。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不磨叽」——说话「不磨叽」就是简短：brevity 即「不磨叽」的品质。

root: 印欧重构词根 *mregh-u-（短）→ 拉丁语 brevis（短的）→ brevitas（短促）→ 中古英语经法语路径借入 brevity；与 brief、abbreviate 同根，与希腊语 brachys（短）同源。

sensesIntro.en: The noun measures shortness twice: in words and in time, then adds the counted remark, the terse person, and the condensed text.
sensesIntro.cn: 名词两度丈量「短」：词之短与日之短，另加可数的简语、寡言之人及缩略之文。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a three-word note that says everything
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写尽一切的三个字便条

branches.en: words kept short: the style, the utterance, the speaker
branches.cn: 词句之短：文风、话语与说话人

branches.en: shortness as craft: praised discipline, artistic economy
branches.cn: 作为技艺之短：受赞的克制、艺术的省笔

branches.en: time kept short: visits, and life itself
branches.cn: 时光之短：来访，以及人生本身

branches.en: the product of shortening: the abstract of a chronicle
branches.cn: 缩短的产物：编年史之简编

branches.en: the shared root of both shortnesses: time measured in words
branches.cn: 两种「短」的共同根源：以词量时

intro.en: A clean Latin formation: brev- plus the abstract suffix -itas, naturalized as -ity.
intro.cn: 典型的拉丁构词：brev- 加抽象后缀 -itas，归化为英语 -ity。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the whole family; Greek offers brachys as a parallel root.
latinIntro.cn: 整个词族由拉丁语供给；希腊语另以 brachys 作平行词根。

definition_zh: 修改；修正；改良；改正（行为）
definition_en: to change or improve something, especially a text or law; to reform one's ways
core_image: 拿起笔把错处涂掉补上：文件修好，人也改好
scene: 委员会讨论后决定对章程中过时的条款动笔修改。 The committee voted to amend the outdated section of the constitution.
sceneCN: 这里的 amend 是「修改、修正」（第 1 个义项：对条文正式修改）；句意是委员会投票决定修改宪法中过时的条款。

pos.zh: 修改；修正；改进
改过自新；改善

derivatives.zh: 动词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「修正案；修改」
动词加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「可修正的」
动词加施动者后缀 -er 构成，义为「修改者」
同源词，经拉丁语 emendare 进入英语，义为「校勘改正（文本）」

senses.title: To make formal changes to a text or law
senses.titleCN: 修改条文：对文本或法律作正式修改
senses.definition: to alter formally, especially a legal document or proposed legislation
senses.definitionCN: 对文本尤其是法律文件作正式修改
senses.example: Parliament moved to amend the voting law before the election.
senses.exampleCN: 议会着手在选举前修改选举法。
senses.why: The Latin root mendare means to free from fault; a formal edit strips errors from a text.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 mendare 意为「除去缺陷」，正式修订就是把文本中的错误清除。

senses.title: To correct a small fault or improve something
senses.titleCN: 修正改良：改正小毛病、加以改进
senses.definition: to put right a minor error or make something slightly better
senses.definitionCN: 改正小错误或使某物略有改进
senses.example: She amended her essay after the teacher's comments.
senses.exampleCN: 根据老师的评语，她修改了作文。
senses.why: Beyond laws, any writing or plan can be freed from its small defects.
senses.whyCN: 除法律外，任何文字或计划都可以被清除小缺陷，词义随之泛化。

senses.title: To reform one's own behavior
senses.titleCN: 改过自新：改正自身行为
senses.definition: to change one's conduct for the better; to give up bad habits
senses.definitionCN: 使自身行为变好，改掉坏习惯
senses.example: After the scandal, he vowed to amend his ways.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻之后，他发誓改过自新。
senses.why: The cleansing image turns inward: a person, like a text, can be edited free of faults.
senses.whyCN: 净化的意象转向人自身：人如文本，也能被修改掉缺陷。

senses.title: To make amends by compensation
senses.titleCN: 补偿弥补：以行动弥补过错
senses.definition: to repair a wrong by paying or doing something in return
senses.definitionCN: 通过赔偿或行动来弥补过错
senses.example: He worked weekends to make amends for missing the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 他周末加班，以弥补误了截止日期的过失。
senses.why: Fixing a fault extends to fixing the harm a fault caused, which requires repayment.
senses.whyCN: 「修复缺陷」延伸到「修复缺陷造成的伤害」，后者就需要补偿。

senses.title: To improve soil or growing conditions
senses.definition: to improve the quality of soil by adding material to it
senses.definitionCN: 通过添加物料改善土壤质量
senses.example: Gardeners amend heavy clay soil with compost.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁用堆肥改良黏重的土壤。
senses.why: Gardening treats the earth as a document with faults that can be corrected by additives.
senses.whyCN: 园艺把土地看作有缺陷的文本，可以通过添加物料来「修改」。

senses.title: To edit a scholarly text
senses.definition: to correct a text critically, as in editing an old manuscript
senses.definitionCN: 以校勘方式订正文本，如整理古代抄本
senses.example: Scholars amended the corrupted passages of the manuscript.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们订正了抄本中讹误的段落。
senses.why: This is the oldest scholarly use, close to the twin word emend, both meaning fault-removal.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的学术用法，与孪生词 emend 同出「除错」之义。

intro.en: Amend descends from Latin emendare, 'to free from fault', built on the root menda, a defect.
intro.cn: amend 源自拉丁语 emendare「使免于缺陷」，词根 menda 意为「缺陷」。

items.en: Root *mend-, physical defect or fault, also seen in mendacity.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *mend-「身体缺陷、过错」，也见于 mendacity（撒谎）。

items.en: menda, a fault or blemish; emendare, to correct by removing faults.
items.cn: 拉丁语 menda「缺陷、污点」；emendare「除错改正」。

items.en: amender, to correct or repair, from a- (to) plus amender root.
items.cn: 古法语 amender「改正、修复」，由 a-（向）加词根构成。

items.en: English amend appears meaning to repair or free from fault.
items.cn: 十三世纪英语 amend 出现，意为修复、去除缺陷。

items.en: The legal sense of amending statutes and constitutions became central.
items.cn: 十七、十八世纪修订法律与宪法的用法成为核心义项。

items.en: Now used for legal edits, small corrections, personal reform, and soil improvement.
items.cn: 如今用于法律修订、小修正、个人改过以及改良土壤。

note.en: Watch the near-twins amend, emend, and mend, plus rival verbs for changing texts.
note.cn: 注意 amend、emend、mend 这组近似词，以及修改文本的其他动词。

entries.definition: to correct a text critically; the pure Latin form for scholarly editing.
entries.definitionCN: 校勘订正文本；纯拉丁形式的学术用语，与 amend 同根。

entries.definition: a shortened form of amend, meaning to repair things or improve situations.
entries.definitionCN: amend 的缩略形式，指修补物件或改善状况。

entries.definition: capable of being amended or corrected.
entries.definitionCN: 可修正的、可修改的，amend 的形容词形式。

entries.definition: to re-examine and change, often broadly rather than in small patches.
entries.definitionCN: 修订、修改，往往是大范围重看重改。

entries.definition: to set something wrong right, formal register.
entries.definitionCN: 纠正、矫正，语域正式。

entries.definition: to change partially, without the moral tone of fault-removal.
entries.definitionCN: 局部修改，不含「除错改过」的道德色彩。

normalIntro.en: Anchor amend on the idea of removing a fault.
normalIntro.cn: 把 amend 锚定在「去除缺陷」这个核心上。

normal.en: a- + mend: mend (repair) with a prefix — amend, then shorten back to mend.
normal.cn: a- + mend：先加前缀成 amend（修正），再缩略回 mend（修补）。

normal.en: Latin menda = fault; emendare = drive the fault out.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 menda 即「缺陷」，emendare 即「把缺陷赶出去」。

normal.en: Family chain: menda → emend → amend → amendment.
normal.cn: 词族链：menda（缺陷）→ emend（校勘）→ amend（修正）→ amendment（修正案）。

normal.en: Remember the Five Amendments of the US Bill of Rights pattern: amend the constitution.
normal.cn: 联想美国权利法案的修正案传统：amend the constitution。

normal.en: make amends = make the fault whole again.
normal.cn: make amends 即「把过错弥补完整」。

abstract.en: See a red pen circling a flaw in the law and writing a better line beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象红笔圈出法条瑕疵，在旁边写下更好的表述。

abstract.en: Picture kneading dough: press out the lump, and the dough is amended.
abstract.cn: 想象揉面团：把疙瘩揉开，面团就「修正」好了。

abstract.en: A person saying sorry plus coffee for a broken mug — that is amends.
abstract.cn: 打碎杯子后道歉再请喝咖啡——这就是「弥补」。

examples.en: The board agreed to amend the bylaws at the next meeting.
examples.cn: 董事会同意在下次会议上修改章程。

examples.en: He apologized and promised to amend his behavior.
examples.cn: 他道了歉，并保证改正自己的行为。

examples.en: To make amends, the airline upgraded every affected passenger.
examples.cn: 为了弥补过失，航空公司为所有受影响的乘客升了舱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿门德」——念句「阿门」忏悔自己的错误，然后动手修改改正，改完心安。

root: 源自拉丁语 emendare「去除缺陷」，由 ex-（出）+ menda（缺陷、污点）构成；经古法语 amender 进入英语。同根词 emend（校勘）、mend（修补）、mendacity（说谎，含「缺陷」引申义）。

sensesIntro.en: Starting from fault-removal in texts, amend spreads to laws, personal reform, compensation, and even garden soil.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「清除文本缺陷」出发，amend 扩展到法律修订、个人改过、过错补偿乃至改良土壤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pressing out a flaw until the surface is clean
core.cn: 核心意象：把缺陷压出去，让表面恢复干净

branches.en: Statutes and constitutions formally edited
branches.cn: 法律与宪法的正式修订

branches.en: Small corrections and scholarly editing of texts
branches.cn: 小处修正与文本校勘

branches.en: A person editing out bad habits
branches.cn: 个人改掉坏习惯、改过自新

branches.en: Repaying the harm a fault has done
branches.cn: 弥补过错造成的伤害

branches.en: Correcting the faults of the earth itself
branches.cn: 改良土壤这类「修正大地」的用法

intro.en: Amend pairs the prefix a- with the fault root mend-, and regrows into amendments of every kind.
intro.cn: amend 由前缀 a- 加「缺陷」词根 mend- 构成，并衍生出各类「修正」词汇。

latinIntro.en: The Latin menda family keeps the idea of fault alive in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 menda 词族让「缺陷」的观念在英语中延续。

items.example: amender in French means to correct
items.exampleCN: 法语 amender 意为「改正」

items.example: emend means to drive the fault out
items.exampleCN: emend 即「把缺陷赶出去」

items.example: sine menda, without fault
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 sine menda 即「毫无瑕疵」

items.example: amendment is the act or result of amending
items.exampleCN: amendment 即修正（案）

items.example: the report exposed the agency's mendacity
items.exampleCN: 报告揭露了该机构的谎言成性

items.meaning: a beggar; one with a flaw of need
items.meaningCN: 乞丐；托钵僧（词根关联存疑，一般认为同源）
items.example: mendicant monks relied on alms
items.exampleCN: 托钵僧靠施舍为生

items.meaningCN: 拆除；动作方向与「修复」相反
items.example: they demolished the old bridge
items.exampleCN: 他们拆掉了旧桥

items.example: rectify the accounting error
items.exampleCN: 纠正账目错误

items.example: revise the draft before printing
items.exampleCN: 付印前修订草稿

items.example: improve your pronunciation daily
items.exampleCN: 每天改进你的发音

definition_zh: 入侵性的；（物种）外来的、迅速扩散并造成损害的；侵入性的；（肿瘤）侵袭性的；侵犯的
definition_en: spreading into a place or body where it does not belong, especially of a species that spreads beyond its native range and causes harm
core_image: 一条堤岸被外来的藤蔓整片盖住，本地芦苇从下面透不出一片叶子，藤尖还在向水面探
scene: 外来的藤蔓沿着堤岸一路铺开，本地芦苇被压在下面几乎见不到光。 Managers call the vine invasive because it smothers the native reeds.
sceneCN: 这里指外来物种迅速扩散并造成损害（第 1 个义项：侵入并扩散造成危害）；句意为管理者称这种藤为入侵性的，因为它把本地芦苇压死。

pos.zh: 入侵性的；外来的并造成损害的
侵入性的；侵袭性的（医学）
侵犯的；侵扰的

derivatives.zh: 该词的基座动词，由表示「进入」的前缀加表示「走」的词干构成，义为「侵入；侵袭」
由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「入侵；侵袭」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「入侵者」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「入侵性；侵袭性」
由表示否定的前缀加该词构成，义为「非侵入性的」
由表示「最低限度」的副词与形容词构成，义为「微创的」

senses.title: Spreading beyond the native range and causing harm
senses.titleCN: 越出原生范围扩散并造成损害
senses.definition: of a species, spreading rapidly outside the range it evolved in and damaging the systems it enters
senses.definitionCN: 指物种在其演化范围之外迅速扩散，并损害它进入的系统
senses.example: The shrimp proved invasive in every estuary where it was released.
senses.exampleCN: 这种虾在每一个被放归的河口都表现出入侵性。
senses.why: The word pictures an entry by force, and ecology borrowed it for species that take ground rather than share it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词画出「强行进入」的画面，生态学借它来形容那些夺取地面而非共享地面的物种。

senses.title: Not every introduced species is invasive
senses.titleCN: 并非所有引入物种都是入侵性的
senses.definition: describing harm and spread, not mere foreign origin, so a naturalised species that stays put is not called invasive
senses.definitionCN: 描述损害与扩散，而不是单纯的外来出身，因此安分定居的归化物种不被称为入侵性
senses.example: The poppy is introduced here but not invasive; it has stayed in the same fields for a century.
senses.exampleCN: 这种罂粟在这里是引入种，却不是入侵性的；它在一个世纪里都待在同一片田里。
senses.why: Origin and behaviour are separate tests, and the word marks the second one.
senses.whyCN: 出身与行为是两套检验，这个词标记的是第二套。

senses.title: Entering the body in medical procedures
senses.definition: of a procedure or device, entering the body by puncture, incision or tube
senses.definitionCN: 指操作或器械以穿刺、切开或插管的方式进入体内
senses.example: The clinic replaced the open operation with a less invasive test.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所把开刀手术换成了侵入性更小的检查。
senses.why: Medicine kept the physical sense of going in, and it measures how far the entry goes.
senses.whyCN: 医学保留了「进入」的字面意义，并衡量进入的程度。

senses.title: Spreading into surrounding tissue
senses.definition: of a tumour or infection, growing into nearby tissue rather than staying contained
senses.definitionCN: 指肿瘤或感染向邻近组织生长，而不是局限在原处
senses.example: The scan showed an invasive growth that had crossed the wall of the duct.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示有一处已穿过管壁的侵袭性生长。
senses.why: Cancer that crosses a boundary is doing exactly what the Latin verb described: going in.
senses.whyCN: 越过边界的癌所做的正是那个拉丁动词所描述的：走进去。

senses.title: Intruding on privacy or rights
senses.definition: of a measure, technology or question, forcing its way into matters that should stay private
senses.definitionCN: 指措施、技术或提问强行进入本应私密的领域
senses.example: Staff called the new monitoring invasive and refused the ankle tags.
senses.exampleCN: 员工称新的监控侵犯个人，拒绝佩戴脚环。
senses.why: The metaphor needs no translation here: a boundary is crossed against the will of the person inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻在这里无需翻译：边界是在里面那个人不情愿的情况下被越过的。

senses.title: Spreading vigorously, of plants
senses.definition: of a plant, growing and spreading so strongly that it displaces others
senses.definitionCN: 指植物生长扩散极强，以致挤走其他植物
senses.example: The reed is invasive in the marsh and has taken most of the open water.
senses.exampleCN: 这种芦苇在沼泽里扩散极强，已经占去了大部分明水。
senses.why: A plant that takes open water is behaving like an army taking ground, which is why the military word transferred.
senses.whyCN: 占据明水的植物，其行为像一支夺取地面的军队，这就是军事词会转过来的原因。

senses.title: Of military entry by force
senses.definition: of a force or operation, entering another territory by armed force
senses.definitionCN: 指力量或行动以武力进入他国领土
senses.example: The history course compared invasive campaigns across two centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这门历史课比较了两个世纪里的入侵性军事行动。
senses.why: The oldest sense is literal armed entry, and it remains available whenever a border is crossed by force.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是字面上的武装进入，只要边界被武力越过，这一义仍然可用。

senses.title: Of technologies that spread into new domains
senses.definition: of a tool or practice, spreading into areas where it was not expected and changing them
senses.definitionCN: 指工具或做法扩散到原本不被期待的领域并改变之
senses.example: Cheap sensors became invasive in daily life before any rule was written.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价传感器在任何人写规则之前就已经侵入日常生活。
senses.why: Tools spread the way organisms do, into spaces nobody assigned them, and the metaphor carries over.
senses.whyCN: 工具扩散的方式像生物一样，进入没人分给它们的空间，这个比喻因此顺手可用。

senses.title: A noun use for such organisms
senses.definition: in the plural, a shorthand for invasive plants or animals in management writing
senses.definitionCN: 在管理文本中以复数形式作为入侵植物或动物的简称
senses.example: The crew spent the summer pulling invasives from the channel.
senses.exampleCN: 这个班组花了整个夏天从水道里拔除入侵物种。
senses.why: Field crews shorten long phrases, so the adjective became a plural noun meaning the plants and animals they pull.
senses.whyCN: 野外班组会缩短长短语，于是这个形容词成了复数名词，指他们拔除的动植物。

intro.en: The word is a Latin participle turned adjective: a prefix for into and a verb for going make the verb to invade, and an adjective ending makes the description.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语分词转成的形容词：表示「进入」的前缀与表示「走」的动词构成「侵入」，再加形容词词尾成为描述词。

items.en: Vadere meant to go or to proceed, and it supplied the movement at the heart of the word.
items.cn: 这个词意为走、前行，提供了词的核心动作。

items.en: The compound meant to go into, enter or attack, and it was used of armies and of disease.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为走进、进入、攻击，用于军队，也用于疾病。

items.en: The adjective meant given to entering or attacking, and Late Latin used it in medical writing.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为好进入、好攻击的，晚期拉丁语在医学写作中使用它。

items.en: French carried the adjective onward, and English took it in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 法语把这个形容词继续传下，英语在十七世纪借入。

items.en: Early English used it for armies and for arguments that encroached on another's ground.
items.cn: 早期英语用它指军队，也指侵占他人地盘的论点。

items.en: Ecologists applied it to organisms spreading beyond their native range with harmful effects; the usage settled in the later twentieth century.
items.cn: 生态学家把它用于越出原生范围扩散并造成有害影响的生物；这一用法在二十世纪后期稳定下来。

note.en: The first group shares the going-in stem; the second group separates invasion from mere foreign origin.
note.cn: 第一组共用「走入」词干；第二组把入侵与单纯的外来出身区分开。

entries.definition: To enter by force, of armies, diseases or organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 指以强力进入，用于军队、疾病或生物。

entries.definition: The act of entering by force, and the event ecology counts.
entries.definitionCN: 指强行进入的行为，也是生态学所计的事件。

entries.definition: One that enters by force.
entries.definitionCN: 指强行进入者。

entries.definition: The quality of spreading and entering, measured in risk screening.
entries.definitionCN: 指扩散与进入的性质，在风险筛查中被度量。

entries.definition: Tending to avoid or escape; it shares the going verb but with a prefix for out.
entries.definitionCN: 指倾向回避或逃开的；共用「走」动词，但前缀意为「向外」。

entries.definition: Present outside its native range, a statement about origin only.
entries.definitionCN: 指存在于原生范围之外，只陈述出身。

entries.definition: Brought by people from elsewhere, without any claim about harm.
entries.definitionCN: 指由人从别处带来，不含损害之意。

entries.definition: Advancing gradually into another's space or time.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐渐侵占他人的空间或时间。

entries.definition: Pushing in where not wanted, common for privacy and devices.
entries.definitionCN: 指进入不受欢迎之处，常用于隐私与器械。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the going-in verb, the medical setting and the ecology test that separates origin from behaviour.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「走入」动词、医学场景，以及把出身与行为分开的生态学检验。

normal.en: Invade is go into, and invasive is the adjective of that going in.
normal.cn: 动词意为「走进去」，形容词就是这种进入的性质。

normal.en: Medicine asks how far the entry goes: open, minimally invasive, or no entry at all.
normal.cn: 医学问的是进入多深：开刀、微创，还是完全不进入。

normal.en: Alien and non-native state origin; invasive states behaviour and harm.
normal.cn: 「外来」陈述出身，「入侵性」陈述行为与损害。

normal.en: A naturalised poppy that stays in its field is not invasive, which is the commonest mistake.
normal.cn: 安分待在田里的归化罂粟不是入侵性的，这是最常见的错误。

normal.en: Minimally invasive is the fixed phrase that keeps the medical sense alive in everyday speech.
normal.cn: 「微创」是让医学义在日常语言里存活的固定说法。

abstract.en: Invasion is a claim about a boundary: the same movement is exploration in one frame and intrusion in another.
abstract.cn: 入侵是关于边界的判断：同样的移动，在一个框架里是探索，在另一个里是侵入。

abstract.en: Nature has no passports; the label is applied by the systems that receive the newcomer and pay for it.
abstract.cn: 自然界没有护照；这个标签由接收新来者并为之付出代价的那些系统贴上。

abstract.en: In medicine the word measures penetration of a body, in ecology penetration of a community: the geometry is the same.
abstract.cn: 医学上它度量对身体穿透，生态学上度量对群落的穿透：几何形状是一样的。

examples.en: The council removed the invasive shrub from the dune system.
examples.cn: 委员会清除了沙丘系统中的这种入侵灌木。

examples.en: Surgeons now prefer the less invasive route through the wrist.
examples.cn: 外科医生现在更青睐经手腕的侵入性较小的路径。

examples.en: Residents objected to the invasive questions at the checkpoint.
examples.cn: 居民反对检查站那些侵犯个人隐私的提问。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因维西夫」——因是进来，维西夫是走，走进别人的地盘还不走，就是入侵性的

root: 拉丁语 vadere「走」→ invadere「走入、攻击」← in-「进入」→ 晚期拉丁语 invasivus「好进入的」→ 法语 invasif → 英语十七世纪借入。二十世纪后期生态学用它指越出原生范围扩散并造成损害的外来生物，此前主要指军事与医学上的侵入。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one movement of going in: the ecological spread, the origin test it is not, three kinds of physical entry, plants, armies, technology and a shorthand noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟随同一个「走入」的动作：生态扩散、它并不等同于的出身检验、三种实体进入、植物、军队、技术与名词简称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foreign vine sheets the bank, cutting light from the reeds below while its tips reach the water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条外来藤蔓铺满堤岸，把下面的芦苇遮死，藤尖还探向水面。

branches.en: THE ECOLOGICAL SPREAD: a species taking ground, and a plant growing strongly enough to displace others.
branches.cn: 生态扩散：物种夺取地面，以及植物长到足以挤走其他植物。

branches.en: THE TEST IT IS NOT: foreign origin alone, which introduced and naturalised species also have.
branches.cn: 它并不等同的检验：单纯的外来出身，引入与归化物种同样具备。

branches.en: THE MEDICAL ENTRY: a procedure entering the body, and a growth crossing into tissue.
branches.cn: 医学进入：操作进入体内，以及生长越入组织。

branches.en: THE OTHER INTRUSIONS: privacy, armed force, and tools spreading into unexpected domains.
branches.cn: 其他侵入：隐私、武力，以及扩散到意外领域的工具。

branches.en: THE SHORTHAND: invasives as the working noun of removal crews.
branches.cn: 简称：清除班组日常工作用语中的「入侵物种」。

intro.en: A prefix for into and a verb for going make the verb, and an adjective ending makes the description.
intro.cn: 表示「进入」的前缀与表示「走」的动词构成动词，形容词词尾构成描述词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies vadere, invadere, invasio and invasivus; the recorded chain runs without gaps.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「走」「走入」「进入」与「好进入的」等形式，有记录的链条中间没有断口。

definition_zh: 合作；协作；两个以上的人或团体共同从事一项工作；（历史）与占领者合作
definition_en: the act of working jointly with others on a shared task or project
core_image: 两个人各执绳子的一端，中间悬着一块沉重的石板，只有同时用力才能把它抬进门
scene: 两个实验室把各自的样本和数据放在同一张桌上，轮流守夜跑完整个实验。 The collaboration between the two labs produced a result neither could have reached alone.
sceneCN: 这里 collaboration 指两个以上主体共同投入、完成一项工作的合作（第 1 个义项：共同劳动）；句意为两个实验室的合作产生了任何一方单独都无法达到的结果。

pos.zh: 合作；协作（不可数，指合作状态或活动）
一项具体的合作项目（可数，用复数 collaborations）

derivatives.zh: 合作；协作（由拉丁 collaborare「一起劳动」经法语进入英语，保留「共同出力」的动作义）
协作的；合作的（由 collaborate 加表示「倾向」的后缀构成，转指以共同参与为特征）
合作者；协作者（由 collaborate 加表示「人」的后缀构成，转指共同出力的人）
实验室（同出拉丁 laborare「劳动」，由「劳作之处」转指进行实验的场所）
详述；精心制作的（由表示「向外」的拉丁前缀加 laborare 构成，从「费力做出」转指细致加工）
费力的；艰苦的（由拉丁 labor「劳动」加表示「充满」的后缀构成，转指劳动量很大）

senses.title: Working together on a shared task
senses.definition: the act of two or more people or groups working jointly on the same task
senses.definitionCN: 两个以上的人或团体共同投入同一项工作的行为
senses.example: The collaboration between the two labs produced a result neither could have reached alone.
senses.exampleCN: 两个实验室的合作产生了任何一方单独都无法达到的结果。
senses.why: Collaboration is labour shared: the Latin verb joins 'together' to 'work', so the core is joint effort rather than mere contact.
senses.whyCN: collaboration 是共享的劳动：拉丁动词把「一起」接到「劳动」上，核心是共同出力，而非仅仅接触。

senses.title: Joint authorship or creation
senses.definition: the state of producing a book, work of art or invention together, with shared credit
senses.definitionCN: 共同完成书籍、艺术品或发明，并共享署名
senses.example: The album is a collaboration between a composer and a field recordist.
senses.exampleCN: 这张专辑是一位作曲家与一位野外录音师的共同创作。
senses.why: When the joint work leaves a named product, the word shifts from the activity to the shared credit.
senses.whyCN: 当共同劳动留下具名成品，词义就从活动转到共享的署名。

senses.title: Wartime cooperation with an occupier
senses.definition: the act of working with an enemy occupier, treated as betrayal by compatriots
senses.definitionCN: 与敌方占领者合作，被同胞视为背叛的行为
senses.example: The post-war trials punished wartime collaboration with the occupying army.
senses.exampleCN: 战后审判惩罚了战时与占领军合作的行为。
senses.why: History gave the neutral word a dark sense: working together becomes treason when the partner is an enemy.
senses.whyCN: 历史给这个中性词添了黑暗义：当伙伴是敌人时，共同工作就变成叛国。

senses.title: Cross-disciplinary collaboration
senses.definition: joint work between specialists from different fields, each contributing a distinct method
senses.definitionCN: 不同领域的专家共同工作，各自贡献不同方法
senses.example: The climate report required collaboration between physicists and historians.
senses.exampleCN: 这份气候报告需要物理学家与历史学家协作。
senses.why: Complex problems no longer fit one department, so the word names the bridge between different expert languages.
senses.whyCN: 复杂问题不再属于单一部门，因此这个词命名不同专家语言之间的桥。

senses.title: Digital collaboration tools
senses.definition: the use of shared software and networks so that people can work on one file or project at a distance
senses.definitionCN: 使用共享软件与网络，使人们能远程处理同一文件或项目
senses.example: Remote collaboration improved once the team shared one editing space.
senses.exampleCN: 团队共用同一个编辑空间后，远程协作改善了。
senses.why: Technology extends the same joint labour across distance, turning a room into a network.
senses.whyCN: 技术把同一种共同劳动拉过距离，把一间屋子变成一张网络。

senses.title: A business partnership
senses.definition: a working arrangement between firms or departments for a shared commercial goal
senses.definitionCN: 企业或部门为共同商业目标形成的合作安排
senses.example: The two firms announced a collaboration to build the charging network.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司宣布合作建设充电网络。
senses.why: Commerce uses the word for a bounded arrangement: the parties remain separate but pool part of their work.
senses.whyCN: 商业用这个词指有边界的安排：各方仍独立，但把部分工作合在一起。

senses.title: Scientific collaboration
senses.definition: joint research by scientists who share data, instruments or authorship across institutions
senses.definitionCN: 科学家跨机构共享数据、仪器或署名权的研究合作
senses.example: The discovery rested on a long collaboration across three continents.
senses.exampleCN: 这项发现依赖横跨三大洲的长期合作。
senses.why: Big science is rarely solitary, so the word becomes the normal label for shared instruments and shared papers.
senses.whyCN: 大科学很少单干，因此这个词成为共享仪器与共享论文的常规标签。

senses.title: Abstract: effort greater than its parts
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：合力超过部分之和
senses.definition: joint effort whose result exceeds what the participants could produce separately
senses.definitionCN: 其结果超过参与者各自单独所能产出的共同出力
senses.example: The essay argues that collaboration is not addition but a third mind.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章主张合作不是相加，而是生出第三个头脑。
senses.why: At its most abstract the word names the surplus that appears when separate skills interlock.
senses.whyCN: 推到最抽象处，这个词命名不同技能咬合时出现的盈余。

intro.en: Collaboration comes from Latin collaborare 'to work together', from com- 'together' plus laborare 'to work'. It entered English in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: collaboration 来自拉丁 collaborare「一起劳动」，由表示「一起」的成分加 laborare「劳动」构成。它在十九世纪进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Labor meant 'work, toil, effort', and also 'a task'. It is the noun behind laborious and laboratory.
items.cn: labor 意为「劳动、辛苦、努力」，也指「一项任务」。它是 laborious 与 laboratory 背后的名词。

items.en: Laborare meant 'to work, toil, take pains'. The verb keeps the physical effort of the noun.
items.cn: laborare 意为「劳动、辛苦、费心」。这个动词保留了名词里的体力付出。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus laborare produced collaborare 'to work together'. The Latin verb had no political colour.
items.cn: 表示「一起」的成分加 laborare 构成 collaborare「一起劳动」。这个拉丁动词没有政治色彩。

items.en: French collaboration and English collaboration appeared in the nineteenth century for joint work in science, letters and business.
items.cn: 法语 collaboration 与英语 collaboration 在十九世纪出现，指科学、文学与商业中的共同工作。

items.en: During the Second World War the same word was applied to cooperation with an occupying power, and this negative sense became fixed in many languages.
items.cn: 第二次世界大战期间，同一个词被用于指与占领国合作，这一负面义在多种语言中固定下来。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the first printed English use of collaboration is not precisely recorded, and the exact date when the wartime sense became standard is disputed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：collaboration 在英语中最早印行于何时没有精确记录；战时义何时成为标准说法也有争议。

note.en: Group one separates the word from other Latin verbs of working together; group two holds the everyday names for joint work.
note.cn: 第一组把这个词与其他表示共同工作的拉丁动词分开；第二组是共同劳动的日常说法。

entries.definition: From Latin cooperari, built on operari 'to work' and opus 'work'. It stresses mutual help more than a shared project.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 cooperari，基底是 operari「工作」与 opus「工作」。它更强调互相帮助，而非共同项目。

entries.definition: From Latin ordinare 'to arrange in order'. It means keeping activities in step, not doing the work together.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 ordinare「按次序安排」。它指让活动步调一致，而非一起做同一件事。

entries.definition: From Latin colludere 'to play together', built on ludere 'to play'. It means a secret, often dishonest agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 colludere「一起玩」，基底是 ludere「玩」。它指秘密且常不正当的串通。

entries.definition: From Latin collega, built on legare 'to send as a deputy', not laborare. A colleague is a fellow worker, not the joint work.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 collega，基底是 legare「派为使节」，并非 laborare。同事是一起工作的人，不是共同工作本身。

entries.definition: The everyday noun for people working well together; collaboration is its formal and project-oriented counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指人们配合良好的日常名词；collaboration 是其正式、以项目为导向的对应词。

entries.definition: A formal arrangement between parties, often legal and long-term; collaboration can be a single project.
entries.definitionCN: 各方之间的正式安排，常带法律与长期性质；collaboration 可以只是一个项目。

entries.definition: Willing help offered to another's effort; it does not require a shared product or shared credit.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意协助他人的努力；它不要求共同成品或共同署名。

entries.definition: A formal union of parties for a common aim, usually political or military; it stresses the bond rather than the work.
entries.definitionCN: 各方为共同目标结成的正式联盟，通常指政治或军事；它强调纽带而非劳动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定说法与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Laborare means to work, so collaboration is literally working together.
normal.cn: laborare 意为劳动，所以 collaboration 字面上就是一起劳动。

normal.en: The 'together' prefix is the same one in collect and cooperate, but only this verb attaches it to work.
normal.cn: 表示「一起」的前缀与 collect、cooperate 相同，但只有这个动词把它接到「劳动」上。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scale: research collaboration, international collaboration, in collaboration with.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出尺度：研究合作、国际合作、与……合作。

normal.en: Laboratory shares the work root: a place of work became a place of experiment.
normal.cn: laboratory 共享「劳动」词根：劳作之处变成了实验之处。

normal.en: The wartime sense is the dark twin: the same joint work, now with an enemy.
normal.cn: 战时义是它的黑暗双生：同一种共同劳动，伙伴换成了敌人。

abstract.en: Picture two people holding opposite ends of one rope around a heavy stone.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人各执一根绳子的两端，绕着一块沉重的石头。

abstract.en: Picture two hands correcting the same drawing, each line continuing the other.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在同一张图上改线，每条线都接着另一条。

abstract.en: Picture a third mind appearing between two speakers as they talk.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人说话时，在他们之间出现第三个头脑。

examples.en: The bridge was built through collaboration between engineers and local masons.
examples.cn: 这座桥由工程师与本地石匠合作建成。

examples.en: International collaboration shortened the vaccine trial by years.
examples.cn: 国际合作把疫苗试验缩短了数年。

examples.en: The wartime collaboration still divides the town's memory.
examples.cn: 战时的通敌合作至今仍分裂着这座镇的记忆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可 拉伯 雷 申」——一起出力把重东西抬起来 → 合作

root: 拉丁 collaborare「一起劳动」= 表示「一起」的成分 + laborare「劳动」；后者来自 labor「劳动」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start with shared labour, then move to shared credit, wartime betrayal, cross-disciplinary work, remote tools, business deals, big science and finally the surplus that appears when skills interlock.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从共同劳动出发，转到共享署名、战时背叛、跨学科工作、远程工具、商业协议、大科学，最后是技能咬合时出现的盈余。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands on one rope, a heavy stone between them, neither able to lift it alone.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手握同一根绳，中间是一块沉重的石头，谁都单独抬不起来。

branches.en: WORK AND CREDIT: joint labour, then the shared name on what it produces.
branches.cn: 劳动与署名：先是共同出力，再是成品上的共同名字。

branches.en: THE DARK TWIN: the same joint work performed with an enemy occupier.
branches.cn: 黑暗双生：同一种共同劳动，伙伴换成敌方占领者。

branches.en: ACROSS BORDERS: different disciplines and different institutions pool methods and instruments.
branches.cn: 跨越边界：不同学科与不同机构共享方法与仪器。

branches.en: TOOLS AND CONTRACTS: software carries the work across distance, and firms bound it with an agreement.
branches.cn: 工具与合同：软件把劳动拉过距离，公司用协议给它划界。

branches.en: SURPLUS: the result exceeds what any participant could make alone.
branches.cn: 盈余：结果超过任何参与者单独所能做出。

intro.en: Collaboration is a Latin verb of work with a prefix meaning 'together', plus a noun ending.
intro.cn: collaboration 是一个表示劳动的拉丁动词，带表示「一起」的前缀，再加名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin labor gives laborious and laboratory; laborare gives collaborate, collaboration and collaborator.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 labor 衍生 laborious 与 laboratory；laborare 衍生 collaborate、collaboration 与 collaborator。

items.example: The root supplies the toil.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「辛苦」这一层。

items.example: Laborare is the act of working.
items.exampleCN: laborare 是劳动的动作。

items.example: Collaborare joins the prefix to the work.
items.exampleCN: collaborare 把前缀接到劳动上。

items.example: Collaborate is the English verb.
items.exampleCN: collaborate 是英语动词。

items.structure: collaborate plus a suffix of action
items.example: The noun names the joint activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名共同活动。

items.structure: collaborate plus a suffix meaning 'tending to'
items.example: Collaborative describes the arrangement.
items.exampleCN: collaborative 描述这种安排。

items.example: The person who shares the labour.
items.exampleCN: 共同出力的人。

items.structure: laborare plus a suffix of place
items.example: The work place became a research place.
items.exampleCN: 劳作之处变成研究之处。

items.example: To elaborate is to work something out fully.
items.exampleCN: elaborate 就是把某物完全做出来。

definition_zh: 可复现的；可重复的；可再生的；可复制的
definition_en: able to be produced again, especially with the same result
core_image: 两台机器读同一张配方卡，出料口各吐出一件一模一样的成品
scene: 车间里两台机器读同一张配方卡，出料口各吐出一件成品，检验员把两件并排比对尺寸。 The result was reproducible in every trial, even when the room temperature changed.
sceneCN: 这里指同样的结果能够被再次做出来（第 1 个义项：结果可被再次得到）；句意为每一次试验的结果都可复现，即使室温发生变化。图中可辨识物件：两台机器、配方卡、两件成品、卡尺。

pos.zh: 可复现的；可重复的；可再生的；可复制的

senses.title: The result can be obtained again
senses.definition: able to be obtained again under the same conditions, as a result
senses.definitionCN: 作为结果，能在相同条件下被再次得到
senses.example: The result was reproducible in every trial, even when the room temperature changed.
senses.exampleCN: 每一次试验的结果都可复现，即使室温发生变化。
senses.why: Reproduce is to produce again, and -ible says the producing can be done again.
senses.whyCN: 动词表示再次产出，后缀表示这件事能够被再做一次。

senses.title: The experiment can be repeated
senses.definition: described fully enough for another team to repeat the whole procedure
senses.definitionCN: 描述得足够完整，使另一个团队能重复整套步骤
senses.example: A reproducible experiment must describe every step in detail.
senses.exampleCN: 可重复的实验必须把每一步都详细写清。
senses.why: A procedure that cannot be followed again cannot produce the result again.
senses.whyCN: 步骤无法被照着再做，结果也就无法再次产出。

senses.title: Able to produce offspring
senses.definition: able to produce new individuals, as a living thing
senses.definitionCN: 作为生物，能够产生新的个体
senses.example: These plants are reproducible from seed within one season.
senses.exampleCN: 这些植物在一个季节内就能由种子繁殖。
senses.why: Biology uses reproduce for making offspring, so the adjective also means able to breed.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用该动词指繁殖后代，所以这个形容词也指能够繁殖。

senses.title: Able to be printed again
senses.definition: able to be copied from an original plate or file without loss
senses.definitionCN: 能够从原版或文件复制而不失真
senses.example: The map is reproducible from the original plate.
senses.exampleCN: 这张地图可以从原版重新印制。
senses.why: Printing was one of the first technologies to make copying a routine, and the word followed it.
senses.whyCN: 印刷是最早使复制变得常规的技术之一，这个词也跟着走。

senses.title: An instrument that reads the same
senses.definition: giving the same reading when the same object is measured again
senses.definitionCN: 再次测量同一对象时给出同一读数
senses.example: The balance gave reproducible readings on the same block.
senses.exampleCN: 这台天平对同一块砝码给出可再现的读数。
senses.why: The adjective can describe the machine as well as the result it produces.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词既能描述结果，也能描述产出结果的机器。

senses.title: Code that can be rerun
senses.definition: able to be rerun from shared data and code to give the same output
senses.definitionCN: 能从共享的数据与代码重跑，并给出同一输出
senses.example: The analysis is reproducible from the shared code.
senses.exampleCN: 这项分析可以用共享的代码重跑。
senses.why: Digital work made the steps into files, so reproducibility became a property of code.
senses.whyCN: 数字工作把步骤变成文件，可复现性于是成了代码的属性。

senses.title: A process that repeats in production
senses.definition: giving the same product or measurement across repeated production runs
senses.definitionCN: 在反复生产中给出一致的产品或测量
senses.example: The coating process is reproducible across the whole line.
senses.exampleCN: 这道涂层工艺在整条生产线上都可重复。
senses.why: Industry asks whether the same process can be trusted to give the same thing twice.
senses.whyCN: 工业要问的是：同一流程能不能被信任地做出两次同样的东西。

senses.title: Sound or image copied without loss
senses.titleCN: 无损复制的声音或图像
senses.definition: able to be copied again without a noticeable loss of quality
senses.definitionCN: 能够再次复制而不出现明显质量损失
senses.example: The recording is reproducible without any loss of quality.
senses.exampleCN: 这段录音可以无损复制。
senses.why: Digital copying separated the copy from the decay that paper copies suffer.
senses.whyCN: 数字复制把复制品与纸面复制品的损耗分开了。

intro.en: Reproducible is reproduce plus the Latin ending -ible, able to be. Reproduce comes from re- again and Latin producere, to lead forth. The source is clear; the first record date of the adjective is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词由「产出」动词加表示「能够」的后缀构成。该动词来自表示「再次」的前缀与拉丁 producere「向前引出」。词源清楚，形容词最早记录的年代不确定。

items.en: Producere joined pro- forward to ducere lead, meaning to bring forth.
items.cn: producere 把意为「向前」的前缀加到意为「引导」的词根上，意为带出。

items.en: Re- adds the sense of a second producing, giving reproduce.
items.cn: 表示「再次」的前缀加上第二次产出的意思，构成「再次产出」的动词。

items.en: Latin -ibilis means able to be, so reproducible is able to be produced again.
items.cn: 拉丁语 -ibilis 意为「能够被……」，因此「可复现的」指能够被再次产出。

items.en: English reproducible is recorded from the modern period with copying and biological senses; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语里这个形容词在近现代有复制与生物两类用法记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Printing and biology each gave the adjective a concrete home before science made it abstract.
items.cn: 印刷与生物学各自给了它一个具体归宿，科学随后把它抽象化。

items.en: Twentieth-century research made reproducible a standard requirement for results and methods.
items.cn: 二十世纪的研究使它成为结果与方法的标准要求。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like reproducible; the second names adjectives close in meaning but different in scope.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「本词」相近；第二组是意思接近但范围不同的形容词。

entries.definition: The verb for producing again or breeding.
entries.definitionCN: 再次产出或繁殖的动词。

entries.definition: The adverb for doing something in a repeatable way.
entries.definitionCN: 以可重复的方式做某事的副词。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality itself.
entries.definitionCN: 这种性质本身的名词形式。

entries.definition: A copy or the process of breeding.
entries.definitionCN: 复制品，或繁殖过程。

entries.definition: To make or bring forth; the base without re-.
entries.definitionCN: 制造或产出；去掉 re- 的基础词。

entries.definition: Able to be done again by the same person, often narrower than reproducible.
entries.definitionCN: 能被同一个人再做一次，范围常比 reproducible 窄。

entries.definition: Able to be copied or repeated by another team.
entries.definitionCN: 能被另一个团队复制或重复。

entries.definition: Giving the same result each time, without claiming it is right.
entries.definitionCN: 每次都给出同一结果，但不声称它是对的。

entries.definition: Trustworthy over repeated use, a broader quality.
entries.definitionCN: 在反复使用中可信，是一种更宽的性质。

entries.definition: Able to be copied exactly, with emphasis on the copy rather than the result.
entries.definitionCN: 能够被精确复制，强调复制品而非结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin producing verb, the real -ible ending and real technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「产出」动词、真实的「能够」后缀与真实技术搭配。

normal.en: Reproducible is reproduce plus -ible: able to be produced again.
normal.cn: reproducible 是 reproduce 加 -ible：能够被再次产出。

normal.en: Producere meant to lead forth, and re- asks for a second leading.
normal.cn: producere 意为向前引出，re- 要求第二次引出。

normal.en: Fixed phrases include reproducible result, reproducible experiment and reproducible code.
normal.cn: 固定说法有可复现结果、可重复实验与可复现代码。

normal.en: A plant that is reproducible from seed and a map that is reproducible from a plate share the same ending but not the same field.
normal.cn: 能由种子繁殖的植物与能从原版印出的地图，共享同一个词尾，却不在同一领域。

normal.en: A balance with reproducible readings is trusted with the same block again and again.
normal.cn: 读数可再现的天平，才被信任地反复称同一块砝码。

abstract.en: Reproducible is a promise made to the next person who tries.
abstract.cn: 可复现是对下一个尝试者作出的承诺。

abstract.en: A copy that can be made again is worth more than a copy that cannot.
abstract.cn: 能再复制一次的复制品，比不能再复制的更值钱。

abstract.en: The adjective asks not whether something happened, but whether it can happen twice.
abstract.cn: 这个形容词不问某事是否发生过，而问它能不能发生两次。

examples.en: The method is reproducible enough for a teaching lab.
examples.cn: 这个方法足够可重复，适合教学实验室。

examples.en: A reproducible figure should come with the data behind it.
examples.cn: 可复现的图应当附上其背后的数据。

examples.en: The effect was small but reproducible across three sites.
examples.cn: 效应不大，但在三个地点都可复现。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「能再产出的」——同一结果还能再做出来：可复现的

root: 这个词由意为「再次」的前缀、意为「产出」的词根与表示「能够」的后缀构成。词根源自拉丁 producere「向前引出」（前缀意为「向前」加词根意为「引导」）。印刷与生物学先有具体用法，现代科学又把它变成结果与方法的标准要求；词源清楚，最早记录年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one repeatable thing: a result obtained again, a repeatable experiment, a breeding plant, a reprinted map, a stable instrument, rerunnable code, a repeatable process, and a lossless copy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一件「可再做一次」的东西：再次得到的结果、可重复的实验、能繁殖的植物、可重印的地图、稳定的仪器、可重跑的代码、可重复的流程，以及无损复制。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two machines read the same recipe card and turn out two identical parts.
core.cn: 核心意象：两台机器读同一张配方卡，各吐出一件一模一样的零件。

branches.en: THE RESULT AND THE RUN: the same number returns, and the steps allow the run to happen again.
branches.cn: 结果与重跑：同一个数值回来，而步骤让重跑成为可能。

branches.en: THE LIVING KIND: plants and animals reproduce, so the adjective means able to breed.
branches.cn: 活物一类：植物与动物会繁殖，于是形容词也指能繁殖。

branches.en: THE COPY: a plate reprints a map, and a digital file copies a recording without loss.
branches.cn: 复制品：原版重印地图，数字文件无损复制录音。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: a balance repeats its reading on the same block.
branches.cn: 仪器：天平对同一块砝码重复给出读数。

branches.en: THE CODE AND THE LINE: shared files rerun an analysis, and a process repeats across a production line.
branches.cn: 代码与生产线：共享文件重跑分析，流程在整条生产线上重复。

intro.en: Reproducible is an English verb with Latin affixes: re- plus produce plus -ible.
intro.cn: reproducible 是一个带拉丁词缀的英语动词形式：re- 加 produce 再加 -ible。

latinIntro.en: Latin producere and ducere supply the stem, re- supplies the repetition, and -ibilis supplies the ability.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 producere 与 ducere 提供词干，re- 提供重复，-ibilis 提供能力。
